oggetti.descrizione: An incendiary grenade which ignites any targets and terrain within the blast radius. use with caution.
This humane device attaches to its target and dispenses repeated electrical pulses, keeping the target in place for humane apprehension and/or termination.
When thrown, the G-11 Caltrops scatters a wide field of proximity-detonated submunitions that slow and stun foes, making them easier to get in your sights.
A high explosive grenade which damages lightly armored targets. Creates high damage over a small area when detonated.
A thermite grenade designed to adhere to surfaces before burning at 2000°C. Capable of burning through some armor.
Detonates on impact, covering the immediate vicinity in self-igniting white phosphorus.
A repurposed firework that showers its immediate surrounding area in sparks before exploding. As delightful as it is incendiary.
A high explosive grenade which detonates on first impact.
Temporarily stuns all targets within the effective radius.
A 'compliance weapon' to modify enemy behavior. Creates a thick smoke screen to block targets' line of sight.
A throwable device engineered to bounce when hitting the ground, releasing bursts of electricity on each impact. Warning: may bounce unpredictably.
A grenade that releases a cloud of toxic gas, effective at blinding and slowing both organic and inorganic enemies.
Designed to render even the largest foes into considerably smaller, and vastly more compliant, constituent parts. Sacrifices throwing range for a massive detonation on impact.
This grenade delivery drone follows the user until it detects an enemy nearby, then flies towards it and explodes on impact. Has a limited battery life.
An antipersonnel fragmentation grenade. Creates damage over a large area when detonated.
Equipped with a heavy payload suitable against armored vehicles, this grenade delivery drone follows the user until it detects an enemy nearby, then flies towards it and explodes on impact.
A cluster fragmentation grenade. The shrapnel submunition allows it to inflict damage over a large area.
An incendiary device that shatters on impact, without explosive force, instantly creating a localized and persistent combustion field.
A smoke grenade that rapidly deploys a small, dense cloud. Allows for rapid personal concealment and exfiltration.
A powerful, single-use, proximity-detonated heat energy mine. During the Fall of Chara, it is said that enough Melta Mines were detonated to outshine the planet's sun.
A throwable emplacement that generates a spherical, projectile-blocking shield on impact. Has a limited lifetime once deployed.
Delivers silent justice to Freedom's enemies.
Creates a far-reaching incendiary blast ideal for crowd control against smaller enemies of Freedom. Equipped with a programmable timer for strategic versatility.
A throwable anti-personnel mine, capable of adhering to most surfaces. Upon deployment, emits lights and sounds which attract nearby hostiles to its proximity-activated detonator.
Mounts a modified AR-23 Liberator to all resupply pods, allowing them to double as automatic turrets.
Equips Hellpods to deploy smokescreens on impact, obscuring Helldiver deployment.
Allows Helldivers to keep sprinting even when they are out of stamina, draining their health instead.
In addition to restoring health, stims temporarily increase movement speed and damage reduction.
Lowers the time it takes for the extraction shuttle to reach the extraction beacon.
Lines all Hellpods with volatile incendiaries that detonate upon impact, igniting any units in vicinity of the drop site.
Reduce time until new reinforcements are granted once they've been depleted.
Helldivers come out of the Hellpod fully stocked on Ammo, Grenades, and Stims.
Increases the number of available reinforcements.

Equips Helldiver uniforms with form-fitting, automated, rapid-response fire suppression systems. Significantly reduces the time it takes to naturally extinguish flames without conducting ground-aided smothering manuevers.
Increases the time between enemy encounters.
Allows all Helldivers to recover faster after being slowed by an attack, such as acid. Does not mitigate “area effects,” such as EMS strikes.
Allows Helldivers to traverse difficult terrain with ease.
Large enemies now have a chance of dropping Samples on death. Capped at 10 drops per mission.
The Sample scanner gives you a 15% chance to receive twice the Samples on sample pick up.
Increases all Helldivers' stamina capacity and recovery.
Exposes Hellpod wiring upon surface contact, stunning any units in the vicinity of the drop site.

Grants two free uses of the Expendable Anti-Tank (EAT) Stratagem per mission; enough to grant a full squad one single-use rocket launcher each, provided squad members employ the proper equipment distribution protocol.
Increases all Helldivers' effective radar range.
Provides minor damage reduction from all sources for all Helldivers.

An assault rifle sporting caseless ammunition and a top-mounted magazine. An electrical firing mechanism releases the rounds in rapid succession upon firing. Equipped with an underslung shotgun for added versatility.
A reliable assault rifle with an antique iron sight, firing incendiary ammunition.
The SEAF standard assault rifle, balancing power, fire rate, and weight for a reliable weapon against smaller targets.
A compact version of the Liberator designed for increased viability in close quarters. Has an increased fire rate at the cost of higher spread.
A modified Liberator featuring concussive rounds which do less damage but stagger enemies.
A modified Liberator fitted with a scope and firing armor-piercing rounds, to help users take down armored targets.
A large-capacity assault rifle firing humane stun rounds. Reports of lethal incidents have been thoroughly debunked.
A fully automatic assault rifle featuring a non-removable suppressor and subsonic ammunition. Slower rounds allow low-profile operation.
A high-caliber assault rifle with a restrictive magazine size but more stopping power.
A combination assault rifle/grenade launcher. Versatile, but heavy to wield.
This shotgun blasts a wide burst of high-voltage electricity that arcs between all units—enemy or otherwise—within range.
An accurate, armor-penetrating rifle, the BR-14 Adjudicator delivers righteous judgement to medium-sized enemies, though its restrictive magazine limits its effectiveness against large groups.
Fires powerful exploding bolts which do maximum damage upon direct impact. Gravity must be accounted for when aiming.
With its two barrels, one trigger, and vintage feel, this shotgun is perfect for historical reenactments.
A lightweight flamethrower. Shoots pressurized fuel through a dispersion nozzle into an open flame

This pump-action grenade launcher trades precision for devastating area-of-effect capabilities with a powerful pump-action grenade launcher. Its manual single-round reload makes it a highly methodical choice for squads requiring an explosive approach to dispute resolution.
Firing jet-propelled rounds, the Dominator trades fire rate and magazine capacity for increased damage per projectile.

A rapid-fire laser submachine gun prioritizing area saturation over pinpoint precision. Its high fire rate makes it effective for close-quarter crowd pacification, provided the user is comfortable with indiscriminate choice of targets.
This time-honored shotgun-like weapon has been improved since the First Galactic War, and now fires six beams instead of three.
A laser rifle, firing in short bursts. Does not need reloading, but if it overheats a new heat sink must be fitted.
A LAS-16 Sickle model with all overheating protections conveniently removed, allowing for far longer bursts of fire. Does more damage when overheating, at the cost of slightly burning the user.
A laser rifle firing a continuous beam. Does not need reloading, but if it overheats a new heat sink must be fitted.
An SMG that fires caseless ammunition and is equipped with a non-removable suppressor. Produced by Martian Armory.
A top-loaded shotgun prominently featured in the final episode of "Obedient Democracy Support Troopers" / Produced by Martian Armory
Often showcased in the "Obedient Democracy Support Troopers" cartoon, this assault rifle comes with a convenient ammo counter and compass. Produced by Martian Armory.
A submachine gun with an extremely high rate of fire, which can be operated with one hand. Ideal for multitasking.
A plasma rifle, firing a bolt of superheated gas which explodes on impact. Avoid standing in proximity to the blast.
A plasma rifle firing a bolt of superheated gas, which can be charged by holding down the trigger. Charging up a shot fully makes the bolt explode on impact.

oggetti.descrizione: A high-precision burst-fire plasma rifle that must be charged to fire.
A semi-automatic ceremonial rifle equipped with a bayonet. Can be set to fire in three shot bursts, to easily conduct the Fallen Hero's Salute.
This ceremonial rifle is modeled after antique relics from pre-Democratic times. It is traditionally gifted to every citizen upon turning 16 to encourage service.
This bolt-action rifle fires jet-assisted shells that explode shrapnel in all directions upon impact. Not recommended for close-quarters use.
A heavy, large-caliber marksman rifle bridging the gap between precision and sheer stopping power. Fires armor-piercing rounds coated in a high-ignition thermite compound to ignite targets.
A heavy bolt-action sniper rifle. Fires high-damage armor piercing rounds with exceptional long-range precision, ensuring Democracy can be delivered no matter the distance.
A mighty rifle with a signature lever-action enabling single round reload. Powerful precision suited to mid- and long-range combat.
This high-caliber marksman rifle trades magazine capacity and rate of fire for powerful, accurate shots.
A modified Diligence rifle offering increased damage at the cost of some maneuverability. Fires a single bullet at a time.
oggetti.immagine: R-63CS Diligence Counter Sniper Primary Render.png

oggetti.descrizione: A mid-range precision rifle. Equipped with an integrated suppressor and subsonic rounds for barely-detectable operation.
The alloy in these long-range rifles includes metals from the dead planet Chara, overrun in the First Galactic War. / Produced by ST Construction.
A humane compliance weapon with two separate magazines: one for armor-penetrating flechette rounds and one for stun rounds.
A fully-automatic shotgun with a high rate of fire, excellent for controlling crowds. Requires frequent reloading.
A modified breaker shotgun firing incendiary projectiles. Generates heat during use, so limited to burst fire.
A modified breaker shotgun firing birdshot, small pellets which saturate and area to clear up smaller targets.
A pump shotgun that fires a burst of incendiary phosphorus pellets, setting targets ablaze.
A powerful dual magazine pump-action shotgun, with limited armor penetration. Ideal for small and fast targets.
A modified Punisher shotgun firing exploding plasma rounds. Fire carefully - exploding plasma can injure squadmates.
A Modified Punisher shotgun firing heavy, high-damage slugs. Perfect for punching holes in big targets.
A slamfire shotgun: fires continuously while the trigger is depressed, via activation of the pump-action mechanism. Loaded with armor-piercing flechettes and equipped with an extended bayonet.
A submachine gun with a longer barrel, allowing for higher muzzle velocity and increased armor penetration.
A heavy-duty submachine gun that fires large-caliber rounds, with a slower rate of fire to manage the high recoil. Ideal for use at close to medium range.
A high-caliber submachine gun which can be fired with one hand. Has a relatively low rate of fire.
Fires concussive rounds that stagger enemies. Slower rate of fire than other SMGs.
This versatile submachine gun equipped with iron sights and frontline inciniration capabilities.
A submachine gun with a helical feed magazine, which gives the weapon a higher ammo capacity whilst making it more front-heavy. Produced by Stål Arms.
An assault rifle with a high-capacity drum magazine, good for providing sustained fire. Produced by Stål Arms.
A speed-loaded volley gun with three different firing modes and three different RPM options. Warning: recoil varies significantly between firing modes.
A melee weapon tipped with electrified prongs that temporarily stun targets. Can be wielded one-handed.
A one-handed ceremonial sword suitable for use in parades, sabrage, and combat.
A lightweight melee weapon that temporarily stuns enemies. Can be wielded one-handed.
A heavy one-handed blade. Slower to swing than other melee weapons, but deals more damage.
A heavy-hitting, one-handed melee weapon.
A pistol front-loaded with a single, powerful explosive. The weight of the projectile limits the weapon's range.
A pistol that fires grenades. Must be reloaded between shots.
An accurate, hard-hitting laser revolver with bespoke break action for heat sink swaps.
A laser pistol that fires a continuous beam. Does not require ammo but can overheat and need to change batteries.
A pistol with a built-in laser sight, suppressor, and flashlight. Produced by Martian Armory.
Fires a ballistic dart at near-supersonic speeds, allowing the user to stim allies from a distance. Might sting.
The gas-operated, semiautomatic P-113 chambers the 14mm "Rapid Deliberation," the largest centerfire cartridge of any magazine-fed pistol.
A fully-automatic pistol with an extremely high fire rate, allowing for efficient crowd control.
The SEAF standard pistol - offering a high rate of fire, generous capacity, and fast reloading.
A pistol firing guided, jet-propelled ammunition. It's lock-on feature ensures high accuracy, but the weapon must be reloaded after every round fired.
A missile pistol equipped with sticky projectiles that use phosphorus fuel to burn through an enemy's armor—or any other outer layer—before finally exploding.
A dart-firing pistol. Each of its six rounds administers a gaseous chemical agent, harmful to hostiles whether organic or artificial, that also induces a state of delirium in the target.
A high-damage revolver, which can be reloaded with single rounds. A heavy-hitting and reliable sidearm.
A one-handed machine pistol designed for a compact carry. If the enemy closes in on you, carve a path out with the help of the P-44!
Loaded with jet-assisted rounds, this pistol is calibrated for creating and maintaining tactical distance from encroaching hostiles
A compact handgun-style flamethrower, able to project a jet of fire over short distances.
A pistol firing bursts of guided, jet-propelled ammunition. Can be set to non-guided mode at any time, removing the need to lock on to targets.
The utilitarian sidearm that was standard-issue to the Charan Colonial Guard in the early days of the Galactic Federation. / Produced by ST Construction.
A plasma pistol that charges each shot until the trigger is released. Plasma projectiles explode on impact.
A triple-barreled, break-action, sawed-off shotgun. Switch firing modes to fire all three barrels at once.
Fires a short-ranged superheated blast of thermal energy that melts the heaviest armor and thickest chitin into slag. / Produced by ST Construction.

Cybernetically enhanced human soldiers equipped with a heavy shotgun and "techno-martial arts."

Heavily armored Automaton walker unit armed with Heavy Fusion Repeaters and explosive grenade launchers.

Swarming drones that fire plasma projectiles and travel in groups. A variation of the watcher.

An Agile skirmisher unit that attacks in hordes.
Elite unit equipped with a large plasma cannon, capable of direct & mortar fire, usually accompanies hordes of Voteless.

Elite unit equipped with an energy shield and a deadly lance capable of launching an explosive projectile, usually accompanies hordes of Voteless.
Flying drone equipped with arc weaponry and the ability to call for reinforcements.
Former Super Earth citizens twisted beyond recognition into ravenous predators as violent as they are nimble.
Ungainly flesh amalgamations that wield massive metallic clubs and are capable of regenerating tissue damage.

Massive autonomous tripod with an energy shield and a large laser weapon. Can also use arc weaponry in close quarters.
Flying Illuminate unit that deploys strafing runs against Helldivers, dealing massive damage over a large area.

Transport aircraft used for deploying reinforcements for the Illuminate.

Agile Terminids that are able to leap great distances to attack Helldivers.

armature.descrizione: The muted colors and relaxed, high-mobility fit make it a favorite among long-distance snipers and hide-and-seek champions alike.
Part of a long line of experimental armor commonly seen on industrial engineering campuses, in the basements of select science aficionados, and around Super Destroyer Mega Garages.
“We fear not poison, fear not death; spite our foes with every breath.” From the beloved classic Hazard Pay: The Musical.
Named for Helldiver Jack Boote, who shut down 908 illegal broadcasts before retiring with honors.
A domestic version of this armor is available for citizens who wish to perform efficient home renovation projects.
Features a utility belt with pockets that can be filled with any number of things, such as pocket knives, mementos from home, and interesting rocks.
With its rustic charm and huntsmanlike detailing, this armor evokes those heroic expansionists who braved the alien wilds and ushered in our current age of bio-uniformity.
armature.immagine: DS-10 Big Game Hunter Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: The end result of several billion Super Credits and 12 years of research into creating “the Soldier of Tomorrow.”
Contains many small pockets, allowing the user to evenly distribute the weight of ammunition, samples, and cool rocks.
First deployed in the mines of Cyberstan, where it offered protection against explosions in the hydrogen-rich caverns.
At the edge of the Federation, sometimes Democracy has only one representative.
The burnished blood-red plates are forged in righteous fire, like the heroes they were wrought to protect.
Assembled from pieces of recovered Helldiver armor and SEAF gear, for those who won't let a lack of full body protection keep them from the battlefront.
The SteerComfort fit of this armor allows the wearer to feel every curve, bump, and jostle of their Exosuit, as if they were one single being.

Based on the uniform of Jackle 6, a veteran of the Viper Commandos who held off an entire Terminid brood on Nublaria in the First Galactic War with nothing but a machine gun, pocket knife, and Orbital Laser Strikes.
Awarded to those promoted to their point of greatest competency, and beyond.

Armor inspired by the legend of the Sanctioner, a figure known only through a bizarrely unanimous patchwork of stifled whispers. As told, this fearsome, covert arbiter of primeval Justice delivered final, state-approved verdicts in the chaotic years before the Federation's founding.
The official uniform of the League of Patriotic Arm Wrestlers, this armor's lycra base layer is supple and sweat-wicking for maximum flexing comfort.
Armor befitting infiltrators of all caliber. Inspired by mythical Democracy-dispensers, whose meticulously undocumented operations remain an inspiration to all students of stealth.
The patented fabric absorbs visible, infrared, and ultraviolet radiation, to prevent detection by all known species.
This armor is based on the antique uniforms of the ‘Super Earth Legion’, a less patriotic precursor to the Helldivers.
This armor's nostalgic color scheme brings to mind beloved trappings of colonial yesteryear: concrete frontier domiciles, slate-colored civilian jumpsuits, and Space Settlers' Pie.

This light armor features state-of-the-art synthetic adaptive fibers and light-diffusing scrim netting, enabling its wearer to blend seamlessly into any wilderness, and carry out unannounced compliance audits with as much surprise as they deem appropriate.

Tailored from insulated canvas, with a design honoring the ghost-like marksmen of ancient sub-zero campaigns. Featuring adaptive camouflage capabilities, it is engineered for long-duration vigils delivering swift, legally binding verdicts from extreme range.
Originally worn by lunar terraformers, this suit can withstand rapid changes in pressure, heat, and personal velocity.
The suit was once designed to hold a variety of battlefield medical equipment. Now it holds a generous supply of stims.
This suit's plutonium-238 nuclear battery enables environmental scanning long after the user has ceased operation.

Inspired by the legendary armored cavalry of the First Galactic War, this lightweight suit features integrated acoustic dampeners to shield the wearer from the deafening roar of Freedom, and the disruptive screams of dissidence.
Made famous by the “Truth Enforcers: Enforcers of Truth” mystery novels, this armor calls to mind those paragons of patriotism who protect us from treasonous lies.
A quality product, this armor can destroy over 300,000 kilometers of fencing with no decline in operational efficiency.
Compact and flexible, this kevlar armor adds minimal mass, making it a common choice for Helldiver fitness tests.
Made famous by the Ministry of Intelligence's hide-and-seek-and-destroy champion of '52, this armor has been improved by removing excess shoulder protection.
Debuted during the New Mombasa Armor Show, this sleek ensemble is sure to turn heads and blow minds.
The breathing apparatus built into this armor helps both soldiers and colonists thrive, even when assigned to planets with atmospheres rated “suboptimal,” “extreme,” and “character building.”
Pushing the boundaries of bionic engineering, this armor collects and dispenses a number of vital fluids, several of which are soon to be declassified.
Developed by the Ministry of Science while investigating the phenomenon known as The Gloom, this armor is non-permeable and squeak resistant.
This armor, together with its friendly-faced helmet, is instantly recognizable from the beloved children's show “Jen Shriver the Science Diver.”
Gifted to Helldivers whose civilian lives were distinguished by exemplary citizenship, patriotism, and service to the Federation.
A welcome sight in all Democratic neighborhoods, this armor inspires both civil pride and civic obedience.
“The ground is just another obstacle that hasn't yet been cleared.”—SGM Janet Jones, Excavation Corps Founder.
After colonists of Hellmire recovered a lost shipment of this armor, the local pastime of fence-smashing was born.
One of the most durable engineer armors available, each set is quality tested by an impact with a full-grown Charger.
Based on a colonial surgeon's gown, where surgeries were often interrupted by a need to perform defensive duties.
Featuring patented reverse-seam technology, to reduce the likelihood of bodily fluids entering the armor's interior.
The distinctive red, white, and green of the Intergalactic Medical Corps signal to all Helldivers that help is at hand.
With extra capacity for storing throwable munitions, this armor ensure every enemy stronghold can be tactically ventilated, as per forceful de-fortification protocols.
This classic armor set is recognized by every citizen: worn by the heroic Helldivers who battled and forever defeated the Terminids, Cyborgs, and Illuminate in the First Galactic War.
The three stripes on the pauldrons stand for the three principles of Super Earth: Liberty, Democracy, and Prosperity.
armature.immagine: DP-11 Champion of the People Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: Though originally intended solely for ceremonial use, its inspirational energy proved equally useful on the battlefield.
armature.immagine: DP-40 Hero of the Federation Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: A faithful replica of the armor worn at The Battle of Liberty Peak. Honor their legacy, and wear it with pride.
armature.immagine: DP-53 Savior of the Free Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: This armor recalls the legendary heroes who scared a ravenous Hive Lord away from a colony village, using only the village's battery of patriotic fireworks.
This multi-layered protective armor keeps rough sand, spores, and other coarse granules from irritating the skin.
Because this prototype's wires operate at 400,000 volts, it also includes a handy rubber underlayer for insulation.
As the electric arc generates a strong magnetic field, wearers should avoid use while in vicinity of stapled paperwork.
Features a patented non-stick coating, which makes scraping viscera off after a long day of battle less taxing.

Inspired by the trailblazing agents of the Super Earth Terraforming Company. These rugged adventurers surveyed hostile new planets during the post-GW1 Great Expansion era, preparing the untamed frontier for rapid and efficient assimilation.
Completely sheathed in 14-cm silica fiber foam, except for a thin tube to the ear canal to enable hearing the satisfying screeches of Freedom's enemies as they burn.
The heavy rubber tunic and reflective limb guards, originally designed to save citizens from burning buildings, now enable the liberal application of the cleansing fires of Justice.
Modeled after the myriad Statues of Judicious Liberty, who keep a watchful eye on checkout lines, schoolyards, perpetual rehabilitation communities, and public confession theaters.
Modeled after the Statue of Mournful Liberty, who weeps over the existence of tyranny, this armor is worn by those who would give their lives to dry her tears.
This armor celebrates the wearer's close relationship to their Exosuit---as intimate as is possible without succumbing to cyborgry.
“Prowl like a jaguar, strike like a viper.”—Motto of the storied SEAF special operations unit whose real exploits were portrayed in the classic comic book series “Tales of the Viper Commandos.”
This traditional armor has remained unchanged since time immemorial. Now with self-heated padding.
The understated color scheme and precision-molded armor plates make this armor a sensible choice for the Helldiver on the go.

This armor, coated in radar-absorbent polymers and a null-signature heat baffle, reportedly turns its wearer into a sensor ghost—a claim attributed to individuals who, curiously, appear to have never existed.
Due to the enhanced strength caused by this armor, caution is advised when using door handles or embracing colleagues.
Each servo-assisted limb contains 138 miniature motors, to support a natural gait and long-term spinal health.
For optimal performance, the manufacturer recommends avoiding immersing this armor in salt water for prolonged periods.
Some soldiers report picking up strange radio interference when wearing this armor near alien artifacts.

Designed for forward observers coordinating long-range decrees. This medium suit features, integrated adaptive camouflage capabilities and an asymmetrical optic visor, ensuring hostile movements are cataloged meticulously--and discreetly--before being permanently stricken from state records.
"Where lesser soldiers break, Helldivers obey. When Tyranny's horrors swarm, Helldivers obey. When death is certain, and hope and sense have fled, Helldivers obey." -- Last Lord Governor of Chara.
For warriors who are so strong and confident that they don't need any reassurance whatsoever.
Bearers of this armor ride no equine mount, but are nonetheless borne to battle atop the trusty steed of Liberty.
armature.immagine: TR-9 Cavalier of Democracy Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: Molded from high-impact synthetic polymers. This sleek, stark white faceless armor both reduces mass manufacturing costs and ensures the wearer is highly visible on almost every battlefield, bravely drawing enemy fire away from considerably more costly vehicular assets.
Disarmingly scrappy and viciously disarming, this armor is a staple of the Balayage FW/2185 collection "Frontline Moxie".
Users are advised not to scratch at the lacquer, as the Red 20,000 pigment that gives this armor its signature sheen may be correlated with rapid DNA unspooling.
Even among the most depraved of dissidents, the mere sight of this armor is enough to inspire a change of heart.
In field tests, 84% of users said that the armor improved their posture and self-esteem.
This armor is the Super Earth Standard Issue, made from the same titanium alloy as the Destroyer's hull.
The pattern used for this armor is the result of the Winter Camouflage Improvement Effort, which considered 136 entrants before determining the color white would best blend in with snow.
This high-visibility armor allows its bearer to be easily seen through smoke, fog, and spewing viscera.
Promotional armor made by SUMY Corp. as part of a highly successful marketing campaign for frozen yogurt.
armature.immagine: TR-7 Ambassador of the Brand Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: Equipped with the latest computational systems, subsystems, and supersystems, this armor is worth the equivalent of a small Megacity.

Heavily layered to protect against ocular blistering, subdermal liquification, and gastrointestinal shattering, this armor is a testament to the power of iterative improvements based on user feedback.
Each gilded detail is polished to perfection by re-educated dissidents, as part of the Lifelong Post-Infraction Atonement Program.
Heavily insulated from animal bites, enemy fire, and the histrionic diatribes of anarchists.
The set's classic advertising campaign “Have you tried a grenade?” has remained unchanged for over 70 years.
An armor often worn by frontline surgeons, who are skilled at both putting bodies back together and taking them apart.
The CW-22 Kodiak armor was thoroughly pressure-tested by patriotic volunteers, as part of the “Test Subjects for Super-Earth” Citizen Advancement Program.
Offering camouflage in snowy environments, surplus sets of this armor are used by nature photographers and keen hunters alike.
This patriotic armor comes recommended by the Ministry of Expansion, empowering the wearer to re-seize from our enemies any territory that any human has laid claim to, at any point in time.
While early prototypes used shock-absorbing gels, this armor stabilizes aim with the use of internal gyroscopes.
Popularized by actor Chip Messiter, who wore this in the action-rom-com-musical “Lost My Heart to a Man in a Helmet.”
This aim-stabilizing armor found surprising secondary market success among alien birdwatching enthusiasts.
Domestic versions of this armor enable colonial farmers to plant crops and mines side by side, safely.
With genuine gold accents, 74% of colonists voted this armor the set they would most like to be buried in.
Embodies the ethos of Manifest Democracy—that it is our voter-given responsibility to emancipate the savage, un-Liberated galaxy. To rest only when every planet is safe, civilized, and Free.
The signature orange pauldron allows easy battlefield detection of the bearer, alive or dead, on ash-strewn battlefields.

Ruggedized for extended operation beyond the reach of paved logistics. This armor's heavy plating is intended for the "unpaving" of hostile territory, providing a mobile bulkhead for Helldivers who don't know the meaning of "environmental obstacles".

This armor is the required uniform for many Super Earth Citizens operating heavy machinery. Long-time users will be delighted to learn that as of this year's Efficiency in Machine Operation Symposium and Gala, wearing this armor is no longer itself considered operating heavy machinery.
The omission of upper-limb coverings allows for optimized freedom of movement, perspiration, and communication of upper body strength to squadmates.
Commonly replicated in stage adaptations of “Lady Liberty's Tower”, in which young Diver Beatrick dons this armor to slay Oppressio, the Tyrant Rex.
armature.immagine: RE-824 Bearer of the Standard Armor Render.png

armature.descrizione: In mountainous colonies, domestic variants of this armor are used to throw weather monitoring equipment uphill.
The crest on this armor's shoulder shows friendlies that safety is near, and foes that they have reached the end of the road.
This armor uses repurposed metal from verified sources, such as vending machine packaging and Automaton scrap, making it a sustainable choice for the environmentally conscious Helldiver.

The design of the Demo-Trooper armor has been a corporate secret since ST Construction first issued it to the Charan National Guard in the early days of the Galactic Federation. Now, STC has contracted with the Ministry of Defense to issue the storied armor of its fallen homeworld to the Helldivers.
Crafted to deliver Justice to the darkest crevices of the galaxy.

Forged from surplus hull plating, this hulking suit features an integrated servo-bracing system and a towering blast-shield collar as favored by Helldiver barbershop quartets heard throughout the galaxy.
The heavy plate used in this armor is sustainably sourced from the corpses of non-sentient Automaton, then processed by other, similarly non-sentient Automatons.
This armour pays tribute to the immovable heroes of the front line—those who refuse to acknowledge incoming fire, and consider "dodging" to be an abstract concept akin to cowardice.
This armor set first appeared in the music video for the summer anthem ‘Our Love Is like Liberty (Indestructible)’.

Addition
Added with the Killzone crossover.

Upon dying, unless gibbed, the player will ragdoll and health is immediately restored to full. While not under the effects of a stim, vision will turn black and white and audio will be muffled. Revived players suffer a permanent bleed penalty, where their stamina will always be fully depleted and their health constantly drains. Health drains at a rate of approximately 20% per second, and the player can still take damage from enemies as normal. This last stand state ends when the player's health is fully depleted, whether from the health drain or from enemy attacks.
This armor passive grants players the opportunity to perform a final stand after their health reaches zero.
In this last stand, you are intended to do as much damage as possible before you fully die, such as with a
, or an
thrown at your feet.
Using a Stim can prolong the duration of the last stand, however the health drain is permanent and can never be stopped.
Boarding the Pelican in a last stand state will count as a successful extraction, as your Helldiver will still pose victoriously upon returning to the Destroyer instead of standing to the side.
Each stim used by the wearer, whether on themselves or on a teammate, lasts 2.0 seconds longer.

The increased stim duration can allow the patient to endure damage for longer periods of time before the effects expire. Principally, this means that players under the effects of the stim have a bigger window during which they will emerge from the stim's effects with full health.
The stim will also increase the duration of the last stand state, allowing the player to continue dealing damage over a longer period of time.
The armor also provides 50% resistance to electrical attacks from certain types of Illuminates or friendly fire arcs from other Helldivers.

If the wearer is a client in another player's lobby, the last stand will sometimes activate upon taking non-lethal damage. This frequency of this issue depends on the connection between the client and the host.

The G-109 Urchin is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Force of Law Premium Warbond for 65 Medals.
The Urchin can be imagined like a cross between the
and the
grenade. Rather than explode and deal damage, it sticks to enemies and periodically emits a pulse in a small area.
After being thrown, it emits one pulse every 2.9s for a total of 4 pulses.
The small explosion radius on the grenade is compensated by its long stun effect, lasting about 13.7 seconds in total from the first pulse, and a high stagger force capable of staggering even
Helldivers can take advantage of this by exploiting an enemy's weak spots or using offensive Stratagems.
Despite the small explosion radius, it is still possible to stun multiple enemies in tight corners.
As this grenade has 0 demolition force, it cannot destroy structures such as Bug Holes or Automaton Fabricators.
Unlike other grenades, the Urchin's fuse time begins after the grenade is thrown.
This gives Helldivers enough time to aim at the enemy without the risk of detonating the grenade in their hands.
If Helldivers are caught in the range of an Urchin Grenade's blast, their stamina will be immediately depleted. The
can negate this effect for as long as it is active, but actions such as using a terminal or stimming will be interrupted.
Much like the
, the Urchin is one of the few throwables that won't alert enemies if it enters their detection radius.
Enemies affected by this also won't detect the Helldiver who threw it, and will simply return to their original position.
To aid its playstyle, it also makes no noise when pulsing, keeping Helldivers undetected from enemies.

One second after hitting the ground, the Caltrops will explode into a small field of several proximity-triggered stun mines, dealing low damage and stunning nearby enemies that detonate a mine.
Caltrops can be used similarly to other mines, in order to cover an area that a Helldiver cannot.
Due to their low damage, it is better to use Caltrops as a "proximity alarm" in this sense, alerting Helldivers that enemies have breached the area.

Alternatively, Caltrops are effective in tight choke-points or when placed in front of patrol paths, as Helldivers can take advantage of the slowing effect by exploiting an enemy's weak spots or using offensive Stratagems (such as an
In an emergency, Caltrops can be used as an improvised
grenade, as it will stun enemies, giving Helldivers a chance to reposition.
Careful consideration must be taken to ensure Helldivers do not stun themselves when attempting close-range use of Caltrops, as this will almost certainly mean death when surrounded by enemies.

Caltrops have a significantly shorter throwing range than other throwables, only being able to be thrown a few meters away. It is highly recommended to aim upwards when throwing to ensure Helldivers don't get stunned when it lands and arms.
Alternatively, Helldivers may utilize armors with the Desert Stormer or Servo-Assisted passives to increase the throwing range.
Like other mines, Caltrops can be detonated early by shooting them.

s: The G-16 Impact is unlocked on the 5th page of the Helldivers Mobilize Warbond for 20 Medals.

and

The nature of the G-16 Impact can hinder the destruction of Bug Holes, Automaton Fabricators, and Bulk Fabricators, as it cannot fall into them like other grenades; it requires Helldivers to throw the grenade as close to the bottom of the hole or vent as possible.
Grounded Warp Ships are an exception, as its open door is large enough for a Helldiver to easily toss the grenade in.
While the instant damage makes utilizing grenades for killing enemies easier, it does have its drawbacks.
As the grenade lacks a fuse, it is not possible to "cook" the grenade to have it airburst above enemies. However, this allows it to be thrown farther than other grenades with a time fuze.
Mobile enemies such as
or
can potentially block the grenade's throwing arc, potentially killing the Helldiver throwing it.
Helldivers that manage to trip while holding the grenade will likely not survive the ensuing explosion at their feet.
The G-16 is loosely based on the British No. 69 Bakelite grenade, a World War II high-explosive impact grenade.

The Melta Mine is similiar to the
, boasting anti-tank armor penetration, high damage, sizeable AoE, and very short throwing distance.
It has a significantly shorter throwing range than other throwables, only being able to be thrown a few meters away. It is highly recommended to aim upwards when throwing.
Helldivers can utilize the
or
armor passives to increase throwing range.
It does not have a standard fuse - it will remain where it is thrown like Mines. It will detonate when medium or heavy enemies step on the Mine.
While attached to a surface and armed, the mine exudes a visual heatwave effect that can help with keeping track of where mines were thrown.

s. Then it detonates again with a "flamewall" that only deals Fire damage and does not inflict fire DoT.

The "flamewall" part of the damage hits twice in short succession, for a total of 1,200 damage.

Hitting a target with both the explosion and flame does a combined 3,200 damage, allowing for an Automaton Command Bunker to be destroyed with a single mine. This can be reliably achieved by placing the mine next to the structure underneath the bunker turret emplacements.
If a Helldiver can get close enough, a single Mine can be thrown through the shield of
and detonate on one of its legs - killing them instantly.
Helldivers should be careful when throwing Melta Mines in the presence of agile enemies such as
s, as they can detonate mines in the middle of their pounce.
Teammates that utilize vehicle stratagems such as Exosuits should be wary of Melta Mines as they are heavy enough to detonate them.

, potentially drawing entire patrols to their doom.

By shooting at it.
By throwing it next to where enemies will appear. Note that Bug Holes can be destroyed only if the mine is thrown inside the hole.

Concealed Insertion is a booster that causes all Hellpods (manned or unmanned) to deploy a short burst of smoke on impact, obscuring the area around the drop site and concealing Helldivers and equipment.
The Concealed Insertion Booster is unlocked on the third page of the Redacted Regiment Premium Warbond for 40 Medals.

When a player is in smoke, enemies can only see them if they are less than 10m away, the minimum view distance. The smoke from Concealed Insertion applies to all Hellpods. It is useful if reinforcing closeby to enemies, as the player has time to escape before being spotted. The smoke helps to protect the Helldiver while using certain mission stratagems, such as when activating Hellbombs, grabbing resupplies, and saluting the Super Earth Flag. The extraction beacon, being called down immediately after the main objective is completed, is also temporarily obscured by smoke. Nearby enemies are alerted to any stratagem, so concealment when grabbing support weapons is also useful.

Localization Confusion is a Booster in Helldivers 2. When equipped, the time between the call for spawned enemy encounters/reinforcements (in the form of Bug Breaches, or Incoming Dropships) will be increased. This increased time gives Helldivers more breathing room, allowing them to react more to the incoming enemies.
The Localization Confusion Booster is unlocked on the 1st page of the Cutting Edge Premium Warbond for 18 Medals.
**It should be noted that Localization Confusion DOES NOT affect the spawn mechanics or rate of enemy patrol spawning!!**
Localization Confusion DOES NOT delay the time for the reinforcements to arrive once an encounter event occurs nor does it reduce the amount of reinforcements that respond to the call.
An encounter (reinforcement call) is another name for a bot drop, bug breach, or incoming Illuminate ships.

There is an internal timer that starts when an encounter is triggered, ranging anywhere from around 2-5 minutes depending on difficulty. This timer acts as a cooldown period and must be completed before another encounter can be triggered. The length of this timer is fixed and does not change during the length of the mission.
Localization Confusion increases the internal reinforcement/encounter timer's threshold by ~15%

Without Localization Confusion equipped, the threshold for the reinforcement/encounter cooldown timer on
9 as a solo diver is 2 minutes and ~30 seconds.
With Localization Confusion equipped, the threshold for the reinforcement/encounter cooldown timer on
9 as a solo diver is ~2 minutes and 52.5 seconds.

However, the shotgun has a low stagger force, meaning that most enemies will not be slowed or staggered after being hit, which can be problematic in close quarters.
When facing high-health enemies, Helldivers are advised to engage at a distance with 4mm shots to weaken them before engaging in close-quarters with the shotgun.
The spread of shot also allows for forgiving aim against chaff enemies (such as
s,

The Arbitrator has a low ergonomics value (30 compared to the
's 65), meaning that it is slower to move around while aiming.
This can be alleviated by wearing armor with the Peak Physique passive, which adds +30 to all weapons' ergonomics value.
As a Rounds Reload weapon, the underslung shotgun is reloaded one shell at a time. This makes it impossible to waste ammo while reloading.

The Arbitrator benefits from being able to quickly switch between its rifle and shotgun to adapt to different situations. Helldivers are advised to set the keybind to "Quick Weapon Wheel: Left" to easily swap between the weapon's two modes without needing to engage the weapon wheel.
The AR-11 Arbitrator is likely inspired by the H&K G11 rifle, a prototype rifle designed to fire caseless ammunition.
This is supported by using the same numeric designation as well as similar ammunition (4mm caseless in-game vs. varying sizes of 4mm caseless in real life).
However, the AR-11 lacks both the high surplus magazine capacity (due to rounds weighing half that of 5.56x45mm) & iconic "hyperburst", both of which were prominent features of the G11.
Additionally, the AR-11 states a "electrical firing mechanism," whereas the G11 is entirely mechanical.

The front end of the weapon may be more in reference to the M-41A Pulse Rifle from the Alien franchise, featuring a perforated heat-shield and underslung shotgun (albeit portrayed as a grenade launcher in the Alien franchise).

The underslung shotgun included with this weapon is likely based on the KAC Masterkey. The attachment was designed to be used as a breaching device, shooting off door hinges or breaking open locks, hence the name "Masterkey."

s: The Liberator is available to all Helldivers by default.
As the standard assault rifle for Helldiver and SEAF forces, the Liberator is a jack-of-all-trades rifle that is effective against various enemies in various situations.
The Liberator boasts high damage, low recoil, and a generous ammo capacity, making it a very easy-to-use rifle while remaining effective on all fronts.
The standard 2x optic can be adjusted to fight at close to medium range, with options at 25m, 50m and 100m, allowing Helldivers to place rounds precisely on enemy weakspots, such as Devestator heads.

Its fire mode can be adjusted between semi-automatic, fully-automatic, or a progressive three-round burst. At short ranges, full-auto can quickly and easily overwhelm enemies with a storm of bullets, while at longer ranges burst or semi-auto firing can be used to precisely land rounds on distant enemies' weak spots.

An under-barrel flashlight is equipped by default and can be adjusted based on visibility conditions. In Auto mode, the flashlight turns on only when the weapon is aimed during night hours. The flashlight can also be set to be always on or off.

Additionally, a laser pointer is activated when ADS, pointing to where rounds will land. This is also visible to teammates, making it a useful aid for hitting targets while also warning teammates to your line of fire.
As the Liberator fires AP 2 armor penetrating rounds, it will have a harder time engaging armored enemies such as
s and Devastators. These enemies have to be killed by targeting their weaker, less-armored body parts, or by using a different weapon that can penetrate their armor, such as a
The appearance of the Liberator and it's derivatives appear to be loosely inspired by the IWI Tavor.

s: The Liberator Carbine is unlocked on the first page of the Viper Commandos Premium Warbond for 20 Medals.

The key advantage that the Liberator Carbine has over the standard Liberator is its extremely high rate of fire. At 920 RPM, it can put over 40% more fire downrange in the same amount of time. This gives it a damage output comparable to the
, a Support Weapon, provided the Helldiver can manage its high recoil and fast ammo consumption.

The Liberator Carbine shines in mid to close range encounters, quickly dispatching of enemies before they can get into melee range. As such, it excels against the Terminids, but struggles more against the Automatons or Illuminate, who demand better accuracy and/or armor penetration.
As it uses the same rounds as the default Liberator's, it has comparable bullet velocity and damage falloff values, giving it an edge over Shotguns or Submachine Guns at longer ranges.

Though advertised through its woodland camouflage and associated Warbond to perform well in a swamp or jungle setting, the Liberator Carbine performs just as well, if not better, in the concrete jungle. Cities offer much more mid range encounters and are generally more predictable terrain-wise than the aforementioned biomes, giving Helldivers space to reload and fire from a safe distance.
The

Armor Passive pairs well with this weapon, as it not only provides more reserve ammo to burn through when needed, but also further lowers the Carbine's already fast reload speed relative to the Liberator.

The drawback of the weapon's higher rate of fire is that it also creates a proportionally higher amount of recoil, making it harder to maintain aim at targets. This can be mitigated by crouching, laying prone, equipping an armor set that reduces recoil (such as
or
), or by attaching a Vertical Foregrip and a Compensator.
Though it possesses a slightly faster reload than the traditional Liberator, it's important to be wary of when and where to reload the Liberator Carbine.

Its high rate of fire and resultant recoil means running out of ammo faster and a higher likelihood of wasting bullets, even if both weapons carry the same combat load. This makes it easier to be caught with an empty magazine mid-combat. It's important to take advantage of its mid-range capabilities to dispatch of enemies before they can get close enough to deal damage. Be mindful of nearby enemies so that they do not get an opportunity to attack while reloading, and be ready to retreat to a safer position to reload if the situation calls for it.
Be ready to call down a Resupply when needed or to look for Ammo Boxes at Minor Places of Interest.

Because it does not carry more magazines to compensate for its high rate of fire, each magazine becomes even more precious. While tactical reloading is still helpful to avoid running empty in the middle of a subsequent engagement, care should be taken to deplete a magazine as much as possible before discarding it.

The selection of a reliable Secondary Weapon may matter more when using the Liberator Carbine, as it can become the fallback weapon more frequently than with other Primary Weapons. As such, weapons like the
, or
may be preferred over more utility-oriented secondaries like the
or
As a AP 2 penetrating weapon, the Carbine shares all the drawbacks of the regular Liberator in that regard, requiring users to target weak points on enemies with AP 3 armor sections.

s: The Liberator Concussive is unlocked on the 1st page of the Steeled Veterans Premium Warbond for 20 Medals.
The primary advantage of the Liberator Concussive is that its concussive rounds inflict heavy stagger and knockback on enemies that it damages, allowing it to stop foes like
s,
s,
s and
s cold in their tracks.
Because enemies will remain staggered for as long as they are being hit by this weapon, they can be rendered completely helpless for teammates to dispatch.

The stagger does not stack with itself, it only resets with each new round that hits the target. Thus, it is best to pace your shots and try to hit the target at a deliberate interval rather than to unload on it.

Repeated impacts can push targets backward a considerable distance. This can be very useful not only for crowd control, but also for pushing enemies towards hazards such as burning ground, gas clouds and Exploding Barrels.

Another advantage of the Liberator Concussive is that it is equipped by default with a drum magazine, which has an increased capacity compared to the box magazines used by default in the standard Liberator. This allows it to maintain stagger-lock on foes for an extended period of time.

The large ammo drum allows the Liberator Concussive to remain in action for longer periods of time. This can mean locking down an enemy for as long as the drum lasts, and remaining on station to support teammates without having to worry about reloading.
Be mindful of the weapon's limited number of drums, and try to avoid tactical reloads when possible. Expend as much of the drum as possible before reloading.

Unlike the standard Liberator, the Liberator Concussive does not have a burst fire mode, and is only equipped with a red dot sight by default. This means that it quickly loses accuracy at longer ranges, making the weapon more of a medium to close-range fighter.
The primary drawback of the Liberator Concussive compared to the standard Liberator is its low damage output due to its greatly reduced firing rate.

While each individual round does only slightly less damage than those of the standard Liberator, this is further compounded by its low firing rate, meaning that it has trouble killing even individual enemies. As such, the Liberator Concussive is especially poor at dealing with crowds, and serves more as an lockdown weapon that disables lone enemies that it is firing at and prevents them from retaliating.

Its inability to quickly kill targets makes the Liberator Concussive function more like a "support primary," locking targets down in place so that teammates with real firepower can kill them while they are helpless.
One quirk of the Liberator Concussive's rounds is that they inflict almost twice as much
as those fired by the standard Liberator. This can give it an edge when fighting lightly armored but highly durable enemies like
s,
s and
s.

s: The AR-59 Suppressor is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Redacted Regiment Premium Warbond for 50 Medals.
As a suppressed weapon, the Suppressor benefits from having a reduced detection presence compared to other weapons.

Suppressed weapons have an audible range of 13 meters. Instead of immediately being aware of a Helldiver's position, enemies will instead become suspicious of the shots and start to investigate. Enemies can still be alerted after several rapid missed shots.
Helldivers can use that advantage to eliminate their targets, such as
s on objectives, without revealing their position. However, killing any unit in patrol will still alert the rest of the group, and the Helldiver will be engaged.
It is recommended to target smaller Automaton units such as
s,
s, and
s first, as they are capable of calling in reinforcements.
When targeting these units, it is recommended to aim for the head to kill them in a single shot without giving them a chance to call reinforcements.
When compared to other suppressed weapons such as the
and
, the Suppressor has a much quieter firing sound.
This difference does not have a tangible effect on gameplay; all suppressed weapons cause the Helldiver to be detected within 13m and their missed shots don't alert enemies as much.

Visually, the AR-59 Suppressor appears to be partially based on the AAC Honey Badger, which is also an AR-style rifle/PDW featuring a suppressor and a similar gas-operated action. However, the Honey Badger features a removable suppressor, while the AR-59's suppressor cannot be removed.

s: The Tenderizer is unlocked on the 1st page of the Polar Patriots Premium Warbond for 20 Medals.

A key feature of the Tenderizer are its high caliber rounds that inflict the most damage per shot of any Assault Rifle in the game. The Tenderizer is able to kill most small targets in only two or three shots, and makes quick work of larger unarmored targets with rapid fire.
The weapon can be switched to 850 rpm via Weapon Wheel for higher damage output.
In exchange for its greater damage output, the Tenderizer has a smaller magazine than the
series assault rifles, sporting a 35-round magazine.

To avoid depleting the magazine too quickly the rifle can be set to burst or semi-automatic firing mode. Take advantage of the high damage rounds to dispatch foes in as few shots as possible, aiming for unarmored weak points.
More frequent reloads require anticipatory positioning to avoid being caught with an empty magazine amidst a group of enemies.
The reduced combat load of ammo may be ameliorated by equipping armor with the Siege-Ready Armor Passive. The
may also be taken to augment ammo capacity.
The Tenderizer's most direct competitor is the
, which sports AP 3-armor penetrating rounds in exchange for less damage per round, much higher vertical recoil, and a lower fire rate.
While the
's magazine is smaller, it carries 8 mags instead of 7, meaning its combat load is only 5 rounds less than the Tenderizer.
A player using the Tenderizer may find themselves having to re-position to target an enemy's AP 0 or AP 1 body parts, such as circumventing a
's AP 3 plated head, or circling around a
to attack its pilot rather than targeting its AP 3 armor legs.
The Tenderizer released with an unusual green-and-tan colour scheme despite being portrayed with a black body in the reveal trailer, though this was later fixed in Patch 01.000.304.
The weapon's appearance and (hidden) 'Rico' ammo type suggest it might be a reference to the Morita Assault Rifle from Starship Troopers, one of the primary inspirations for the Helldivers franchise.

s: The AR/GL-21 One-Two is unlocked on the 1st page of the Python Commandos Premium Warbond for 35 Medals.
The AR/GL-21 One-Two's underbarrel grenade launcher allows for greater loadout versatility, alleviating the need to bring a dedicated explosive weapon/throwable to destroy certain .
The underbarrel grenade launcher is statistically identical to the

The explosive damage and radius of the grenades allows the grenade launcher to eliminate multiple light enemies with a single shot, or inflict significant damage to large body parts such as the butt of
s.
However, this should be done sparingly, as the grenade launcher's ammo is limited to five spare rounds, which are typically better used for destroying enemy spawners.

Helldivers are advised to not fire the grenade launcher at very close range, as the fuse has a range safety that prevents it from detonating too close from the point of fire. If the grenade hits an enemy at point-blank range, it will simply bounce off and ricochet, exploding far from its intended target, potentially even killing the Helldiver who fired it.

Because of its very slow initial velocity and high drag factor, it can be difficult to land precise shots at long distances with the grenade launcher, especially against Automaton Fabricators, since gravity must be accounted for. Helldivers are advised to regularly practice the use of the grenade launcher to accurately predict its trajectory.
Other weapons such as the
, and
can also be used to practice, as all three share the same physical attributes and trajectories with the AR/GL-21 One-Two's underbarrel grenade launcher.
The One-Two has a low ergonomics value (30 compared to the
65), meaning that it is slower to move around while aiming.
This can be alleviated by wearing armor with the Peak Physique passive, which adds +30 to all weapons' ergonomics value.

With a 40 round magazine and six spare magazines, the One-Two has a poor ammo economy (280 rounds compared to the Liberator's 405). Helldivers are advised to practice good precision and rapid, semi-automatic fire (rather than full-auto), in order to maximize each round.
The One-Two has only five reserve grenades, compared to the GP-31 Grenade Pistol which carries six reserves.

The One-Two benefits from being able to quickly switch between its rifle and grenade launcher to adapt to different situations. Helldivers are advised to set the keybind to "Quick Weapon Wheel: Left" to easily swap between the weapon's two modes without needing to engage the weapon wheel.

The AR/GL-21 One-Two's inclusion is a potential reference to the gun used by Arnold Swarzenegger in the 1987 film Predator, hence its inclusion in the Python Commandos Warbond which draws several other Predator references. That weapon was a modified AR-15/SP1 rigged with an M203 grenade launcher.
The AR/GL-21 One-Two's appearance is loosely based on the FN SCAR family of rifles, including the FN40GL grenade launcher)

The One-Two was the first primary in the game with a permanent underbarrel attachment, preventing the weapon from equipping any weapon customization related to underbarrel attachments. (i.e. foregrips, laser or flashlight attachments).

AR/GL-21 One-Two may not fire after switching ammo types after reloading from empty and switching ammo types mid-reload. The only way to fix this is to pick up a different AR/GL-21 One-Two or respawn.

s: The Blitzer is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Cutting Edge Premium Warbond for 80 Medals.
The Blitzer is a unique primary slot weapon due to having truly infinite ammo. If combined with heat based weapons, the wielder will rarely have to worry about their ammo supply.
Similar to its predecessor, the Blitzer has very short range, and it may only chain once per arc on a restrictive chain angle. The Blitzer, however, is powerful enough to take down enemies like

s in a single shock-burst if all the bolts connect with their heads.
The addition of AP 3 armor penetration allows the Blitzer to sweep away most infantry-class armor alongside reliably stagger enemies like
at a rate that allows them to be stun-locked.
Unlike its predecessor (and the

The Blitzer possesses high stagger and is good for stun-locking aggressive enemies such as
or charging

Care should be taken when facing enemies like Heavy Devastators, as the Blitzer's short range and distinct pump/cycle time leaves little room for error; one wrong move (accidentally hitting the Heavy's shield, for instance) will result in a quick death for the wielder unless they are very lucky.
Like the Arc Thrower, the Blitzer can sometimes prematurely ground itself into obstacles between the desired target and the user, such as corpses or other static objects.

It is inadvisable to use the Blitzer against the Automatons, due to its incapability to target weak points, and short range. It fares slightly better against the Illuminate, but truly shines against the Terminids, especially the Predator Strain.

As can be seen from the damage values of one arc, each salvo with a total damage of 250 is divided into five arcs with damage of 50. Because of this, the total damage per target depends on the number of targets hit by the ARC-12 Blitzer salvo, which affects the time-to-kill.

s: The Exploding Crossbow is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Democratic Detonation Premium Warbond for 80 Medals.

The primary use of the Exploding Crossbow is to inflict significant damage to a single target while also dealing explosive damage in a radius around the impact point. This makes it a flexible weapon that can deal heavy damage to a single target or significant splash damage in an area.

The explosive bolts fired by this weapon have a relatively slow travel speed and are greatly affected by gravity, making it difficult to use against distant targets. Practice is required to get accustomed to its arc.

Because it is a Primary Weapon with a very low rate of fire and a small magazine, equipping the Exploding Crossbow means that the wielder must rely on the Secondary or Support Weapon in the event that a rapid fire option is required. Weapons like the
or
can fill this role.
The exploding bolts fired by the Exploding Crossbow are highly flexible, capable of dealing with many battlefield threats.

The crossbow bolt itself inflicts high damage, and when combined with the subsequent explosion can deal significant damage to targets with light armor. As such, the weapon excels at destroying lone enemies not protected by medium armor or stronger.
The exploding tips give the weapon a damage profile similar to the
grenade even if it does not directly impact a target. As such, it can be aimed into clusters of enemies to inflict powerful splash damage to multiple targets.

Unlike other explosives detonation on impact, the crossbow bolts can "skip / slide" over flat surfaces if they're not making contact at a perpendicular angle. In practice, undershooting a crowd on the same level can leave a bolt sliding past all targets and exploding too far behind them.
The Exploding Crossbow possesses several traits that make it a strong utility weapon.
Although it fires crossbow bolts, it is not a silenced weapon. Enemies within a 30-meter radius will detect the sound and go on alert.
It is also the only primary weapon which isn't a Submachine Gun to have the One Handed trait. This not only allows it to be paired with the
, but also allows the wielder to carry secondary objective objects like the SSSD Hard Drive or the Confidential Data or Mutated Egg from a
Mega Nest.

The exploding tips of the bolts allow them to destroy enemy spawners, making it extremely useful when dispatching Bug Nests or Automaton Outposts. The weapon's semi-auto nature and generous magazine supply are well-suited to this task, as misses at long distance can be easily corrected and even Heavy Bug Nests can be cleared using this weapon alone.
Like other explosive weapons, the Exploding Crossbow can pose significant harm to the wielder if used up-close. It can be helpful to switch to a different weapon if enemies get too close for comfort.

s: It is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Freedom's Flame Premium Warbond for 40 Medals.
The Torcher is a compact version of the
that occupies the Primary Weapon slot; as such, it possesses similar characteristics.
Like the basic Flamethrower, it has a range of 20m, measured in first person view.
While this weapon's fuel canister is smaller than that of the FLAM-40, (100 vs. 150), it reloads faster and carries more spare canisters (6 vs. 5).
Each canister contains enough fuel for 12.4 seconds of sustained fire, and fuel is not consumed by the pilot light ignition.
Before firing, the pilot light must be ignited by holding the fire button for roughly 0.7 seconds. It may be fired instantly at any time while the pilot light is active.
It is a good habit to ignite the pilot light before an engagement to ensure that it can be fired immediately. This will ensure that the weapon is ready to face any oncoming threats.

The pilot light only persists for roughly 10 seconds after the last time it is fired. This gives the weapon a grace period where it can still be immediately fired without having to re-ignite the pilot light.

Like the Flamethrower, the Torcher's primary role is to incinerate targets at close range by dousing them in fire, dealing direct flame damage while also inflicting damage over time with the fire status effect.
With decent direct fire damage, the Torcher is able to kill medium enemy units quickly and excels at dispatching large groups of small enemies like
, and

Beware that even though it has better handling than the Flamethrower, the Torcher is still vulnerable to flanking, as the contact flames still take time to kill targets. Always be ready to retreat to re-orient against incoming threats, as the close combat nature of the weapon always leaves the wielder at risk of being surrounded and overwhelmed.

Because of its short range, the Torcher is generally ineffective against Automatons, due to most bots possessing laser and rocket weaponry that far outrange the Torcher. It is more useful against Terminids and Illuminate, which have numerous melee-ranged enemies that must close to within the Torcher's attack range to fight.
A unique characteristic of the Torcher is that, like the Flamethrower, its particles have AP 4 armor penetration. This allows it to engage medium-sized enemies like
s and
s, and even take on heavy enemies like
s and
s, though it will still take a moderate amount of time due to the weapon's relatively low damage output.

As with other fire-based weapons, this can be aimed at the ground to set it on fire, creating a zone where anything that steps foot inside (friend or foe) will be quickly inflicted with the fire status effect.

Setting the ground on fire can be very effective in creating a defensive buffer zone. If anticipating an enemy approach, ignite a swathe of ground that the enemy must pass through, and then retreat. Enemies will be forced to walk on burning ground and take damage before they even come within range.

Be very careful about which ground is ignited, as it may cut off maneuvering space for teammates. Always keep an eye on the locations of teammates as well as enemies, and avoid igniting areas that may become necessary escape routes.

Because of the way that flame particles spread after leaving the weapon, as well as burning terrain that naturally results from its use, it is very easy for the wielder to set themselves on fire. For this reason, it is highly recommended to utilize the armor passives
, or
as they will greatly reduce the damage suffered from being set on fire.
Known Issues

The Evictor excels at delivering devastating damage with each shot but suffers from a very low fire rate and limited ammo capacity.
The weapon’s action must be manually cycled after each shot, giving it a considerably slow rate of fire.
The explosive grenades of the Evictor are highly versatile, capable of dealing both high single-target and area damage.
Medium/Large enemies will take small damage from the projectile impact and explosion AoE all at once. This combined damage can eliminate most medium-sized enemies in one or two shots.
Groups of small enemies can be quickly killed, as they are easily damaged by the large explosion.
This is especially effective against Terminids, allowing a single shot to wipe out entire patrols of
s,
s, or even

of the Evictor's explosion makes it effective against enemy spawners and certain mission objectives. A single round can destroy a Bug Hole, Automaton Fabricators, and Grounded Warp Ships by hitting their weak spots.

and the

Because of the explosion dealt at the point of impact, Helldivers can easily kill themselves by accident by shooting targets that are too close. This same care should be extended to allies as well.

and

or

s: The Dominator is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Steeled Veterans Premium Warbond for 80 Medals.
The Dominator functions as a sort of Marksman Rifle, utilizing powerful rounds that inflict high damage in exchange for a low fire-rate and very high recoil.

The key feature of the Dominator is its jet-propelled ammunition, which inflicts high damage and extreme stagger, while having 0 bullet drag (meaning it deals full damage no matter the range) and almost no bullet drop.
A single round from the Dominator is capable of killing any small enemy regardless of hit locations, and similarly dispatch medium-sized foes by hitting their weak spots.
Each round inflicts a significant amount of durable damage, so even when fighting enemies with durable body parts like
s, the Dominator is still capable of making short work of them.
The Stagger Force of each round is virtually guaranteed to interrupt the actions of any foe it hits, even the likes of
s,
s and
s.

The Dominator suffers from a low ergonomics stat, which means the weapon is slower to follow the player's crosshair and generally has to be "dragged" around. This can be mitigated by equipping armor with the Peak Physique passive.
The Dominator by default has a red dot sight with no magnification options, hence it functions poorly at long range.
One of the Dominator's greatest weaknesses is its small magazine size, only holding 15 rounds.
For this reason, it is very important to make each round count. Never fire more than a single round at small enemies and try to dispatch medium enemies efficiently by aiming at their weak points.
Having a reliable Secondary Weapon is important account for the Dominator's lack of ammo and long reload. Using a pistol like the
or
to dispatch weaker enemies can save the Dominator's scarce ammunition for handling tougher foes.
The 4x Combat Scope is misaligned with the Dominator's true direction of fire, requiring the user to manually compensate:
Close range (~0m): Align the target with the inner edge of the green ring above the centre dot. This compensates for the upward launch bias and gets you clean headshots or solid center-mass hits.
Mid range (~30m): Align the target with the centre dot.
Long range (>100m): Align the target with the middle of the green arrow below the centre dot.

The Dominator's armory description describing jet propelled ammunition exists in real life via the now discontinued Gyrojet, a unique family of firearms designed to fire specialized mini-rockets called "Microjets." Unlike its real life parallel however, the Dominator appears to have significant recoil.

s: The LAS-12 Sai can be bought from the Ironclad Democracy page on the Superstore for 400 Super Credits.
Compared to the

, the Sai has AP 3 armor penetration, higher standard damage, and slightly higher fire rate. This comes at the cost of significant spread, a shorter effective firing time, and a massively reduced projectile velocity.
Because of its immense spread and incredibly low projectile velocity, the Sai is best used in close quarters, similar to other SMGs like the
The Sai's Triple Lens spread is comparable to that of a shotgun, like the

The Sai's spread can be reduced by 53.57% by using the Focus Lens at the cost of a 25% fire rate reduction (800 to 600). Despite the spread reduction, It remains inaccurate for hitting small weak points outside close range.

Due to the Sai's nature as a heat-based weapon, the Sai has the potential to never run out of ammo. The length of time it can fire before overheating is affected by Intense Heat & Extreme Cold modifiers.
Like the
, the Sai will immediately cools down after every shot.
The Sai will can accumulate heat less quickly when using the Focus Lens due to it lowering the fire rate of the weapon.

Unlike other heat-based weapons, it does not have a faster "full" reload versus its "tactical" reload because the ICE pack is not ejected automatically when burned out. If a Helldiver is committed to a full reload instead of letting it cool down, it doesn't matter much if they reload it early or let it overheat if they want to save time.
The One Handed trait means that the Sai can be used while holding items like the SSSD Hard Drive or while using the
The LAS-12 Sai bears some semblance to the LAS-12 Tanto from Helldivers 1, including its shared designation.

Additionally, it bears a loose resemblance to the Star Wars E-11 Blaster Rifle, a weapon used by Stormtroopers. The E-11 itself, and thus the Sai by extension, is based off of the Sterling submachine gun.
The name "Sai" is based on the armory's tradition of naming laser weapons after bladed tools or weapons, and submachine guns with defense-related names, as Sais are historically a defensive weapon.

s: The LAS-13 Trident is unlocked on the 1st page of the Siege Breakers Premium Warbond for 35 Medals.
The Trident acts as a side-grade to the
, providing very high damage against large groups of Enemies at close range.
The Trident fires 6 beams per shot along a very wide horizontal spread.
Due to its very wide duckbill-style spread, the Trident struggles to hit smaller weakpoints at range, such as
heads.
Like the Breaker, Helldivers are advised to tap-fire the Trident instead of firing in full-auto, in order to preserve the very few heat sinks that it has spare.
Being a shotgun-like weapon, the Trident's main weakness is its spread, making it less effective at range than other Primary Weapons.
However, as the Trident fires beams, it does not suffer the effects of damage falloff or drag, meaning that shots will do full damage up to 200m, where the laser then dissipates.
Additionally, the Trident's horizontal spread is very dramatic and unpredictable. Some beams may hit towards the center of the reticle while others may drag very far to one side.
The Trident is very effective against large groups of lightly armored enemies, such as
s and several types of Terminids.
Like other laser weapons, the Trident has a very low stagger force, meaning that enemies will not be slowed or staggered after being hit, which can be problematic in close quarters.

Due to the Trident's nature as a heat-based weapon, it has the potential to never run out of ammo. The length of time it can fire before overheating is affected by Intense Heat & Extreme Cold modifiers.

Since the Trident's rate of fire is much slower than other laser weapons, it will begin to cool down before the next shot is fired, making its effective firing time (in full auto) roughly 2.75s on standard and Intense Heat weather, and 3.5s on Extreme Cold weather.
Uniquely, the Trident fires individual bursts of beams, rather than energy projectiles like the
, or a continuous laser beam like the
However, unlike other beam-firing laser weapons, the Trident does not set enemies on fire.
As with other beam weapons such as the LAS-5 Scythe, the Trident will sometimes display incorrect hitmarkers, displaying ricochet hitmarkers when there was no such ricochet.
