s: The Sickle is unlocked on the 1st page of the Cutting Edge Premium Warbond for 20 Medals.
The Sickle fires bursts of lasers in a manner similar to Assault Rifles, relying on replaceable Internal Cooling Elements to operate.
The Sickle can be fired continuously for up to 7 seconds before its ICE burns out, and needs to be spun up for roughly 0.5 seconds before it begins firing.

From nearly maximum heat, the weapon requires 12.5 seconds to fully cool down. This is affected by Extreme Cold and Intense Heat, which causes the weapon to cool down 50% faster or 25% slower, respectively.

Like other heat-based weapons, if the ICE burns out, it must be replaced before the weapon can be fired again. The Sickle can carry up to three spare ICE units, giving a tolerable amount of leeway for overheating the weapon.
As it functions effectively like a heat-based Assault Rifle, the Sickle is a dependable weapon that offers potentially infinite ammunition in exchange for fire discipline.

The weapon's fire rate and ICE limit give it a maximum of 87 consecutive shots before it burns out. If the weapon is allowed to cool down between engagements, it is possible to never have to reload it.
Because its effective magazine size is almost twice what the

family carries, the Sickle has a respectable amount of staying power. Even in the worst-case situation where the player must burn out its ICE, it is capable of inflicting more damage using a single "magazine" than most Assault Rifles.
Effective use of the Sickle requires managing its heat buildup. It is crucial to not fire the weapon occasionally in order to prevent its ICE from burning out.

However, there may come situations where it is better to expend the weapon's ICE in order to maximize damage output, and reload the weapon. As it carries three spare ICE units, expending one is not a major detriment.

Like other heat-based weapons, the fully overheated reload process is faster than a partially spent reload becuase the ICE ejects itself hands-free at the moment it overheats. If a Helldiver wishes to save time reloading, they may want to fully burn it out instead of reloading manually when almost burned out.

Choosing proper Secondary and Support Weapons can help to maximize the Sickle's potential. As it will continue to cool down even when using a different weapon, bringing a reliable alternate weapon to bear when the Sickle's ICE is almost fully burnt out can buy it time to cool down.
Compared to its cousin the
, the Sickle boasts roughly twice the damage output, but is less precise due to spread and recoil. It is also incapable of setting targets on fire.
The Sickle's sole Weapon Wheel firing option is the sight's zoom level. Helldivers can choose between 25m, 50m, and 100m zoom levels.

An effective strategy is to use first-person aiming to utilize the 100m scope setting for precision shooting, such as firing at Automaton heads, and switching to third-person aiming when precision is less important. This grants the ability to quickly swap between two different zoom levels, without having to open the Weapon Wheel.

s: The Double-Edge Sickle is unlocked on the 1st page of the Servants of Freedom Premium Warbond for 35 Medals.
The LAS-17 Double-Edge Sickle is a

with all overheating protections conveniently removed, expelling excess heat to the user. This allows it to fire for much longer before reaching maximum heat, and the heatsink does not need to be replaced upon reaching maximum heat.
As the weapon heats up, the laser pulses it fires increase in power, but so does the damage dealt to the user when firing:
0-25% heat: Laser pulses are AP 2 armor penetrating and deal 60 damage. Does not deal damage to the user.
26-50% heat: Laser pulses are AP 3 armor penetrating and deal 55 damage. Deals 10 heat damage per second to the user.
Visually, the weapon starts to emit sparks from the sides as it fires, as well as bursts of fire. This can cause visual noise in first-person mode, but otherwise, visual clarity is unaffected.
51-90% heat: Laser pulses are AP 3 armor penetrating and deal 70 damage. Deals 20 heat damage a second to the user.
Visually, the weapon starts smoking and emitting even more sparks and flames. Visual clarity in first-person mode is moderately affected, but still allows for some use.

91%+ heat: Laser pulses are AP 4 armor penetrating and deal 70 damage. Sets the user on fire and deals 50 heat damage a second (in addition to damage from being set on fire.) Without proper resistances, this stage is incredibly lethal and is very likely to kill the user.

Visually, the weapon fully catches on fire, billowing smoke, and emitting an extreme amount of sparks in every direction. First-person mode is nigh useless at this point, and the sheer number of sparks can even make it difficult to tell if your shots are landing in third-person mode.
The Double-Edge Sickle is not affected by Intense Heat, but cools down 50% faster on planets with Extreme Cold.
This weapon has the potential for massive suppressive damage, but at a steep cost- the self-inflicted damage can eventually kill its user, and can only be mitigated, not completely removed.
Several items can reduce the burden of the burn damage for Helldivers trying to make the most of this weapon;
Wearing an
armor set reduces burn damage to a quarter of its normal value.
and

also decrease burn Damage by 50% and 40% respectively in addition to their other effects. Heavier variants of these armors allow for longer firing periods before taking damage compared to lighter options.
The
booster reduce all ticks of damage by a flat amount.
If combined with Acclimated or Desert Stormer, burn damage is reduced enough that the Double-Edge Sickle is unable to harm the user until passing 51% heat.
If combined with Inflammable, burn damage is reduced enough that the Double-Edge Sickle is unable to harm the user until passing 91% heat.
When passing the safe level of heat, further damage can be mitigated by burst firing the Double-Edge Sickle for under a second. However, doing this will impact the damage per second.
When the weapon passes 91% heat, going prone prevents the user from being set on fire. This can greatly improve its use time at this level of heat.
Using a Stim when the burning is too much to bear can keep the shooter alive as long as they have spare stims. This can be supported by the
passive and/or
booster. The
can provide healing to Double-Edge Sickle users, and benefits from the aforementioned perks.

While it has the longest firing capacity of any LAS weapon (theoretically infinite), it has the longest cooling time of its family. Reloading a new ICE will reset the heat quickly, but also remove the bonus damage that comes with it. Regardless, it can still be prudent to simply reload the weapon after reaching dangerous heat thresholds during extended engagements; expending an ICE is often more economical than continuing to fire at high temperatures and using up valuable stims.
The Double-Edge Sickle cannot actually exceed 100% heat, so the cooldown remains the same regardless of how long it is used at this level.

Only the third round shot from a 91%+ heat Double-Edge Sickle will damage the user. This allows the user to fire AP 4 laser pulses indefinitely, but greatly impacts damage per second. Useful for gravely injured Helldivers that are in desperate encounters.

As the Double-Edge Sickle accumulates heat, sparks, smoke, and flames will fly toward the Helldiver firing it. This increases in intensity as heat rises. At high levels of heat, this obscures the Helldiver's vision when firing in first-person mode, and can even make third-person aiming more difficult.
Resistance Chart

If marked with an X, the combination at the listed heat level will take no damage, and is completely safe. If unmarked, Helldivers will still take damage (albeit sometimes minimally) with the combination at the listed heat level.
Armor class does not affect the amount of damage received.
Remember, below 26% no damage is taken regardless.

for raw damage-per-second.

s: The Purifier is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Polar Patriots Premium Warbond for 80 Medals.
The Purifier fires a plasma projectile that inflicts Ballistic and Explosion damage. If the trigger is held down, the power of the projectile is greatly increased.
Fully charging the Purifier for one second increases the initial velocity and impact damage of the projectile, as well as increasing the explosion's damage, radius, push force, and stagger force.
There are no increases from a partial charge and there is no overcharge.
During the charging process Helldivers are greatly slowed. Releasing the trigger, switching to a different weapon or meleeing will immediately fire the weapon.
Because of the different properties of its charged & uncharged projectiles, the Purifier can be effective in a variety of situations.
Uncharged shot can be fired extremely quickly, allowing multiple small enemies to be dealt with at reduced risk or single large targets at the cost of ammo consumption.

Charged shots inflict a very high amount of damage and stagger force in a respectable radius, at the cost of a slower rate-of-fire and movement speed. This makes it efficient against tight groups of enemies, as well as interrupting enemy attacks and stagger-locking survivors.
The Purifier performs best when engaging enemies at medium range -- roughly 20-40 meters -- for several reasons:
Like other plasma weapons, the Purifier suffers from a drag factor of 150%, causing significant damage falloff at range.
The weapon features a short 1.5x optic at the highest, on top of a low initial projectile velocity it can be significantly more difficult to hit precise shots from afar.
Firing at very close range can be dangerous, as the explosion will inflict a significant amount of self-damage uncharged or prove lethal when charged without explosion resistance.
A non-explosive or melee Secondary Weapon is recommended to compensate for the close range weakness.
With a magazine capacity of 15 and 6 spare, the Purifier can fire 105 shots total when fully supplied.
When combined with the Siege-Ready armor passive, it can become easier to leverage the uncharged shots for damage output on large targets.
Like other plasma weapons, the Purifier does not benefit from tactical reloads. Because of this, every round should be fired before reloading.
Like other plasma weapons, the Purifier's explosions have very low
, and are incapable of destroying fences or enemy spawners.
Contrary to the weapon's armory description, the bolt will explode whether or not the weapon is charged
This is also the case for every plasma weapon in Helldivers 2
[1.001.104] The Purifier's minimum charge time is incorrectly set at 0.01s, instead of the stated 0.1s. This results in a much higher firing rate than expected.
The explosion appears to be larger based on the distance from the impact to the shooter. This is a visual bug and does not represent the actual explosion size.

s: The PLAS-39 Accelerator Rifle is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Righteous Revenants Legendary Warbond for 50 Medals. Previously, it was given as a free log-in reward for the Helldivers x Killzone collaboration as of December 19, 2024.
The PLAS-39 Accelerator Rifle is characterized by its incredible long-range power but low magazine and ammo capacity.
Combined, the three shots of a burst deal immense damage. This is enough to put down any medium-sized target with one burst, provided the user can land their shots.
Note that one burst to the torso is not quite enough to kill an undamaged
if all three shots hit the armored chest. To kill in one burst, at least one round must strike the unarmored head or abdomen. As such, it is advised to aim for the gut against these targets.
In addition to its power against medium-sized enemies, the PLAS-39 shines at rapidly defeating heavier ones such as Hulks or
by targeting their weak points. This is also the case against emplaced enemies such as Bunker Turrets.
The PLAS-39's muzzle velocity is extremely high, exceeding any ballistic-based weapon, and has a nearly non-existent drag factor.
This means that the PLAS-39's projectile damage fall-off is minimal at long range.

The PLAS-39's Achilles' heel is its combination of low magazine capacity and lack of semi-auto fire mode. Only three bolt bursts can be fired before the magazine is emptied. Reloading the PLAS-39 occurs frequently, which is a liability when facing close-range targets.
The
armor passive is a match made in heaven for the PLAS-39. In addition to providing extra ammo, it greatly improves the reload time of the PLAS-39, which means more time can be spent shooting targets.
Although most plasma weapons are effective against crowds, the PLAS-39 fares poorly due to its small area-of-effect and tiny magazine capacity.
The PLAS-39 is based off of the VC39 Accelerator Rifle from Killzone. Like the
, it wasn't featured in Killzone 2, in this case instead being from the PS Vita spinoff Killzone: Mercenary.

The PLAS-39 was previously categorized as a Sniper Rifle in the loadout menu, the first and only loadout weapon to hold such a distinction. The weapon was moved to the Energy category in patch 1.003.000, which withdrew the Sniper Rifle category from view.

s: Distributed to all present and future Helldivers as of October 27, 2024, along with the
, to celebrate Liberty Day.
The Constitution does not have any attachments.
The Constitution is commonly considered a "challenge weapon" by the community due to its lackluster performance and in-game status as a "ceremonial" firearm.
The Constitution has the lowest damage-per-second value out of all primary weapons. This is largely because of its very slow fire rate, at just 60 rounds-per-minute.

In addition to its low damage output, the Constitution's 5 round capacity is among the smallest of the primary weapons. Reloads are frequent and relatively long, depending on how much of the magazine is expended.

However, when the magazine is completely expended, the Helldiver will insert a stripper clip containing 5 bullets, drastically decreasing the length of the reload. In most situations it is probably best to expend the entire magazine, instead of undergoing the potentially lengthy process of partially reloading it.
The Constitution cannot be customized with attachments; this prevents the use of more powerful optic sights than the basic irons included with the weapon.
Despite its shortcomings, the Constitution is not without redeeming qualities.
Its rounds can damage AP 3 armor, allowing it to engage a wide variety of enemies.
The Constitution has a generous ammo reserve, capable of holding 100 extra rounds, 120 if the
armor passive is equipped.
As each round is reloaded individually, no ammo is wasted when reloading.
The attached bayonet penetrates AP 3 armor similar to the rifle, and it gives the Constitution greater melee damage than weapons without a bayonet. Using the
or
armor passives increase melee damage even further.
Attacking with the bayonet is also completely silent, which can prevent nearby enemies from being alerted to one's position.
The Constitution demands great skill and accuracy to be used effectively, and even then it still underperforms compared to most weapons due to its inferior stats in nearly every category.
It fares poorly against the Terminids and Illuminate. These factions attack in hordes that are far too large for the Constitution to handle, even considering its bayonet.

On the contrary, the Constitution's precision, armor-piercing rounds, and damage can make it a viable weapon for the Automatons; many of their infantry units can be eliminated with a well-placed shot while also spawning in smaller numbers than the former two factions.
These traits, however, are also possessed by the
, which shares armor penetration values, deals slightly more damage, has triple the magazine size, a faster reload, and access to scopes. The
only sacrifices 10 rounds in overall capacity, the shell-loading feature, and the bayonet which would typically see much less use against Automatons.
When using the Constitution on high-difficulty missions, Helldivers are advised to use it more like a secondary weapon option in conjunction with AP 2 armor penetrating, fast firing weapons like the
or
, using the automatic weapons to deal with crowds and using the Constitution for long-distance targets, melee kills, and AP 3 armored enemies.
The Constitution closely resembles World War I rifles, specifically the M1903 Springfield and the M1917 Enfield.
The Constitution has a tactical reload animation that is more easily seen in first-person, where the Helldiver holds down the rounds in the internal magazine to prevent them from ejecting.

Tapping backwards during the bayonet stab animation will cause the Helldiver to freeze their stab animation; this does not negatively affect any control over the Helldiver. Turning or moving will fix this.

s: The R-36 Eruptor is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Democratic Detonation Premium Warbond for 60 Medals.
The Eruptor excels at delivering devastating damage with each shot but suffers from a very low fire rate and limited ammo capacity.
The weapon’s bolt must be manually cycled after each shot, making it the slowest-firing primary weapon in the game.
With a five round magazine and six spare magazines, the Eruptor has a total ammo capacity of only 35 rounds.
This can be alleviated by equipping armor with the
passive, increasing spare magazines and reload speed.

Tactical reloads are most effective when only one round is left in the weapon, as this ensures that no ammo is wasted, as well as increasing reload speed. Due to the Eruptor's limited ammo capacity, every shot is very valuable, and leaving excess rounds in the discarded magazine is wasteful.
Having a base value of 25, the Eruptor has the lowest ergonomics value of all primary weapons (tied with the
), meaning that it is slower to move the weapon around while aiming.
This can be alleviated by wearing armor with the
passive, which adds +30 ergonomics value to all weapons.
Additionally, equipping the Eruptor with Iron Sights and an Angled Foregrip can alleviate its poor ergonomics by increasing its practical ergonomics value from 21 to 35.
The jet-assisted rounds of Eruptor are highly versatile, capable of dealing both high single-target and area damage, while having no damage falloff.
Medium/Large enemies will take damage from the projectile impact, explosion, and shrapnel all at once. This combined damage can eliminate most medium-sized enemies in one or two shots.
Shrapnel makes the Eruptor especially useful against certain unarmored Illuminate targets, such as
s,
s and the energy shields used by
s.
Groups of small enemies can be quickly killed, as they are damaged by both the explosion and shrapnel.
This is especially effective against Terminids, allowing a single shot to wipe out entire patrols of
s,
s, or even
s (via chain reaction).
The

of the Eruptor's explosion makes it effective against enemy spawners and certain mission objectives. A single round can destroy a Bug Hole, Automaton Fabricators, and Grounded Warp Ships by hitting their weak spots.
Certain optional objectives such as Illegal Broadcast Towers. Spore Spewers, and Shrieker Nests can be destroyed in very few shots.

The Eruptor performs best at long ranges by utilizing its jet rounds and standard 10x Sniper Scope. Helldivers are advised to engage targets at a distance, as the poor ergonomics, fire rate, and danger of shrapnel make the Eruptor a hazard in close-quarters.
The Eruptor's rounds have a one-second lifetime with a maximum range of 185 meters, after which rounds will automatically explode.

Because of the explosion and shrapnel dealt at the point of impact, Helldivers can easily kill themselves on accident by shooting targets that are too close. This same care should be extended to allies as well.
A reliable Secondary or rapid-fire Support Weapon is recommended to deal with enemies at close range. Pistols like the
and
can quickly dispatch individual targets, while Support Weapons like the
or
are effective options for several close-range enemies.
Drone backpacks like the
or
can also be useful, killing most small enemies before they can get too close.
The Eruptor appears to be based on the prototype Barrett XM109 OSW (Objective Sniper Weapon), also known as the AMPR (Anti-Materiel Payload Rifle).
This was a Barrett M82 converted to fire 25x59mm grenades out to a range of 2,000 meters.
The description for the YouTube video documenting the changes that occur in Patch 01.003.000 erroneously lists the Eruptor as the "R-32 Eruptor" as opposed to correct designation of R-36 Eruptor.

s: The SG-20 Halt is unlocked on the 1st page of the Truth Enforcers Premium Warbond for 20 Medals.
The SG-20 Halts magazine tubes are independent from each other. Swapping the tubes by using the Weapon Wheel can help avoid a reload in dire situations.
Due to this, Helldivers are advised to ensure both tubes are loaded before engaging in combat.
Shells share the same reserve ammo pool. Helldivers should prioritize what shells they immediately need if they're low on ammo.
Stun rounds can be used to effectively stall enemies when you need to reload your flechette tube.
Using stun rounds on decapitated charging
is a good tactic to completely halt their berserk charge, providing time to switch to a Support Weapon to finish them off or to retreat.
Using stun rounds on any form of
will give you plenty of time to switch to the
, or even
and line up a shot at their head, killing them instantly. At close range, the Halt's own flechette shells can achieve the same effect if enough flechettes hit the head directly.
The Halt has significant spread which is slightly better than the
. Therefore, it is ill-advised to engage enemies at medium range as most of your pellets will not hit your target.

The Halt benefits greatly from being able to swiftly switch between its flechette and stun firing modes. For PC players, it is advisable to set an accessible keybind to "Quick Weapon Wheel: Left" to easily swap between the weapon's two modes without needing to engage the weapon wheel every time a different mode is needed.
Both the
and SG-20 Halt are the only shotguns to feature rifled barrels for better projectile velocity and accuracy. However, the Halt does not fire any slug rounds, making its rifling redundant.

In real life, rifling is actually detrimental to shotguns that are not firing slugs - as rifling is known to cause a pattern akin to a donut. While the in-game shotgun does not have such a pattern, its lower overall accuracy could be due to the fact it has a rifled barrel.
The appearance of the SG-20, like all Punisher variants, is loosely based on the UTS-15.

s: The Cookout is unlocked on the 1st page of the Freedom's Flame Premium Warbond for 20 Medals.
A
variant, the Cookout is a pump action shotgun that ignites targets that it hits and individually reloads into two eight-round tubes.
With a 16-round internal magazine and the Rounds Reload trait, the Cookout is very ammo-efficient and will never discard any ammunition while reloading.
Unlike the Punisher, the Cookout fires a large number of low-damage pellets, which gives it wider coverage.
The general role of the Cookout is to ignite small enemies from range, letting the afterburn inflict damage over time.
Due to its ability to set targets on fire, it is particularly effective against small enemies like
s,
s and
, which have small amounts of health that can be completely dispatched by the burning alone.
Compared to the standard Punisher, the Cookout inflicts less damage per round, giving it less raw damage output against single targets with larger amounts of health.
The Cookout can be compared to the

, another shotgun that sets its targets on fire with incendiary ammunition. However, unlike the Breaker Incendiary, the Cookout's buckshot can stagger most targets that it hits, giving it a measure of stopping power when faced with tough enemies.
The ideal use of the Cookout is shooting at groups of small enemies from range, allowing the burning to deal damage to them over time and kill them before they can get close enough to attack.

Beware that burning damage is inflicted to the main body of the target, and thus does not weaken any particular body parts regardless of where the pellets hit. This makes the weapon fare poorly at trying to kill targets by destroying their weak points.

Generally, try to shower multiple targets with pellets when possible, then retreat and allow the burning damage to hurt them without having to engage them. Effective use of the this tactic involves keeping targets on fire with as few shots as possible, only engaging them to set them on fire if they've been put out.

When reloading with exactly 8 rounds in the magazine, the final round count will increase by one round, making it 17 rounds. Moreover, every subsequent reload performed with 8 or more rounds remaining will result in a final count of 17 rounds, until the number of rounds in the magazine drops below 8.
The SG-451 Cookout's designation is likely a reference to Fahrenheit 451.
Compared to other shotguns based off of the
, the Cookout has a very prominent muzzle flash, evidence of which can be seen in the rainbow oxidation ring on its muzzle brake.
The appearance of the SG-451, like all punisher variants, is loosely based on the UTS-15.

s: The SG-97 Sweeper can be bought from the Entrenched Division page on the Superstore for 400 SC.
The Sweeper boasts increased damage, pellet count, 46% tighter spread, and a bayonet compared to the
. In exchange, it can not fire stun pellets and has a slightly smaller magazine for flechettes.
Compared to other pump-action shotguns, the Sweeper has much lower stagger force, meaning that enemies will not be as slowed or staggered after being hit, which can be problematic in close quarters.

Uniquely, the Sweeper can "slamfire," meaning that Helldivers can hold down the trigger to automatically operate the pump and fire the weapon at the same time, almost doubling its effective rate of fire compared to the SG-20 Halt.
This is functionally no different from regular full-auto fire.

As a Rounds Reload weapon, the Sweeper is reloaded one shell at a time. This prevents wasted ammo upon reload. As a trade-off, a complete reload from empty will be slower than that of a traditional magazine. Helldivers are advised to reload frequently and ensure the magazine is always full.
Helldivers can continuously fire by pressing Reload after each shot. This is made even easier to execute with the
armor passive.
The Sweeper comes equipped with a bayonet, which can provide useful damage and stagger at point-blank range, as well as providing an attack option while out of ammo.
The appearance of the Sweeper seems to be loosely based on the Winchester Model 1897, a shotgun famous for its use in World War 1 by United States forces.
Specifically, the Sweeper is based on the "Trench Gun" variant of the 1897, fitted with a shortened barrel, heat shield, and bayonet.
The Sweeper also shares its real-life counterpart’s ability to “slamfire”, where the trigger is held down, and the pump is operated continuously to rapidly fire off shells.
Additionally, the Sweeper shares the designation of "SG-97" and reports claim that U.S. troops referred to the 1897 as the "trench-sweeper."
As with many weapons in the game with modeled ammunition reserves on the gun, the 4 shells attached to the gun disappear when loading the last 4 shells carried by the Helldiver.
When selected in the Weaponry tab, the Sweeper will play an animation of a shell being loaded into it before it gets cocked.

s: The StA-11 SMG is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Righteous Revenants Legendary Warbond for 65 Medals. Previously, it was given away for free for all players who logged in during the second phase of the Helldivers x Killzone crossover event.
This weapon doesn't support attachments.
The StA-11 is an extremely rapid-fire SMG, most comparable to the

; it has less recoil, a lower fire rate, slightly lower capacity, and higher damage rounds. Like most weapons in its class it trades accuracy and lethality at range for close-range combat potential, whilst the position of its large helical magazine precludes the installation of underbarrel attachments like flashlights. Its lower recoil and fire rate means it's much more stable than the Knight and doesn't climb quite as aggressively.
As a crossover weapon, the StA-11 SMG cannot be customized in any way using the attachments system.

When the reload process is interrupted, resuming the reload will immediately consume a magazine, even if the reload has not been completed. This can occur each time the reload process is interrupted, which can result in multiple magazines being lost without the weapon being readied to fire.
The StA-11 is based on the StA-11 Submachine Gun from Killzone 2.

The StA-11 appears to be a mashup of the the PP-19 "Bizon" and IMI Uzi SMGs, having a Bizon-style skeletal stock and the distinctive helical magazine, with the more rectangular chassis, longer barrel, and top-mounted charging handle of the Uzi. Its capacity is much lower than the PP-19 at just 48 rounds compared to the PP-19's 53 to 64 round magazines (depending on exact caliber).

s: VG-70 Variable is unlocked on the 1st page of the Control Group Premium Warbond for 35 Medals.
The VG-70 Variable, as its name suggests, is a weapon system with variable firing modes and rpm options.
Auto: Fully-automatic with three available rpm options; 300, 550 & 750.
Volley: Fires one round from each barrel simultaneously, totaling 7 rounds on target with one trigger pull.
This firing mode is semi-automatic, but is affected by the selected rpm. Produces significant recoil.
Total: Fires all remaining ammunition in the magazine.
Using this mode will deal 15 damage to the Helldiver's right arm and ragdoll them if not prone and when firing more than 22 rounds at once.

This mode has the added usecase of acting as a mini jump pack if the Helldiver dives while firing towards the floor. This is most useful for getting up some small ledges or over city walls when already on an elevated position (such as a garbage bin).
The Variable, as implied, comes with 3 fire modes.
Auto: Fully-automatic, like a standard assault rifle, with 85 normal damage per shot.
Recommended for infantry or fodder.
Volley: Fires one round from each barrel simultaneously. 595 damage (85 x 7). It deals 161 damage to 100% durable enemy parts.
Recommended for tough medium enemies (eg.
heads,
mouths,
stomachs or
stomachs).
This firing mode suffers from high recoil. This can be mitigated by aiming down sights, crouching, going prone, and using armors that reduce recoil, such as
and

Total: Fires all remaining loaded ammunition from all barrels. Maxes out at 4,165 damage (85*49) when fully loaded. On 100% durable enemy parts the maximum durable damage of TOTAL mode is 1,127 damage.
Recommended for the weak spots of heavy enemies, like Hulk vents,
butts,
heads,
heads or
eye sockets.
Firing while leaning out of the FRV's doors will not ragdoll Helldivers, but will still deal damage.

Diving backwards and firing or using a jump pack and firing backwards midair in this mode enables players to "jump" much greater distances thanks to the recoil, useful when a quick escape or a large gap must be crossed. With skill, jumps can be made in excess of 50 meters, though significant damage may be incurred.

The Variable's projectiles have much higher drag than other assault rifles, resulting in a noticeable decrease in damage per bullet over longer ranges. This is slightly compensated by the Variable's firing modes that fire more bullets at a time.
The Variable suffers from very low ergonomics. Armor passives like
and
can help mitigate this.
The Variable's seven-barrelled configuration resembles the 18th century Nock gun, a flintlock muzzleloader.

The Variable's functionality appears inspired by the "Bertha" prototype volley gun developed by Metal Storm, which electronically fires projectiles superposed inside each of its barrels. Like the Variable, Bertha could adjust its rate of fire, even to the point where it could fire all of its ammunition in a fraction of a second.

Operating similarly to the
, the Ultimatum fires a single powerful anti-tank explosive round and has to be reloaded after every shot.

Ammo Boxes disproportionately benefit the Ultimatum, granting full reserve ammunition.

The GP-20 Ultimatum is likely inspired by the German Kampfpistole, a World War II flare pistol of the Wehrmacht that was later modified to fulfill the role of a short-ranged grenade launcher by firing a specially designed rifle grenade known as a Sprengpatrone in a low-arc similar to the in-game Ultimatum, but with much less explosive and penetrative power.

The Grenade Pistol is a very useful utility secondary weapon, as it can inflict explosive damage.
In particular, when used properly it is capable of destroying Terminid Nests and Automaton Fabricators, allowing the wielder to equip a different type of grenade such as
while retaining the ability to destroy enemy spawners.

The explosive and splash nature of the grenades allows the Grenade Pistol to dispatch multiple enemies with a single shot, or inflict significant Structural damage to large body parts such as the thorax of
s.
Because of its significant falling arc, it can be very difficult to land precise shots at long distances since gravity must be accounted for. Be sure to practice in order to get used to the arc.
Be wary when using this weapon, as it is very easy to exhaust its ammo supply. When picking up supplies from a Resupply or

four grenades will be replenished, and when picking up an Ammo Box two grenades will be replenished; Grenade Cases do not replenish the Grenade Pistol. Be sure to balance grenade consumption with that of the primary and support weapons.

Be careful when firing the Grenade Pistol at very close range, as the fuse has a range safety that prevents it from detonating too close to the wielder. If the grenade hits an enemy at point-blank range, it will simply bounce off and ricochet, exploding far from its intended target.
The One Handed trait means that the Grenade Pistol can be used while holding items like the SSSD Hard Drive or while wielding the
, and it will be automatically equipped in these cases if no other weapons with One Handed are equipped.

The Grenade Pistol makes no noise when fired, allowing it to destroy Terminid Nests and Automaton Fabricators without alerting nearby enemies. The explosion can also be used to distract enemy patrols.
The GP-31 Grenade Pistol was suggested by an R&D intern who was executed for making an unauthorized suggestion to a superior and posthumously promoted to Sergeant.

s: The Dagger is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Cutting Edge Premium Warbond for 60 Medals.
The weapon comes with 3 reserve heatsinks, but with good heat management, Helldivers should never run out of ammo.

This heat sink is less effective on hot planets and more effective on cold planets. It takes approximately 11 seconds to cool completely from 99% heat on hot planets, and approximately 6 seconds on cold planets.
Heat sinks dissipate heat even when the weapon is holstered. It will only cease to do this if the heat sink is completely overheated and must be replaced.

If a Helldiver is in a situation where they have to reload, they should note that fully overheating the ICE of any heat-based weapon and letting it eject itself from the weapon first takes less time than a partial "tactical" reload. It's best to fully burn out the ICE if already committing to reloading.
As with other
, the Dagger trades instantaneous damage for its ability to sustain damage output for long periods.
Prolonged exposure to the beam can set targets
, further boosting the damage-over-time effect. As this ignition doesn't take very long, this works well on crowds if the beam is only used on each enemy long enough to ignite them.
The laser will still not light enemies on fire instantly, as both the weapon has a 0.25 second warm-up period before it starts firing, and some enemies take more than one "tick" of damage to ignite.
This tradeoff makes it unsuitable for stopping
or
that are about to fire a flare to call reinforcements.
The One Handed trait means it can be used while holding items like the SSSD Hard Drive or the

Being a One Handed beam weapon makes the Dagger very forgiving to fire while running. It can serve as a side-grade from the "Guard Dog" Rover in this capacity, exchanging steady, autonomous targeting for an unoccupied backpack slot.
The Dagger is an excellent utility weapon to quickly remove Environmental Hazards from a considerable distance. Any contact with the beam will detonate Automaton (or
) mines and destroy various hazardous flora, allowing the user to sweep their crosshair across a problem area and avoid an embarrassing accident later.
Prior to patch 1.003.104, beam weapons such as this were capable of detonating the backpacks of Automaton
and
with the same ease that they can destroy Environmental Hazards.
This change coincided with the introduction of heavier Jet Brigade units, and was presumably made to avoid trivializing the lighter Jet Brigade enemies.

As a suppressed weapon, the M6C/SOCOM benefits from having a reduced detection presence compared to other weapons.

Suppressed weapons have an audible range of 12 meters. Instead of immediately being aware of a Helldiver's position, enemies will instead become suspicious of the shots and start to investigate. Enemies still can be alerted after several rapid missed shots.
Helldivers can use that advantage to eliminate their targets such as

When targeting these units, it is recommended to aim for the head to kill them in a single shot without giving them a chance to call reinforcements.
The M6C falls between the

The serial number printed on the sides of the suppressor is the release date of Halo 3: ODST (September 22, 2009) followed by the date in the Halo timeline on which The Covenant discovered humanity's home solar system (October 10, 2552). The events of the game take place 10 days later.

The aiming laser/flashlight has Korean script on it. In Halo 3: ODST, this translated to "7," a number that is a running meme among Halo's developers. The text in the Helldivers rendition translates to the word "freedom".

'Martian Armory' is a play on the Mars-based manufacturer of this weapon in the Halo universe: Misriah Armory. Given the condition of Mars at the time of this weapon's release, it is unclear whether these two fictional companies share a location in their respective fictions.

s: The Stim Pistol is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Chemical Agents Premium Warbond for 80 Medals.

The Stim Pistol is a revolver with a cylinder holding 6 Stim darts. Upon hitting a teammate, it gradually restores roughly 90% of their HP over approximately four seconds. The darts' effects otherwise function identically to Stims, healing injured body parts, restoring stamina, and benefiting from the
booster and both the
and the
if the weapon wielder is wearing the appropriate armor.

Unlike regular stims, the Stim Pistol's ammo heals Helldivers for around 90% of their HP per stim and heals them over a period of ~4 seconds rather than instantly. The stim duration can be boosted with the
or the
to provide a full heal, but its healing rate will not be boosted.
Therefore, if a Helldiver is expecting to take near-lethal damage multiple times quickly, the stim pistol will not provide the same protection as a regular stim.

This can change if the patient is stimmed twice in rapid succession - the healing speed will match the speed of a regular stim. It is somewhat impractical and difficult to pull off consistently over longer ranges.
To compensate for this, the Stim Pistol comes equipped with 30 (24+6) stims based compared to the 4 regular stims in a Helldiver's loadout, although without

Another armor passive that pairs well with the Stim Pistol is
for the ability to quickly draw in an emergency and spend less downtime reloading.
The Stim Pistol only heals Helldivers and SEAF units, despite the appearance of hitmarkers, with the exception of being able to detonate Automaton mines.
The Stim darts have somewhat low projectile speed, making it difficult to hit moving teammates at range. Voice communication is advised for maximum stim efficiency.
Good opportunities to heal teammates are right after they land from a dive or ragdoll, reloading a support weapon, operating a terminal, or manning an emplacement.
The
booster applies to the Stim Pistol's ammunition, granting team members valuable buffs in combat situations.
users benefit greatly from a teammate with the Stim Pistol as it permits them to outheal the damage received from continuous fire. It grants unrestricted use of the
and unlocks its full potential without fear of burning to death.

or

Bringing one in Commando Missions can be really helpful, since it grants a reliable source of healing for the entire team during the whole mission despite limited access to Resupply or Stim Crates.

s: The Verdict is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Polar Patriots Premium Warbond for 60 Medals.
A high-caliber pistol, the Verdict can be considered a more powerful version of the

While it has fewer rounds per magazine, each round from the Verdict deals almost 50% more damage, meaning that both weapons inflict nearly the same amount of damage per magazine. While the Verdict can make quick work of lightly armored targets, precise shooting allows the Peacemaker to win out in total damage against unarmored parts.

The Verdict carries as many spare magazines as the Peacemaker, for a combat load of 90 rounds compared to the Peacemaker's 135 rounds. With its fewer rounds per magazine, the Verdict will find itself having to reload more often, creating more situations where the wielder may be vulnerable.
Because of its high damage per round, the Verdict benefits greatly from targeting the weak points of enemies, for instance killing

s with three shots to the abdomen or one precise headshot. In order to counteract its comparatively small magazine, hitting the weak spots of enemies can allow the Verdict to dispatch medium infantry or finish off weakened heavies with only a handful of shots.

Because of its heavy cartridge, the Verdict is capable of penetrating AV 3 armor for reduced damage. This makes it more effective at handling targets with medium armor than most other sidearms, such as
s and
s, where their rounds would simply just ricochet off.

As it carries a large number of reserve magazines, it can be beneficial to always reload the Verdict to a full magazine between engagements, so that in the event that it is needed it will always have all rounds at the ready.
As a Secondary Weapon, the Verdict can be wielded when the left hand is holding mission-critical equipment, or when equipped with the
The Verdict's appearance seems to be loosely based on the Desert Eagle, with its "Rapid Deliberation" cartridge being a play on the Desert Eagle's Action Express cartridge.
The Verdict’s armory description claims that the weapon fires 14mm, however the projectile in-game is 12mm, similar to other pistol caliber ammunition in the game.
This projectile is likely the exact same projectile as the

. This is evident by the fact that both weapons' projectiles share the exact same properties, such as stagger force and muzzle velocity. As well as the fact that balance changes to one weapon's attack always happen to the other.

s: The Redeemer is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Helldivers Mobilize Warbond for 5 Medals.

The Redeemer's high burst damage output makes it an ideal emergency backup weapon. It pairs well with Primary or Support weapons that cannot fend off multiple or close-ranged enemies, such as Marksman Rifles and backpack-based Support Weapons.
It shares this niche with the
. The Redeemer is far more adaptable to different situations and ranges, but the Bushwhacker can output more damage under ideal circumstances.

The Redeemer can empty its magazine in less than two seconds. Firing short, controlled bursts is almost mandatory to avoid spending excessive ammunition on an enemy when it has already died, and also to tame the Redeemer's frantic recoil.

The Gunslinger passive armor effect drastically mitigates full-automatic recoil. It also improves the reloading speed, which, while convenient in emergencies, can lull the user into spending all their reserve ammunition in the heat of the moment.
Setting the Redeemer to its semi-automatic fire mode mitigates both of these shortcomings, and is generally sufficient for thinning out groups of AP 2 armored enemies with low HP (e.g.
, who die in one shot).
The One-Handed trait means that the Redeemer can be used while holding items like the SSSD Hard Drive or while using the
, and it will be automatically equipped in these cases if no other weapons with One-Handed are available.
The P-19 Redeemer has an attached flashlight, which can be set to Auto (turning on while aiming at night), always-on, or always-off. It does not have a laser pointer.
The Redeemer seems to be loosely inspired by the Ingram M11 both in appearance and function.

s: The P-33 Missile Pistol is unlocked on Page #2 of the Exo Experts Premium Warbond for 50 Medals.
When firing, the the Missile has an extremely slow initial velocity of 1m/s which gradually acceleratess to about 50-70m/s.
The Missile Pistol has two firing modes: Guided and Non-Guided.
Guided Mode disables the gun from firing unless it has locked onto a valid target. A 'valid target' is any Medium, Large, or Massive enemy.
Maximum lock-on distance is 100 m.
The lock-on time is the same as the
, which is one second.
A fired missile will steer towards the targeted enemy. If it cannot reach its target, it will self-detonate.
Once a lock is set, it will not acquire a different target unless the user stops aiming, breaks line-of-sight with the target, or the target is killed.

As with all weaponry with lock-on capability, guided shots always target center mass rather than weak points. This makes it very unlikely to hit an enemy's most vulnerable area. Some Terminids are an exception to this, due to their large heads and quadrupedal posture.
Non-Guided Mode allows the user to fire the pistol freely, like any other firearm. While in ADS, the small indicator on the left side of the weapon will display the current firing mode.
Maximum range is ~197 m
The Missile Pistol can toggle guidance modes, allowing for easy shots on fast moving targets or precise shots on enemy weakpoints.
Aiming at the weak points of moving targets in Non-Guided mode can be tricky due to the low initial velocity of the missile.
However, the missile does not have projectile drop like the
, meaning that it is much easier to snipe targets at long range.
The Missile Pistol's explosion has 30 demo force, and can be used to destroy Bug Holes, Automaton Fabricators, and Grounded Warp Ships.

Breakable armor can also be destroyed quickly for follow-up attacks.

due to matching armor penetration.

or

If the magazine is empty, Helldivers may choose to only load half the magazine and cancel loading the other clip by interrupting the reload. This can be done by swapping to another weapon, pressing melee, opening the map/stratagem menu, diving or simply firing.
Like the

Due to its high recoil and slower than average reload, Helldivers are advised to equip armor with the
or
passives.

The Veto's appearance is loosely based off an amalgamation of the Mauser C96 and the P08 Luger pistols, both famous for their service in World War 1, sharing the C96’s distinctive clip-fed magazine, and the Luger’s iconic toggle-lock action.

s: The Crisper can be unlocked on the 3rd page of the Freedom's Flame Premium Warbond for 45 Medals.
The P-72 Crisper is a
that occupies the Secondary Weapon slot.
It boasts the same damage, firing range, and penetration power as the

Each canister contains enough fuel for 6.1 seconds of sustained fire, and fuel is not consumed between lighting the pilot light and firing.
It can be wielded with one hand, allowing Helldivers to use it while carrying objectives.
The Crisper possesses AP 4 penetration, meaning it can directly damage
and Hulks through their front armor.
As with all flamethrower weapons, the pilot light must be ignited before firing by holding the fire button. It may be fired instantly at any time while the pilot light is active.
The pilot light will extinguish automatically after a roughly 12-second period of disuse.
The pilot light will appear to visually extinguish roughly 2 seconds before it mechanically extinguishes.
Firing at the floor will create a pool of fire that continues to burn for several seconds. This can set Helldivers on fire too, so advancing whilst firing is not advised.
Due to the Crisper’s small ammo capacity, lighting the ground on fire, and kiting enemies through the flames is an effective, economical strategy.
Diving directly backwards while shooting the Crisper will catch the Helldiver on fire, due to their legs passing in front of the jet.

s: The P-92 Warrant can be bought from the Force of Law page on the Superstore for 300 Super Credits.
The P-92 Warrant is unique in that it's the one of only two loadout weapons with the ability to lock onto enemies by aiming down the sights (The other being the
The Warrant has two firing modes: Guided and Non-Guided.
Guided mode
Disables the gun from firing unless it has locked onto a valid target. A 'valid target' is any Small, Medium, or Large size enemy - it cannot lock on to Massive enemies.
Maximum lock-on distance is 60 meters.
The lock-on time is extremely fast - approximately half a second, and almost instant for follow-up shots on targets that were near the first.
Shots will steer towards the targeted enemy, curving in mid-air. The degree at which bullets swerve is limited, and doesn't exceed 40°~ of curvature.
Once a lock is set, it will not acquire a different target unless the user stops aiming, breaks line-of-sight with the target, or the target is killed.

As with all weaponry with lock-on capabilities, guided shots always target center mass rather than weak points. This makes it very unlikely to hit the most vulnerable area of an enemy. Some Terminids are an exception to this due to their large heads and quadrupedal posture.
Non-Guided mode
Allows the user to fire the pistol freely, like any other firearm. When switching to this mode, the optic sight flips down.
Despite being a AP 3 penetrating weapon, the Warrant is most efficient at clearing out smaller enemies at mid-range. This makes it exceptionally useful on low
missions. A Helldiver needs merely aim in the rough direction of their enemies. The targeting system does the rest.
The most practical use cases for the guided mode are:
Hitting targets that are difficult to land shots on due to their mobility, such as
etc.
Targeting units surrounding fellow helldivers without risking friendly fire.
Targeting units in low visibility conditions, such as on planets with a lot of dust or fog, at night, or while in Blizzards / Sandstorms.
Even when not directly aiding in combat, the lock-on can serve as a niche scouting tool, detecting enemies that otherwise may be difficult to spot. Notably, it can lock-on to
even while they're invisible.
The guided mode will target the pilots of
and
, allowing one to dispatch them when their cockpit shield is depleted.
Guided mode can be a hindrance in some other cases:

The lock-on circle on the HUD can indicate a lock on an enemy that is near the edge of the circle at any range. In close quarters, this is too far off-target for the guidance system to compensate for. The wielder will have to both aim manually and have a valid lock on in order to score a hit in this situation.

The guided mode is also not infallible at extended ranges. Targets that are moving laterally may still require leading in order for projectiles to hit. Approaching, retreating, and stationary enemies are most likely to be hit.
Enemies behind partial cover may not be exposed enough for the targeting system to lock on to them. Ranged enemies in this scenario can attack with impunity unless the weapon is on unguided mode.
are worth particular mention in this context. They can occupy a target lock in addition to being very difficult to angle guided shots around their shield.
Guided mode's requirement that the weapon be sighted makes it impossible to fire the weapon without slowing to a walking pace. Against
and other resilient, aggressive enemies, it may be wiser to switch to unguided mode and fire while running.
The Warrant is the second firearm obtainable from the Superstore, the first being the limited time crossover exclusive
The Warrant along with its

appear to reference Judge Dredd from the 2000 AD comics, with the Warrant specifically resembling Dredd's signature "Lawgiver" pistol. It differs from its source material in that it does not have the ability to switch between multiple exotic ammunition types on demand.

The Warrant's armory description describing jet propelled ammunition exists in real life via the now discontinued Gyrojet, a unique family of firearms designed to fire specialized mini-rockets called "Microjets." Unlike its real life parallel however, the Warrant appears to have recoil and a system for guiding its rounds towards targets.
As of version 1.003.101, The P-92 Warrant's Non-Guided rounds are able to penetrate through enemies and their hitboxes, regardless of their armor class.
The round stops at the first obstacle hit, and then continues to do damage a short distance after impact, similar to melee weapons. Hitboxes under armor, such as
legs and inner flesh are the best examples of this.

Additionally, the P-92 Warrant's reticle whilst using its Non-Guided mode is bugged, moving towards Heavy and above enemies in view and turning green as if using the Guided mode. Fixed as of PATCH 01.003.103

s: The P/40-K Bolt Pistol is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Castellan’s Creed Legendary Warbond for 50 Medals.
The Bolt Pistol possesses the highest damage per shot of all conventional sidearms in the game, as well as AP 4 armor penetration and explosive rounds.
Like the
, this high damage comes with the drawback of considerable recoil, making follow-up shots more difficult as well as rather poor ergo for a sidearm.
At a value of 325, the Bolt Pistol currently has the highest recoil value of any weapon in the game.
This kickback can be mitigated by crouching, aiming-down-sights, and wearing armor with passives that reduce recoil, such as
, and
The Bolt Pistol is capable of killing a majority of medium enemies with a single shot, when aimed at a weak point. Examples include
, and
Despite being an explosive projectile, Bolt Pistol rounds cannot destroy enemy spawners (such as Bug Holes and Automaton Fabricators), as the explosion only has 10
With a 6 round capacity and 4 spare magazines, the Bolt Pistol has a very poor ammo economy; it is important that Helldivers pick their shots carefully.
This can be slightly alleviated by equipping armor with the
passive, adding one more spare magazine.
Like the
and primaries such as the
, the Bolt Pistol fires jet-assisted rounds, meaning they suffer no damage falloff and minimal drop over distance.

Helldivers may find that the Bolt Pistol's large frame and stubby iron sights make First-Person View quite difficult to aim precisely. They may find it easier to simply use the normal aiming reticle in Third-Person View.

The P/40-K Bolt Pistol shares similarities in appearance to the Godwyn-Branx Pattern Bolt Pistol. It is predominantly featured in the video game, Warhammer 40,000: Darktide, as one of the few Bolt-weapons that can be used by the player characters.

The producer of this weapon is ST Construction, referencing the Warhammer 40,000 Standard Template Constructs. These STC Systems are equivalent to technological time capsules, serving to preserve blueprints and knowledge from the Dark Age of Technology.

s: The Loyalist is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Truth Enforcers Premium Warbond for 45 Medals.
Functioning effectively as a sidearm equivalent of the
, the Loyalist is distinguished from it by its lower damage and much lower ammo capacity.
Like the Purifier, the Loyalist can either be charged up to fire highly damaging and moderately large plasma explosions, or tap-fired in a pinch to rapidly deliver lower-damage bolts.
Unlike the Purifier, the Loyalist's direct plasma bolt penetrates only Light armor when uncharged.
Due to its innate splash damage even on un-charged shots, the Loyalist proves to be a poor emergency self-defense weapon. However, it is a powerful tool for bombarding enemies at medium range.
It's especially risky to use the Loyalist's fully charged blasts against aggressive enemies that manage to catch a Helldiver off-guard, such as
, and especially
, since the explosion can cause self damage when fired at close range combatants.
The explosion from a fully-charged shot will stagger and greatly push back enemies as large as
and
. Use this to maintain distance and safely follow up with more blasts.
Both the charged bolt and accompanying explosion deal high amounts of damage to durable enemy parts, even relative to many primary weapons. This is especially useful against
butts and Tank vents.
Because the Loyalist is a one-handed weapon, shots can be charged from the hip while maintaining full walking speed.

One notable quirk with the Loyalist's Third Person aim mode is that the reticle isn't an accurate representation of where the pistol will shoot; the actual shot will stray slightly to the left. This can be nullified by using First Person aiming.
The Loyalist's high stagger/push force, and relatively low damage makes it an ideal weapon for flipping a rolled FRV without popping the tires.

s: The Bushwhacker is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Viper Commandos Premium Warbond for 50 Medals.

The Bushwhacker is a one-handed shotgun that offers two distinct firing modes. The first mode fires each barrel individually, while the second mode fires all three barrels of 10-Gauge Buckshot simultaneously. and

or

s: The 40-K Meltagun is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Castellan’s Creed Legendary Warbond for 110 Medals.
The Meltagun fires a continuous beam like the
but trades range and unlimited ammo for massive DPS and higher armor penetration. However, unlike other beam-firing laser weapons, the Meltagun does not set enemies on fire.

The Meltagun has a short charge-up time before firing, leaving a short window of vulnerability for users. To effectively fire it, Helldivers should maintain some distance between enemies in order to charge up the weapon and land shots.
Once the Meltagun is charged, it fires continuously for roughly 1.4 seconds before needing to be charged again, dealing a maximum theoretical damage of 3,640 per burst.
The Meltagun, however, suffers from damage fall-off, which is unique for beam weapons. 40% of damage is lost at its maximum range of 15 meters — dealing ~1,560 DPS.
With 3 rounds per magazine and 4 spares, the Meltagun can be fired 15 times before running empty.
This can be alleviated by equipping armor with the
passive, adding one more spare magazine.
While firing, aiming adjustments to the beam are limited by the poor ergonomics of the Meltagun.
This can be alleviated by wearing armor with the Peak Physique passive, which adds +30 to all weapons' ergonomics value.
The Meltagun is extremely effective against heavy enemies such as
, and
s, killing them in 1 to 2 shots anywhere on their body.
Massive enemies can be destroyed with 1 to 2 shots to their weak spots, such as a
's belly panels and a
's head.
The Meltagun is also extremely effective against a variety of enemy structures such as Shrieker Nests, Spore Spewers, and Command Bunkers, destroying them all in one shot.
All enemy spawners (besides Bug Holes) can be destroyed with 1 to 2 bursts of the Meltagun.
Grounded Warp Ships will require 3 bursts if the energy shield is deployed, one burst being used to take down the shield.

Within its operational 20-meter of its line of sight, the Tesla Tower will shock any valid target starting with the closest one to use as a conduit for arc-chaining.
Targeting list includes but is not limited to:
A non-crawling Helldiver
Hostile non-SEAF units
Specific stratagems
Other destructibles (E.G. Terminid Eggs).
However, Tesla Tower specifically will not target Citizens or Generators (though both can be caught as a conduit for chain-lighting).
The Tesla Tower prioritizes on targets with lower health and armor rating, switching to them if already having engaged with heavier targets (E.G. from a
to a Helldiver if one has entered the targeting range).

The line of sight (LoS) is mainly measured from the ground / two-dimensional-plane. This is most noticeable by having an active (protruding) Hellpod Stratagem placed between a Helldiver and a Tesla Tower, rendering the Tesla Tower not even attempting to zap the Helldiver. This negation of LoS is easiest to reproduce with the
The Tesla Tower considers a diving Helldiver being already in a prone position. It is possible to keep on "dolphin-diving" near a friendly Tesla Tower for faster traversal.
Tesla Towers will zap any Helldiver whose "prone"-stance is broken / disrupted in the middle of dive. For example, falling from too high and thus transitioning into the "ragdolled"-state.

Tesla Tower may also inadvertently hit Helldivers if an enemy enters the targeting range of Tesla Tower and a Helldiver is within the range, either being in the path of the arc or to be chained to from the enemy.
The A/ARC-3 Tesla Tower takes 1 second to charge up, after which it sends out a devastatingly powerful electrical arc at its target. Lighter enemies like
and
will die to a single hit.

The Tesla Tower's necessary proximity to enemies can both help and hinder it. It will attract the attention of light enemies that it will easily kill, but also heavy enemies that will just as easily destroy it with a long-ranged attack or a rapid close-range attack.
Distracted ranged enemy units (primarily by being "aggroed" to a Helldiver) such as
however do enter the attack range of Tesla Tower. But otherwise, when given enough line of sight, they won't enter the shocking range and instead will engage the Tesla Tower from outside its range.
The Tesla Tower is still able to stagger many heavy enemies such as
. Clever placement will allow Tesla Tower to stun and dispatch heavy enemies before they able to fully focus upon it.

The arcs that chain from target to target can reach beyond the initial targeting range. These chains can also travel outside the line of sight of the Tesla Tower, and oftentimes hit Helldivers in prone position due to arc-conduiting-mechanics; for this reason, it is not advised to reside next a Tesla Tower in the first place.
An arc-chain has a maximum horizontal turn angle of 300-degrees from target to target and can chain and split twice.

The arc-chains of Tesla Tower severely lack vertical elevation climbing capability, virtually rendering the chains of arcs uncapable travelling between targets of even small elevation differences (E.G. from a
to an
and vice-versa).
Tesla Tower will attempt to use the protruding or otherwise active Hellpod Stratagems such as Resupply pods and
as conduits without success; this will fortunately only negligibly damage the Hellpod-stratagems due to the built-in arc-damage protection akin to even more potent
armor passive.
The arcing / chaining (and fast destruction) does occur through vehicles such as the
, and even the Pelican extraction shuttle.
Tesla Tower often prioritizes destructibles such as Exploding Barrels as conduits.
Helldivers will be killed instantly if hit by the Arc attack.
Helldivers wearing
armor take significantly reduced damage from the Tesla Tower's attack. However, during Acid Storms the damage inflicted is doubled.

Damage amount also depends on the first body part hit. E.G. A shock on a leg causes approximately 30-damage while torso/chest approx. 50-damage. Each initial shock will damage/break the targeted body part.

The targeted body part depends on the elevation differences: On same "bottom" elevation Tesla Tower always hits either of the leg of Helldiver. If Helldiver is at least a metre above the base of Tesla Tower, the chest of Helldiver is targeted.
If not destroyed, a single Tesla Tower will remain in place for 150 seconds, firing an infinite number of arcs until it expires.
With the base cooldown of 120-seconds, it is possible to have multiple active Tesla Towers even before any associated Ship Module upgrades.

Setting up another Tesla Tower within 20-meters of other is highly recommended against due to aforementioned conduit-preference attempts. In practice, this will render a Tesla Tower being unable to arc on target units located near the other Tesla Tower due to arc getting stuck in (and negligibly but still destructively damaging) the other Tesla Tower.
This same goes every other SEAF-armaments, especially even Helldivers located opposite direction of non-SEAF-units.
The light variant of the
-passive armor allows Helldivers to dodge the electrical arc at a sufficient distance at while running perpendicular to the direction of the arc.
Armor with the
or
passive effects will reduce the range at which the Tesla Tower targets a Helldiver from 20 to 16 and 14 meters respectively, a slightly wider radius than described by the passive effects themselves.
Crouching additionally reduces these targeting ranges by another ~25%.

The Gatling Sentry fires the same rounds as the A/MG-43 Machine Gun Sentry but at 153% higher rpm. This effectively means that the Gatling Sentry has more than double the DPS.
The Gatling Sentry has a spool up and spool down time which results in it continuously firing as it changes targets.
The downside to this high rpm is that the Gatling Sentry does not stop firing when rotating towards new targets and will overkill most enemies, leading to a short lifetime.

This trait gives the Gatling Sentry a bit of a reputation for teamkilling. Helldivers should exercise caution in the placement of this sentry, and take note of its fire arc, especially if Civilians, SEAF troopers, or other friendly units are nearby.
This also makes the Gatling Sentry distinctly better at dealing with masses of
s and
s.
The Gatling Sentry has a range of 75m and requires line of sight to valid targets. Note that enemy corpses can block line of sight.
While a massive friendly fire hazard, this does benefit the Gatling Sentry against masses of Terminids.

Like the A/MG-43 Machine Gun Sentry unlocked before it, the Gatling Sentry will prefer to target small and medium sized enemies, but will still target heavily armored enemies if they are no other valid targets and also continue firing at the same target until said target is destroyed, the sentry runs out of ammo or the sentry itself is destroyed.

Due to Gatling Sentry longer cooldown, higher DPS and total ammunition pool, the Gatling Sentry is more specialized to holdouts compared to it's MG counterpart - being significantly less likely to be overrun.
Note that a single Gatling Sentry also has more than double the ammunition supply compared to the MG-43 Sentry.

The Rocket Sentry fires AP 5 armor penetrating rockets with a low rate of fire. Due to this, its main role is to destroy heavy enemies.
The Rocket Sentry is the longest-range direct-fire sentry, with a 100m engagement distance.
This alone makes it better for engaging ranged units than other sentries, a fact especially true when fighting the Automatons.

It also allows for a greater range of deployment positions in general. Placing one on a high point before Helldivers move onto an objective will allow it to provide excellent covering fire with minimal chance of destruction.

. Effectiveness can depend on the range to its target, as the projectiles are slow, and can easily miss a fast-moving enemy.
The sentry has a backblast when it fires, which will ragdoll and slightly damage Helldivers in a small cone behind it. Be mindful of this when deploying the sentry or fighting around it.

, etc)
The Autocannon has a 10-round internal magazine that is reloaded via 5-round stripper clips pulled from the backpack.
Reloading while carrying the backpack causes the Helldiver to drop to one knee and remain immobile during the animation.
Reloading a single clip takes 1.2 seconds, but reloading the entire magazine from empty takes about 3.6 seconds, due to the Helldiver needing to cycle the bolt.
It is advised to never let the magazine run empty to avoid a longer reload time.
If the magazine is empty, Helldivers may choose to only load half the magazine and cancel loading the other clip
The Autocannon's wielder can carry the ammo backpack, but if a teammate assists in reloading and/or carries that backpack instead, Team Reloading is much faster.
Ammo Boxes will add 2 clips to the backpack, and a Resupply box will add 5 (10 if Superior Packing Methodology has been unlocked).
Like all explosive weaponry, Helldivers are advised to not fire at enemies at point-blank range. The explosion from the Autocannon's explosive rounds will kill the wielder.
It is highly advised to crouch or go prone when possible to fire the weapon for reduced recoil.
The Engineering Kit or Fortified armor passives can help with reducing the Autocannon's recoil.
The Autocannon has a low ergonomics value of 17, meaning that it is slower to move around while aiming.
This can be alleviated by wearing armor with the Peak Physique passive, which adds +30 to all weapons' ergonomics value.
Additionally, armor with the True Grit passive increases the ergonomics by 20 while also making reloads faster. This is especially effective when used with the Autocannon.

s) from over 100m away in a single shot.

s: The AMR is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center for 5,000 Requisition at Level 1.

The AMR can also be found in some Places of Interest, primarily in Pods and Cargo Containers, and can also be found near the missile silo on Launch ICBM, Evacuate High-Value Assets, or Rapid Acquisition missions.

The AMR is a long-range support weapon, boasting a powerful 10x scope zoom and AP 4 armor-piercing rounds. Its high damage rounds excel at dispatching medium sized enemies with a single well-placed shot.
Several medium & large enemies on all fronts, such as
, and
can all be killed in a single shot to their weak spots.
Hulks can also be killed with a single shot to the eye, however this only works at closer ranges. Beyond roughly 30m, a second shot is required.
The scope can switch between 50m, 100m, and 200m zeros, enabling the Helldivers to engage enemies from a mid to long range.
The AMR can be fired as fast as the trigger is pulled. This grants high damage potential, albeit with high recoil.
Aiming down sights, crouching, laying prone or equipping armor that reduces recoil, (such as
and
) can greatly mitigate recoil.
This high firerate is useful when firing into the weakpoints of heavy enemies, downing or killing them outright at speeds quicker than other AP 4 support weapons.
Due to the AMR's low ergonomics stat and the high importance of placing shots accurately, Helldivers may get improved results in shot placement by equipping armor with the
or
perks, both of which grant improved ergonomics.
The low magazine size and lack of area-of-effect damage render the AMR ill-suited for crowd control. Helldivers may cover this weakness by bringing reliable close-range weapons like the
or other stratagems like the AX/AR-23 "Guard Dog".
Uniquely, the AMR does not offer a weapon reticle in third person, meaning that Helldivers must switch to ADS to accurately aim the rifle.
Despite this, it can be possible to aim and fire at targets without using the scope, as shots will still fire towards the center of the screen.

It will independently target and attack any nearby enemies, regardless of whether or not it can penetrate their armor. When its magazine is depleted, the Guard Dog will return to its backpack to rearm; it carries up to eight reserve magazines, which can be refilled with the Resupply stratagem or by picking up Ammo Boxes during a mission. The amount of reserve magazines remaining can be seen visually on the backpack, the dark rectangle "arms" that open and close whenever the drone returns to the backpack to reload; the status of the magazine that is currently loaded in the drone is tracked in the HUD. and hovers around the user, engaging any targets within 30 meters.

s: The Supply Pack is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center (in the Engineering Bay subsection) for 4000 Requisition at Level 1.

When called in, the Supply Pack arrives fully stocked with four resupply boxes. Each of these functions the same as a resupply box from the Resupply stratagem, though it does not benefit from the Superior Packing Methodology ship module upgrade. Pressing the "Interact" button on a teammate (PC default press E, PlayStation default press X) will resupply their ammunition, stims, and grenades in the same fashion. The Supply Pack can also be used by its wearer to resupply their own stocks, this is done by pressing the "Use Backpack Function" button (PC default press 5, PlayStation default press D-Pad Down).

The Supply Pack can only be refilled by picking up a supply box from the Resupply stratagem. One Resupply box will refill one box on the Supply Pack, regardless of whether or not the Superior Packing Methodology upgrade has been unlocked. Stray Ammo Boxes, Grenade Cases, and Stim Crates found within a mission cannot refill the Supply Pack. Refilling the Supply Pack will also refill the wearer's other supplies as normal.

The primary utility of the Supply Pack is to be able to provide supplies to oneself and to teammates on the move, without having to call down the Resupply stratagem. This can be particularly useful when the team is split up in such a way that a Resupply stratagem cannot be used by all teammates, or a team member has a particularly ammo-hungry weapon that needs to be constantly replenished.
The number of supply boxes carried in the Supply Pack is visible on the wearer's back. This makes it easy to visually keep track of how many spare supplies are on hand.
It is most supply-efficient to carry supply-hungry equipment alongside the Supply Pack, such as the Engineering Kit or Med Kit Armor Passives, or the
. This way, refilling the Supply Pack from a Resupply will help to top off the increased threshold for maximum Grenades and Stims on Engineering Kit and Med Kit armor, respectively.
Keep track of your team's supply situation to see when they need a resupply.

When their supply icon in the lower-left corner of the HUD is flashing red, it means they are low in that category. If it is solid red, they are fully depleted. However, be aware that the backpack icon status may be misleading in the case of backpacks like the
and
, which are not crew weapon ammunition backpacks.
You can also visually confirm how much reserve ammunition certain support weapons like the
or
have by looking at their backpacks.
Be strategic about calling in a Resupply and picking up supply boxes, keeping teammates' needs in mind.

As with normally calling down Resupply, it is ideal to do so when the team is not in immediate combat. This not only allows teammates to refill their supplies at their leisure, but also grants an opportunity to replenish the Supply Pack without depriving teammates of supplies. Effective communication is key.

Because a supply box refills your supplies while also adding a box to the Supply Pack, it is doubly efficient to pick up a Resupply box to refill your supplies and then directly resupply teammates. However, be aware of whether or not Superior Packing Methodology has been unlocked, as giving a teammate a resupply from the Supply Pack will give them less ammo for their support weapon than if they picked up a box from the Resupply Hellpod themselves. Be mindful of the situation, and communicate with teammates prior to taking more than one supply box.

After the team is finished resupplying, pick up the remaining supply boxes from the Resupply Hellpod to replenish your Supply Pack. It is better to carry supplies with a team member in a known location than to leave the boxes strewn around where they may never be found or used again.

If a team's supplies are low in a situation where the Resupply stratagem is not enough, and the Supply Pack stratagem is off cooldown, it can be useful to call down another Supply Pack in a pinch. Refill everyone's supplies with the currently-equipped Supply Pack to deplete it, and then replace it with a fresh one via calldown.
Keep in mind that the cooldown time for the Supply Pack is significantly longer than that for a Resupply, so this should only be done in emergencies.

As with other backpack stratagems, calling in a spare one for a teammate who has an empty backpack slot can benefit the team as a whole. Two players with the ability to carry supply boxes around and resupply their teammates can significantly augment the team's overall robustness, though both backpacks still need to be refilled individually from Resupply calldowns.
If in a duo, it can work well to have one diver hold a support backpack weapon and supply pack and a loader to have the support backpack, as the shooter can resupply ammo to the loader.
