The Portable Hellbomb is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Servants of Freedom Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

In Destroy Spore Lung missions, because the objective is in an underground cave, a free B-100 Portable Hellbomb stratagem is granted in place of the standard Hellbomb until the mission objective is complete. It uses an alternative stratagem code: ↓ → ↑ ↑ ↓

By default, the Portable Hellbomb is in an inert state, providing no benefits while inactive and occupying the backpack slot of the player when carried. In order to utilize it, the Portable Hellbomb must first be activated, either by the bomb carrier or a teammate standing close to the wearer. The wearer can activate it by pressing the "Use Backpack Function" button (PC default press 5, PlayStation default press D-Pad Down), while another player close by can interact with the backpack with the "Portable Hellbomb" prompt (PC default press E, PlayStation default press X).

Upon activation, the Portable Hellbomb will emit a loud alarm and begin counting down. After ten seconds it will explode, regardless of whether or not it is being worn. There is no way to suspend or cancel the countdown, and no way to detonate the explosive payload early.
True to its name, the Portable Hellbomb is an explosive payload that allows the player to deploy a Hellbomb explosion at any location that they can reach.

The Portable Hellbomb has the same destructive capabilities as the standard NUX-223 Hellbomb, meaning that it can instantly kill most enemies within 17-25 meters of the epicenter and destroy any structures that require a
of 60 or lower, which currently includes all structures. Meanwhile, the only enemy that can survive a Hellbomb's epicenter are
s.

Wearing armor with the Democracy Protects passive will grant a 50% chance to survive the explosion even if the backpack is still being worn. However, the massive push force imparted by the explosion can still throw the player into nearby rocks, trees, or buildings, initiating another 50% chance to survive the force of hitting these objects.

The Portable Hellbomb is very useful for quickly destroying mission-related structures (such as Automaton Orbital Cannons, Illuminate Monoliths as well as tactical objectives such as Gunship Facility and Destroy Rogue Research Station) without needing to manually call in, wait for, and then arm a standard Hellbomb.
Due to the massive damage and radius of the Portable Hellbomb, Helldivers are advised to immediately reach a safe distance after activation to avoid injury.
The Portable Hellbomb has a rather large destruction radius, meaning it can be dropped below a Stratagem Jammer or Detector Tower rather than next to it and still reliably destroy it.
As previously mentioned, a free Portable Hellbomb will be granted during missions with an active Destroy Spore Lung objective. Once the objective is destroyed, it will no longer be available.
In combination with an
, the Portable Hellbomb can be activated and placed behind the incoming beam, causing it to be catapulted when the Stratagem unfolds.

s: The Hellbomb is based off the B54 Special Atomic Demolition Munition, an American, Cold War era, man-portable nuclear explosive with a yield of up to 1 kiloton. It was intended for use in the demolition of hardened enemy infrastructure by engineer units, or behind enemy lines to destroy troop concentrations, enemy infrastructure, or armored formations such as tank laagers, as part of a covert insertion, usually by parachute, by specially trained US Army Special Forces Green Light teams.

There is a legible warning label above the timer display screen on the back of the Hellbomb. Amongst other prudent warnings, it states that the device should not be given to children under the age of 12.

The B/FLAM-80 Cremator is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Entrenched Division Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

The B/FLAM-80 Cremator boasts increased fire damage and an ammunition backpack with 500 units of fuel. As a backpack hose-fed weapon, it has the unique feature that it does not need to be manually reloaded like other backpack-reliant support weapons; however, it cannot be fired without its ammunition backpack equipped. Unlike the
, Helldivers can move freely while firing the B/FLAM-80 Cremator, allowing for greater flexibility.

When the B/FLAM-80 Cremator and its Ammunition Backpack are initally picked up, a roughly 1-second animation will play where the Helldiver connects the fuel hose into the Support Weapon. This connection will remain unless the two parts are forcibly detached, in which it must be reconnected in order to fire again.
The B/FLAM-80 Cremator is a more powerful

. It has increased range and coverage, deals more damage due to its double-barreled nature, and can fire for longer periods of time. However, it requires its associated backpack tank to operate and has less fuel time overall than a fully resupplied FLAM-40.
The Cremator has a range of roughly 25 meters (measured in first person), which is 25% more than the FLAM-40's 20-meter range.
Before firing, the pilot light must be ignited by holding the fire button. It may be fired instantly at any time while the pilot light is active.
The pilot light will extinguish automatically after a roughly 12-second period of disuse.
The pilot light will appear to visually extinguish roughly 2 seconds before it mechanically extinguishes.
Firing at the floor will create a pool of fire that continues to burn for several seconds. This can set Helldivers on fire too, so advancing whilst firing is not advised.
Diving directly backwards while shooting the Cremator will catch the Helldiver on fire, due to their legs passing in front of the jet.
While the weapon is fired from slightly different locations between first- and third-person views, both can still easily light a Helldiver's legs on fire.
Its fire jet deals continuous damage throughout its travel. Skewering a target lengthwise can greatly increase the effect.
This weapon performs best on open ground. The flames are easily blocked by terrain or worse, bounced back at the Helldiver at short range.
Each full backpack contains enough fuel to fire for 62.35 seconds, and fuel is not consumed between lighting the pilot light and firing.
Entering and exiting any FRV type, the
, any Exosuit, and any Emplacement stratagem will always make the Helldiver reattach the hose of the B/FLAM-80 Cremator.
The following bug also occurs every time the Helldiver leans out of any FRV and the Bastion's passenger seats.

The Cremator resembles the Imperial Guard version of the ubiquitous flamer from Warhammer 40,000, seen in this model of a Kasrkin. Both are fed from a backpack fuel tank connected by a hose, but the Cremator is double-barreled whereas the flamer has a single barrel.

The Cremator seems to be inspired by real-life backpack-fed flamethrowers, such as the American M2, M9, and M1 flamethrowers used during WWII and the Cold War. All of these designs feature two fuel tanks, but only a single barrel or nozzle.

s: The B/MD C4 Pack is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Redacted Regiment Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

The B/MD C4 Pack has two different components to it, the backpack and the detonator. The backpack stores up to 6 charges for the trigger and the trigger can hold a seventh to be thrown. The detonator has two different firing modes:
Deploy Mode.
This throws out a destructible C4 charge which will stick to the first surface it hits, which will be ignored by enemies.
Detonate Mode.
This will instantaneously trigger all currently deployed C4 charges to deliver a powerful explosion in a small radius.
C4 is a middle ground between dedicated Anti-Tank weaponry like the
and explosive chaff clear weaponry like the
As the C4 lacks a long or stationary reload, it is able to destroy multiple heavy units quicker than other AT weapons, and the explosion can be used to destroy swarms of chaff as well.
In addition to the fast reload rate, C4 can also be thrown while running thanks to the one-handed trait. Because of this, C4 is very effective at fighting massive units like
s,
s and
s, as it can deal large damage very quickly while dodging attacks at the same time.
It is highly recommended that Helldivers bind their "Quick Weapon Wheel Left" key in order to quickly switch between deploy and detonate mode with the C4.
Helldivers can look at their right hand to see which mode they are in. In Deploy Mode they'll hold a C4 brick, in Detonate Mode they'll hold the detonator instead.
A single C4 can be used to destroy spawners such as Bile Titan Holes, Bot Fabricators and shielded Grounded Warp Ships, even from the outside.
C4 can also be used to destroy several Mission Objectives such as Command Bunkers, Bio-Processors, and Broadcast Towers.
C4 can also be used to destroy obstructions such as Colony Walls and Mega Factory Gates.
The C4 Pack can be used offensively against large enemies such as
s, Hulks,
s, and
s, killing them with a single charge if placed correctly.
The C4 is one of the best ways to kill
s, requiring only two from any angle without the need to hit weakpoints.
Thrown C4 charges have a very generous throw range, but also benefit from the bonus throwing range of the
and
armor passives.
With quick timing, charges can be detonated in mid-air to 'airburst' them near vulnerable targets.
There is a short delay when the trigger is pulled before C4 detonates. Pulling the trigger again will restart the delay, so avoid repeatedly tapping the trigger to ensure prompt detonation.
The C4 pack is uniquely suited for stealth gameplay, allowing Helldivers to set explosives on enemy assets, then retreat to a safe distance before detonation.
There is no limit to how many C4 charges may be deployed as long as the Helldiver can keep the backpack supplied.

When hosting a game, Helldivers may often experience a bug where thrown C4 bricks will alert any enemies they come in contact to. To alleviate this, the C4 carrier should designate another Helldiver as the host.

s: The Defoliation Tool is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Python Commandos Premium Warbond for 85 Medals.
The Defoliation Tool increases armor penetration from AP 3 to AP 5 as well as
from 10 to 30 over the course of 0.5s of continuous contact with an enemy or structure at the rate of +2 AP and 20 demo force per second.
Defoliation Tool Specific

The Defoliation Tool is unique among all melee weapons in that landing an attack on an enemy or destructible object will cause the sawblades to slowly drag along the target, rapidly dealing damage throughout the animation.
Once the blades make contact with a target, the weapon will not disengage until the blades are no longer in contact with any target, even if the attack input is released.
In the event the blades make contact with terrain such as the ground Helldivers will immediately disengage, resetting AP and demo accumulation.

The damage is applied both per second (at multiple ticks per second), and per hit, meaning if you switch between body parts or move the saw in and out of the enemy quickly your DPS can be higher, however the blade needs to lose contact with the enemy for the ”swing damage” to reset. Switching between body parts or losing contact with the enemy will reset any AP and demo accumulation.
Foliage, low concrete barriers, heavy steel fences, Automaton Fabricators, Grounded Warp Ships, Landed Automaton Dropships and Lightning Spires can be destroyed via the Defoliation Tool.
The range of the Defoliation Tool can be extended by diving, allowing it to damage and stun enemies further away.
Moving the camera towards enemies while attacking will allow for more damage onto targets.
It is advised to pair the Defoliation Tool with a backpack that either protects Helldivers, such as the
, or one that allows for faster movement, such as the
and
Due to the swing speed being just slow enough for stamina to start regenerating, this number is affected by Stamina Regen value and the
Booster. Additionally, hitting any targets will slow effective swing speed, further complicating this.
Wearing Light armor with stamina enhancement booster, Helldivers can swing the Defoliation Tool a total of 34 times before stamina is completely drained.
Wearing Heavy armor without the booster, Helldivers can swing the Defoliation Tool a total of 65+ times before stamina is completely drained.
The Defoliation Tool's engine will not alert enemies to the Helldiver's presence while the weapon is being held or otherwise in use, unless swung in directly proximity to them.
The Defoliation tool along with the
are the only melee weapons that require both hands to use. Therefore, carriables like the
or data drives will be stowed or dropped when these weapons are equipped.
Melee Weapons

Melee weapons deal all of their damage to the first segment or "body part" of any given entity that they come into contact with. Additional segments of the same unit that the weapon passes through will be ignored. This only applies to the swing damage of the chainsaw, and only as long as it maintains contact with the enemy.
Wearing
with the
or
passive will increase melee damage by 40%, greatly increasing its lethality. Armor with the
passive will increase melee damage by 20%,.
Attacking with the Defoliation Tool drains stamina.
Holding the attack button will allow Helldivers to continuously thrust the Defoliation tool, even when stamina is empty.

The Anti-Tank Emplacement is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Urban Legends Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.
The Anti-Tank Emplacement is a stationary fortification that grants accurate long-range rapid-fire anti-tank capability that can easily destroy even the largest of enemies.
Like its cousin the
, the Anti-Tank Emplacement is a mounted weapon that players can man to directly control their fire. It will persist for the entirety of the mission so long as its ammunition has not been depleted.
As an Emplacement, it cannot be relocated once it has been called in and requires a Helldiver to physically man the weapon.

This emplacement can only be interacted with or entered from in front of or atop the operator chair; lack of ground around the chair itself after initial assembly can render an Anti-Tank Emplacement impossible to enter.

The cannon of the Anti-Tank Emplacement launches anything on top of it when deploying, making it a falling hazard to any Helldivers standing atop. With a little practice, this can also be used to launch armed
toward objectives, enemy encampments, or enemy patrols.

The AT Emplacement rotates very sluggishly, roughly half the turning speed of the HMG Emplacement. This makes it extremely dangerous to engage enemies at close range or to get attacked from multiple directions.
The Anti-Tank Emplacement's shells inflict roughly 18% more damage per shot than the
(1,300 vs 1,100), and can destroy the same targets. However, it can do so much more quickly due to its huge shell reserves, fast projectile speed, and fast autoloader capability.

As it meets the same breakpoints as the Commando, this means that it generally requires two or more shots to kill most heavy enemies, even when aiming at weak points. However, its rapid-fire capability means it can sustain this firepower over an extended period of time, giving it much more staying power than anti-tank support weapons.

Because it has a 30-shell reserve, the Anti-Tank Emplacement is very effective at eliminating all heavy enemies during an engagement, whether it be while assaulting an enemy base or fighting a reinforcement wave.
Keep in mind that the Anti-Tank Emplacement can shoot virtually anything it can see, only taking into account projectile drop due to gravity. As such, try to put the emplacement down on high ground.

As the Anti-Tank Emplacement can engage targets from very far away, it does not have to be placed near teammates in order to support them. Putting it down farther behind the line can provide a measure of safety while still allowing it to safely engage any heavy targets.
The Anti-Tank Emplacement fares extremely well against Automatons, as it is capable of easily and quickly killing Hulks,
s and Tanks, as well as shooting down
s and

s with ease. Its ability to destroy Automaton Fabricators, Cannon Turrets, and Command Bunkers also allows it to destroy bases from standoff range and even inflict significant damage to Fortresses on Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive) difficulty.
While actively using the Anti-Tank Emplacement, Helldivers are quite vulnerable to flanking enemies, such as
s and
s.
This issue can be partially mitigated with the use of Guard Dog stratagems, as they stay active while operating the Anti-Tank Emplacement.

will always make the Helldiver reattach the feeding mechanism of the support weapons listed.

The HMG Emplacement is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center (in the Bridge section) for 10000 Requisition at Level 10.
A defensive emplacement, the HMG Emplacement calls down a pair of mounted machine guns on a manned rotating emplacement.
Despite the name, the machine guns mounted on the emplacement version are different from the
that the player wields as a support weapon, inflicting more damage per round and only being capable of a single fixed firing rate.
As an expendable emplacement, the HMG Emplacement cannot be reloaded or repaired, and will persist on the field until it runs out of ammunition or is destroyed.

When continuously fired, the HMG Emplacement is capable of maintaining its fire for approximately 30 seconds, affected by Extreme Cold. Each gun contains 300 rounds, and both are fired simultaneously for a combined 11 rounds per second.

The weapon mount can be rotated a full 360º, allowing the operator to engage targets in all directions. However, the turning rate of the mount is very slow, so turning to engage enemies to the sides can take a considerable amount of time. The mount can aim in approximately a 120º cone in front of the base without being subjected to the mounting base's slow rotation speed.
The HMG Emplacement is an extremely effective defensive structure that can quickly and easily eliminate all non-heavy targets it is brought to bear against.

Like the support weapon, the emplacement is capable of penetrating heavy armor, meaning that it outright ignores the armor of almost all medium-sized enemies and can threaten most heavy enemies such as Hulks and
s, even being able to bring down
s.

Because of the turret base's slow rotation speed, the HMG Emplacement is best placed in a position where enemies are funneled into a narrow chokepoint that it is already pointed at. If it does not have to aim in a cone wider than 120º, the base does not have to rotate to engage targets.
The emplacement itself will block incoming projectiles for a limited time, however it cannot withstand high-powered projectiles such as shots from the main gun of an
or being impacted by the melee attacks of a Charger or Bile Titan.

Because the HMG Emplacement does not expire unless empty or destroyed, multiple emplacements can exist simultaneously at the same location. When reaching a defensive hardpoint, try to call down an emplacement as early as possible, to allow the Stratagem to come off of cooldown quickly and call down a second one or more.

The EAT-17 is the first unlockable Support Weapon that is designed to penetrate
, allowing Helldivers to kill heavily-armored enemies from the front.
Its low cooldown, two uses per call-in, and disposability make the EAT-17 stratagem highly flexible.
It can be used as a supplement to a more regularly carried Support Weapon, only being called down upon encountering armored targets and structures.
Conversely, Helldivers can call in EATs immediately when off cooldown, stockpiling several launchers for later use.

Attacks with the Hellpod itself are a potent and economical option against enemy spawners (Bug Holes, Bile Titan Bug Holes, Fabricators), also able to be leveraged against heavies with careful timing or by sticking the Stratagem ball to them.
The EAT can be safely used at close range, dealing the majority of its damage with its projectile and having a small explosion radius.
This and the launcher's ability to be hip-fired are particularly useful when being closely pursued by heavy enemies like
and Hulks.
One disadvantage is its lengthy readying time each launcher requires before firing when equipped from the Hellpod or after being stowed.

Another drawback is a vulnerability to Stratagem-disrupting effects such as Ion Storms, Stratagem Jammers or Scramblers, and Cognitive Disruptors. It also becomes completely unavailable after Super Destroyers leave.
In terms of damage, the EAT occupies the middle tier compared to other anti-tank weapons.

The EAT-411 Leveller and how it operates appears to be partially inspired by the Panzerfaust expendable anti-tank weapon in real life.

In real life, the Panzerfaust was an inexpensive, single-shot, pre-loaded recoilless anti-tank weapon featuring a super-caliber warhead propelled by a black powder charge. It was designed for use by a single infantryman.
In terms of destructive firepower and the overall appearance, the Leveller appears to be partially based upon the Davy Crockett tactical nuclear recoilless gun.

The Davy Crockett was a man-portable weapon system, designed to fire a nuclear warhead with a yield of 10 to 20 tons of TNT (0.01-0.02 kilotons), intended to break up or deter massed attacks of tanks through its initial pulse of high-energy neutrons, hence its status as a neutron bomb.

before getting hit. This "parry" maneuver will significantly save Exosuit durability and will provide an opportunity for a quick countermeasure rather than just taking the hit.

s: The Spear is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center for 9000 Requisition at Level 20.

The Spear cannot be dumb-fired, unlike other rocket launchers. The wielder must aim it at a target which is inside of the large white reticle, causing a small yellow triangle to appear. This triangle is centered on the target and turns green with an accompanying "click" sound when the Spear has successfully locked on, which takes one second. The Spear can then be fired to launch a seeking missile which does high damage. Locks cannot be attained past 300 meters.
The Spear only locks onto "large" targets (larger blip on the minimap) and non-SEAF structures. A list of valid targets can be found below this section.
The Spear requires a clear line of sight to the target to successfully lock-on. Obstacles like foliage and fences can prevent locks, even if it looks like they shouldn't.
This is most egregious with the Bulk Fabricator as its targeting point is very low to the ground relative to its height.
The Spear can still attain locks through smoke and fog, making it useful at countering
s.
The missile's upwards trajectory may cause it to miss enemies at close range. Staying at least 30 meters away from the target is advised.
If forced into close range, Helldivers can go prone to lower the missile's trajectory. Aiming downwards will lower it further.
The reload animation can be cancelled as soon as the HUD shows that a missile has been loaded into the launcher.
The Spear performs best in relatively flat and open biomes, where enemies can be attacked at farther distances.
Sandy and moor biomes are good examples, while the trees in primordial and swamp biomes can block missiles.
The buildings in urban environments can obscure sight lines.

The missile's trajectory is affected by where the Helldiver aims. Aiming left and right can curve the missile to hit weakspots at an angle, while aiming above and below affects the vertical trajectory of the missile.
Diving right before firing a missile imparts the Helldiver's momentum onto it for advanced trajectory manipulation.
The Spear's higher demolition force allows it to destroy Bile Titan Bug Holes.
The Spear is able to destroy a
with a single hit to the fuselage, killing all of its occupants.
This is also able to destroy
s and
s.
Engine strikes are undesirable, as this will generally not guarantee the occupants' deaths.
Helldivers should wait until the Dropship begins slowing down before firing to prevent misses.
The Spear is able to lock onto
even while they are invisible. This can be used to find them if one is aware of their presence, but not their precise location.
The Spear is an effective counter to
es, as one missile is sufficient to destroy a wing or the abdomen.
The
and Dragonroach can outrun the Spear's missiles, causing them to expire and be wasted.
Stingrays are vulnerable when preparing a strafing run.

s: The weapon and how it operates appears to be inspired by the real world FGM-148 Javelin man-portable anti-tank system.
A javelin is a throwing spear, built lighter and with a smaller head, but in shape and ability to pierce armor is very similar to spears, hence the name.
The weapon's designation "FAF" stands for Fire And Forget, referring to the weapon's ability to guide itself to its target upon firing without additional input from the wielder.

s: The FLAM-40 Flamethrower has a range of 20 meters, measured in first person view.
Before firing, the pilot light must be lit by holding the fire button. It may be fired instantly at any time while the pilot light is active.
The pilot light will extinguish automatically after a roughly 12-second period of disuse.
The pilot light will appear to visually extinguish roughly 2 seconds before it mechanically extinguishes.
This excels in dealing with hordes of enemies due to the large 10-meter reaching Area of Effect damage it provides.
Firing at the ground will create a pool of fire that continues to burn for several seconds. This can set Helldivers on fire too, so advancing while firing is not advised.
Diving directly backwards while shooting the Flamethrower can catch the Helldiver on fire, due to their legs passing in front of the jet.
Both first-person and third-person views can do this. While the first-person view fires from higher up near a Helldiver's head instead of the hip, both can still easily catch their feet on fire.
Its stream of fire deals continuous damage throughout its travel. Skewering a target lengthwise can greatly increase the effect.
This weapon performs best on open ground. The flames are easily blocked by terrain or worse, bounced back at the Helldiver at short range.

Unlike chambered weapons, reloading it always takes the same amount of time regardless of how spent the canister is. Conserving a small amount of fuel will not remove any steps from the reload process.
Each canister contains enough fuel for 18.6 seconds of sustained fire, and fuel is not consumed between lighting the pilot light and firing.

s: The GL-28 Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Siege Breakers Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

The GL-28 boasts high rate of fire and an ammunition backpack with 120 grenades. As a backpack belt-fed weapon, it has the unique feature that it does not need to be manually reloaded like other backpack-reliant support weapons; however, it cannot be fired without its ammunition backpack equipped. Unlike the

When the GL-28 Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher and its Ammunition Backpack are initally picked up, a roughly 1-second animation will play where the Helldiver connects the ammunition feed chute into the Support Weapon. This connection will remain unless the two parts are forcibly detached, in which it must be reconnected in order to fire again.

The GL-28 Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher is a high-capacity grenade launcher that excels at inflicting area damage against very large groups of small enemies while also being able to eliminate heavier targets thanks to its AP 4 Armor Penetration.
Compared to the standalone
, the GL-28 trades damage and blast radius for AP 4 armor penetration, increased ammo count and rate of fire.
The GL-28 has better ammo economy and higher uptime vs. the GL-21 due to having a single long belt of 120 grenades vs having to reload 10-round belts.

The GL-28 has two higher rpm options (240 & 320) as well as significantly lower recoil and spread than the GL-21, allowing for much more accurate shots and making it ideal for horde-clearing and stagger-locking fast enemies such as
and charging

Attacking heavy enemies with the GL-28 set to its maximum rate of fire is a relatively quick way to destroy them without an anti-tank weapon, but will take many dozens of grenades to accomplish against massive enemies like
s at full health.
Grenades fired from the GL-28 have a 4m arming distance that prevents them from exploding too soon after firing, causing them to harmlessly bounce off objects and enemies at very close range.
However, after ricocheting, the grenade can still explode once it travels beyond this safety range and strikes the ground, nearby objects, or enemies.
Like other explosive weapons, the GL-28 can destroy Bug Holes and Automaton Fabricators by shooting into their apertures.
This is especially useful on high-difficulty Terminid missions, as there can sometimes be upwards of 50 Bug Holes in total.
The GL-28 has the same issue as the M-1000 Maxigun where leaning out of the FRV (Fast Recon Vehicle) removes the belt from the grenade launcher forcing the Helldiver to re-attach it.

When firing the GL-28 behind low cover, its grenades can hit the cover in front of its user due to the weapon being hip-fired. Aiming in first person will make the projectiles come from the center of the camera, making firing from cover easier.

s: The Recoilless is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center for 6000 Requisition at Level 5.
The Recoilless Rifle has two firing modes:
HEAT, or High-Explosive Anti-Tank mode fires a highly-damaging AP 6 armor-penetrating projectile with a small, low damage, AP 3 armor-penetrating explosion.
HE, or High-Explosive mode fires an AP 5 armor-penetrating projectile with greatly reduced damage (750 vs 3,200) in exchange for a larger, more powerful AP 4 armor-penetrating explosion, similar to a
grenade, albeit with a slightly larger inner radius (3.5m vs 2.5m) and greater stagger force (50 vs 30).
The GR-8 Recoilless Rifle is an AP 6 armor-penetrating support weapon with damage second only to the
excellent for swiftly eliminating large, heavily-armored enemies.
It is capable of killing the majority of armored enemies such as
and Tanks in a single shot. Certain larger enemies, such as
and
, can survive the one shot if it does not strike a weakpoint.
The stratagem Hellpod contains both the Recoilless Rifle weapon and the ammunition backpack. The weapon cannot be reloaded without the backpack.
The weapon wielder can carry the backpack to perform a solo reload, and a teammate can either assist the wielder and/or carry a backpack of their own to perform a team reload.
One of the weapon's weaknesses is its stationary reload, requiring Helldivers to kneel in place for several seconds, leaving them vulnerable to enemy attacks. This can be mitigated in several ways:

The staged reload has four steps: opening the venturi nozzle, removing the expended shell, inserting the new shell, and closing the venturi nozzle. Helldivers can take advantage of this by interrupting the process when under pressure, and resuming it once safe, retaining reload progress up until the latest completed stage.
The reload animation can be cancelled to expedite the process once the HUD icon changes from red to white after the new shell is inserted.
Performing a team reload greatly reduces the reload time, but requires another Helldiver's assistance. The effective rate of fire while team reloading is approximately 38-40 round per minute.
Searching Minor Places of Interest for Ammo Boxes can help keep the weapon topped up without needing a Resupply.

The Recoilless Rifle generates significant backblast when fired. While this will only knock down Helldivers rather than injure or kill them, it can still be a significant danger if a live grenade or stratagem ball is dropped as a result.

s: The LAS-44 Nova is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Scope of Authority Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.
An Energy-Based Support Weapon, the Nova fires a burst of energy that can penetrate Anti tank I armor (despite it's game description of having heavy penetration) and inflict significant damage.

Rather than immediately firing the weapon when the trigger is pressed, holding it down begins a charging cycle that requires 1.6 seconds to complete. While aiming and/or charging the weapon, the wielder's movement speed is significantly reduced. If the trigger is released before charging is complete, all built-up charge is immediately dissipated and the weapon must start the process over. However, if the weapon is allowed to complete charging, it will launch a high-velocity energy projectile which is not affected by gravity. After firing, the weapon immediately overheats and cannot be fired again for three seconds, which is affected by weather modifiers. The weapon will cool down regardless of its wielding status, whether it is being actively held, it is being carried on the player's back, or lying on the ground.

The Nova is a long-range support weapon, boasting a powerful scope and armor-piercing rounds. Its high-damage rounds excel at dispatching medium-large sized enemies. The Nova acts as an intermediary option of the
and
As an Energy-Based weapon, the Nova has several unique quirks and advantages.
The Nova does not need to be reloaded, nor does it require an ammunition backpack, giving it effectively infinite ammo.
Its infinite ammo supply makes the Nova especially useful for Commando Missions.
The Nova's projectile travels at a similar speed to the Railgun and is not affected by gravity or damage falloff.
The Nova comes equipped with a 4x Combat Scope as standard with 25, 75, and 150 meter settings, allowing for easier target acquisition at long-range.
The Nova is best utilized against large, heavily armored targets with fatal weakpoints.
Many large enemies such as Hulks,
s, Tanks, and
s have weak points that can be destroyed in a single shot.
Automaton structures like Anti-Air Emplacements, Mortar Emplacements, Cannon Turrets and Bunker Turrets can be taken out with one shot to their weak spots.
Automaton Fabricators can be destroyed in three shots.
Due to its 1.6 second chargeup and 3 second cooldown time, the Nova is not ideal for killing several enemies at one time, though this can be mitigated with distant positioning.
A reliable Secondary or rapid-fire Primary Weapon is recommended to deal with enemies at close range. Secondaries like the
and
can quickly dispatch individual targets, while Primary Weapons like the
or
are effective options for several close-range enemies.
Drone backpacks like the
or
can also be useful, killing most small enemies before they can get too close.
Due to the Nova's nature as a laser weapon, the Nova has the potential to never run out of ammo, and is affected by the Intense Heat & Extreme Cold modifiers.
Changes in temperature will only result in changes to how quickly the Nova cools down after a shot is fired.

s: The Laser Cannon is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center (Engineering Bay subsection) for 4000 Requisition at Level 5.

Rather than using magazines of ammunition, the Laser Cannon builds up heat in its Internal Cooling Element while it is firing. If too much heat is built up in the ICE, it will burn out and render the weapon unable to fire until the heat sink is replaced via a reload. As long as it has not fully burnt out, the heat sink will slowly cool down automatically when not firing, even if a Primary or Secondary Weapon is currently being wielded; this effectively gives the weapon infinite ammo if it is fired judiciously.

From a nearly maximum heat ICE, the weapon will require 15 seconds to fully cool down under standard conditions. Additionally, the beam from the Laser Cannon is capable of igniting targets, setting them on fire if the beam has been focused on them for a period of time. A burning target will take damage over time to its main body, but only if its armor level is not greater than the penetration power of the Laser Cannon. Finally, when firing the Laser Cannon for the first time after a period of inactivity, it requires a short "warm-up" period where the weapon has to be charged before discharging its beam.
Because of its beam nature, the Laser Cannon is very easy to aim, since gravity does not affect its beam. This makes it particularly strong against highly mobile enemies like
s,
s and
s, as firing is as simple as placing the reticle on target and shooting.

When firing, the color of the refracting light on the target will help indicate whether or not damage is being dealt. Blue light indicates that no damage is being done, while orange lights indicate dealing damage.
It will emit a buzzing sound when its Internal Cooling Element reaches around 75% of its capacity as a warning that it is about to burn out.

Like other heat-based weapons, the fully overheated reload process is faster than when partially spent becuase the ICE ejects itself hands-free at the moment it burns out. If committing to a manual reload, Helldivers may want to burn the ICE out completely first instead of doing a slower "tactical" reload.
The Laser Cannon has a warmup period of 0.5 seconds before firing, it is advised that Helldivers try to bring the Laser Cannon out earlier and prime it before it is needed.
The Laser Cannon's beam nature, AP 4 armor penetration, potentially infinite ammo, and it’s great range gives it great flexibility.
Generally, it is best used to destroy medium armored enemies such as
s and
s, as it can easily punch through their armored areas and inflict full damage while also igniting them. Against Automatons, it is also capable of destroying Hulks and
quickly by focusing on their red eye units.
Most light enemies can be ignited by sweeping the beam across them in one to two passes, allowing it to efficiently deal with large groups.

Outside of a few exceptional enemies than can't be set on fire, quickly and repeatedly igniting larger enemies with short bursts allows for steady, sustained damage on them while still staying mobile.

Despite having low damage output for a support weapon, it can sustain this damage over time and also inflicts respectable durable damage from a considerable distance. Combined with its ease of aim, the Laser Cannon is capable of melting high durability weak points over time.

Its armor penetration allows the Laser Cannon to deal damage to certain secondary objective structures such as Anti-Air and Mortar Emplacements, as well as Shrieker Nests and Spore Spewers. This can be handy for destroying objective buildings without having to call down and wait for a Hellbomb.
The Laser Cannon can open shipping container doors and break fences, thanks to its 20 demo force.

s: The orange label on the side of the Laser Cannon reads: "CAUTION; LASER WEAPON SYSTEM; AVOID EXPOSING EYES, HEAD, OR BODY TO BEAM.; CLASS V LASER SE PRODUCT; 1500 MW 520/160 2600/800".
The all-uppercase labeling makes it ambiguous as to whether the Laser Cannon is designed as a 1.5-watt (1500 milliwatt) or 1.5 GW (1500 megawatt) weapon.

Given that 1.5-watt lasers can be used to engrave soft material, light matches, and pop balloons while 1.5-gigawatt lasers are potentially capable of instantly vaporizing organic material and explosively ablating other materials, it is more plausible that the label refers to megawatts.

However, as seen in-game, the Laser Cannon does not produce the extreme effects of sudden thermal discharge expected from gigajoule-level power. Considering the weapon's stats — heavy armor penetration, +8 °C per second into the heatsink which ejects at 100 °C, and ignition of targets after several seconds of sustained focus — its optical output is more likely around 1.5-megawatts rather than 1500, making the label misleading.
Comparing the

’s ballistic damage to the Laser Cannon’s damage values suggests the cannon delivers roughly 34 kW of energy to its target. This number reflects in-game damage scaling rather than the weapon’s apparent actual physical output and effects (which is closer to 1.5 megawatts, as explained earlier).

The “Class V” designation is loosely analogous to real-world laser classifications, in which lasers with outputs of 500 mW and above fall into the highest category: Class 4. Class V (or Class 5, as it would really be written) is an extension of that system, as Super Earth's technology has progressed past 21st-century laser tech to warrant extending it to better specify powerful lasers that are more common.

s: The backpack's energy recovery rate is 6% per second, and each teleport consumes 33%, meaning it is safe to teleport every 6 seconds. Energy is consumed after teleporting.
By holding the climb button, Helldivers will teleport 10 meters in the same direction they are moving.
The Orb on the backpack indicates its energy level and warp safety, additionally it will produce a noticeable amount of steam out the bottom back end while in cooldown.
If it is purple (>85% energy), warping is safe.
If it is orange (56% - 85% energy), warping will cause damage.
The Warp Pack will choose which limb will take damage in a random pattern, choosing between arms, legs and head. It can also damage the same limb on the next warp, even if it is already broken.
The Warp Pack will deal 35 damage if it hits either arm, 45 if it hits either leg, 10 if it hits the head, and light Helldivers on fire if it hits the chest.
Using Servo-Assisted or
allows a Helldiver's limbs to survive at least one warp before they break; Reinforced Epaulettes & Feet First can also prevent limb breaks caused by warping.
If it is red (<56% energy), warping will kill the Helldiver, regardless of any armor passives or other modifiers. The Warp Pack will be destroyed as well.
Warping can bypass terrain, buildings, enemies, and Bunker doors. Warping can also position Helldivers upwards or downwards a maximum of 5 meters.
Warping while diving/prone will allow Helldivers to bypass certain inaccessible areas, such as hard to access bunkers.
The most effective use of the Warp Pack is to quickly reposition themselves behind enemies.
This allows Helldivers to get a better target enemy weak spots or to avoid enemy attacks.
Warping can be used in mid-air to travel horizontally to travel across canyons and other gapped terrain.
Helldivers warping in mid-air will stay in mid-air. If there is no ground beneath the Helldivers feet at the destination they will fall, potentially taking damage.
Helldivers coming out of a warp cause a large explosion at the destination.
This explosion will kill most small/medium enemies (such as
s,
s, and
s) as well as other Helldivers.
The explosion has sufficient
to open Cargo Containers and chain-link fences.
Warping into most large enemies and friendly vehicles (such as the
), will result in Helldivers instantly dying. The Warp Pack will still deal its normal damage if this occurs.
This instant death can be prevented by Democracy Protects, causing Helldivers to take no damage.
A Warp Pack can be used while prone or crouched, but will not function when swimming or climbing.
Any chargeup weapon will keep its charge while warping. However, warping will interrupt all reloads, including weapons with stationary reloads such as the
or
If a weapon has a staged reload, warping will reset Helldivers to the last completed stage.
When in the passenger/gunner seat of a vehicle or emplacement, it is possible to use the Warp Pack as an alternative method of disembarking.
This cannot be done while driving/piloting a vehicle.
Warping from a passenger seat can be a safer alternative to exiting a moving FRV.
However, warping out of a

The LIFT-860 Hover Pack is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Borderline Justice Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

The Hover Pack activates when the user presses their Jump Pack input. It launches the user high into the air before slowly leveling out, maintaining the user's height for six seconds before deactivating. Before landing, the Hover Pack will briefly re-activate for up to four seconds to slow the user's fall to a safe velocity. It is not possible to deactivate the Hover Pack until the fuel has been expended. The Hover Pack will take at most 12 seconds to recharge before it can be used again, depending on how much fuel was spent to slow the user's fall.
While hovering, the user can slowly move around in the air in any horizontal direction. They can aim and fire their weapons, input and throw Stratagems, and use Stims.

A secondary function occurs when the user activates the Hover Pack while falling from any height. Rather than launching them into the air, the Hover Pack will begin to slow the user's descent until they land, while only using a small fraction of its fuel - being ready again shortly after landing. This cannot activate if the user is in a ragdoll state while falling.

If the Hover Pack is activated and then unequipped (voluntarily or not) in flight, it will continue to fly on its own. Without an operator to weigh it down, the Hover Pack's velocity is massively increased and will cover great distances before it runs out of fuel.

The Hover Pack provides fantastic vertical mobility. The amount of height it reaches grants a significant advantage over melee units. It can also be used to reach otherwise inaccessible areas such as mountains or rooftops.
Compared to the

, the Hover Pack grants more height, better control over the landing location, and is better suited for fighting while in mid-air. In exchange, users lose the ability to travel longer distances more quickly.
The Hover Pack can be used to negate fall damage from otherwise dangerous heights such as cliffs, if activated before touching the ground.
Aiming stability and recoil are significantly worse while airborne. It can be alleviated by remaining in place, but is difficult to control while moving.
Hovering does not make the user unreachable by enemies;

can jump high enough to hit a hovering Helldiver, and Automatons can knock users out of the sky with rockets. Being ragdolled while airborne can be fatal, as the Hover Pack will not be able to save the user from a hard landing.

As Automatons and Overseers are able to fire upwards with ease, it is inadvisable to use the Hover Pack against them in combat situations. Instead, it should be used by Helldivers to access otherwise inaccessible areas to use as cover, vantage points or an escape route.
If using a flamethrower-type weapon with the Hover Pack, avoid firing directly downward as the Helldiver's legs will be caught in the flames.
Catching on fire while using the Hover Pack may be survived with the timely use of a Stim and/or wearing the
Armor Passive.

The M-1000 Maxigun is unlocked on the 3rd page of the Python Commandos Premium Warbond for 110 Medals.

The M-1000 Maxigun boasts an extremely high rate of fire and an ammunition reserve of 1000 rounds. As a backpack belt-fed weapon, it has the unique feature that it does not need to be manually reloaded like other backpack-reliant support weapons; however, it cannot be fired without its ammunition backpack equipped. The M-1000 Maxigun is also the first support weapon that prevents Helldivers from moving to fire it. However, they can still rotate, elevate, and depress the weapon.

When the M-1000 Maxigun and its Ammunition Backpack are initially picked up, a roughly 1-second animation will play where the Helldiver connects the ammunition feed chute into the Support Weapon. This connection will remain unless the two parts are forcibly detached, after which it must be reconnected in order to fire again.
Due to the Maxigun's extremely high rate of fire and, by comparison, relatively mediocre capacity, it is recommended to stay near ammo boxes, a Resupply, or a Helldiver carrying a
The Maxigun continuously feeds ammunition from its backpack, which means an ally supplying ammunition via the B-1 Supply Pack can keep the Maxigun continuously firing.
Picking up an ammo box will restore 250 rounds directly to the backpack.
The Maxigun has a brief 0.5s spin-up period before it begins to fire.
This can be mitigated by spinning up while performing a dive. This also helps reduce recoil, due to the Helldiver now being prone.
The Maxigun has extremely high recoil, so aiming down sights or going prone is recommended to reduce recoil. Additionally, Helldivers can use recoil-reducing Armor Passives such as
or
The
passive significantly improves handling, allowing for extremely fast targeting. The passive also assists with minor recoil recovery and overall control.
It is impossible for Helldivers to move while firing the Maxigun, but they can still aim in any direction and transition between prone, crouching, and standing positions.
As the Maxigun leaves the Helldivers stationary during usage, it is advised to equip armor passives that reduce incoming damage like
, as well as prone to take cover. Not only does this reduce the size of the Helldivers' profile, but it also reduces the high recoil of the Maxigun.
The
or
can also be used to protect the user.
It takes exactly 40 seconds of sustained fire with a full backpack to empty.
The Maxigun excels at the destruction of many small to medium targets and delivering extremely high DPS on lightly armored weakpoints.
The Maxigun's bullets cannot reliably penetrate corpses, so it is advised to keep a reasonable distance when fighting large hordes of bugs.
Entering and exiting any FRV type, the
, any Exosuit, and any Emplacement stratagem will always make the Helldiver reattach the belt of the M-1000 Maxigun.
The following bug also occurs every time the Helldiver leans out of any FRV and the Bastion's passenger seats.

turret, which can be reloaded using a charge from the supply rack. The reloading mechanism is on the back-right and back-left of the vehicle, so it's not possible to reload it while inside the cab.
The turret will fire ~120 rounds before running out of ammo. When this happens, the turret will point straight up and will not target any nearby enemies until reloaded.
When no enemies are nearby, the turret will point upwards.
The turret can be reloaded as soon as it falls below 100% ammunition; this will still consume one supply charge.
The automated turret will target enemies regardless of whether the Supply FRV is being driven or not.

Helldivers are advised to consider when the automated turret should be reloaded, and should prioritize resupplying their own gear first.
The Supply FRV's charges can not be restocked by any means other than calling in a new Supply FRV.

Since the Supply FRV does not come equipped with a dedicated HMG, Helldivers are advised not to use the Supply FRV as an offensive vehicle, instead bringing individual Support Weapons to deal with larger enemies.
The large supply cache in the back creates blind-spots for passengers, preventing them from shooting enemies at certain angles.
According to AH support, the Supply FRV and HMG FRV both have the same base - the same handling, physics, etc.

Despite this, manual testing has shown minor differences. The Supply FRV has a marginally higher top speed and acceleration, while also being lighter. However, the difference is so small that it has almost no practical effect on gameplay.

The Stalwart has several advantages as compared to heavier options like the
or

For this reason, primary and secondary weapons with AP 3 or greater armor penetration pair well with the Stalwart.

bodies or legs,

The weapon's fire rate can be toggled between 700, 850, and 1,150 rounds per minute.
A lower fire rate can be utilized to conserve ammunition when targeting distant enemies or small weakpoints.
A higher fire rate maximizes damage output, best used when faced with crowds or large unarmored targets.
The Stalwart is one of the few support weapons equipped with an underbarrel flashlight, convenient for night missions or Hive World underground areas.

s: The Helldivers failed three times in acquiring this stratagem before unlocking it due to failing an mine efficacy review from Super Earth High Command.

26th of April 2024 - For the "Operation Legitimate Undertaking, Phase I: Citizen Rescue" Major Order, Helldivers were tasked to liberate two planets, Choohe and Penta, in order to unlock and utilize the MD-17 Anti-Tank Mines and

, respectively. Helldivers successfully liberated Penta, but made very little attempt in securing the path to Choohe. The Major Order did highlight the lack of visible supply lines, which hampered larger helldiver efforts, and supply lines were made visible in a later update.

10th of May 2024 - For the "Decommission Automatons for Mines" Major Order, Helldivers were tasked to decommission 2 billion Automatons in order to acquire the necessary materials to produce the MD-17 Anti-Tank Mines. Helldivers would fail again in unlocking the stratagem by not achieving the ordered amount. This subpar report delayed the production of the Anti-Tank Mines for the second time.

11th of June 2024 - For the "Rescue Children or Explosives" Major Order, Helldivers were tasked with liberating Marfark and Vernen Wells, with both planets containing valuable importance to Super Earth. Vernen Wells harbored civilian survivors who were sheltering in Super Citizen Anne's Hospital for Very Sick Children, with supplies dwindling; Intelligence discovered a large amounts of explosives stolen from Choohe were located on Marfark, and contained enough raw materials to produce the MD-17 Anti-Tank Mines. Due to the urgent situation for both planets, Helldivers would receive a reward for the first planet liberated (though High Command would float the idea that by liberating both planets, both rewards might be received).

Helldivers managed to liberate Vernen Wells first, rescuing the stranded civilians inside Super Citizen Anne's Hospital for Very Sick Children, including 4,311 children, but were unable to liberate Marfark in time, achieving only around 50% completion of the liberation process by the time the Major Order expired. As a result, Super Earth was not able to secure the necessary materials to produce the MD-17 Anti-Tank Mines, leading to the Helldivers once again failing to obtain the stratagem.

The Anti-Tank Mines were finally unlocked after Helldivers failed to kill 1,500,000,000 enemies for the "Mine Efficacy Review" Major Order for the Mine stratagems, proving they needed more weaponry to kill Super Earth's enemies.

The failure to obtain this stratagem is notable as the failure of the Helldivers includes the failure to protect civilians, the subpar reduction of Automaton forces, and the termination of civilian jobs in Super Earth's industrial centers. Nonetheless, the liberation of Vernen Wells and successful rescue of the civilians there coincided with a USD$4,311 donation to the Save the Children Fund from Arrowhead CCO Johan Pilestedt and was a much-needed moral victory for the Helldiver Corps.

s: The MGX-42 Bullet Storm is unlocked on Page #1 of the Exo Experts Premium Warbond for 75 Medals.
Due to its low cooldown, two uses per call-in, expendable nature, and large ammunition load, the Bullet Storm is extremely flexible as a support weapon.
The Bullet Storm boasts an extremely high fire rate of 1300rpm, comparatively low recoil, and an impressive 100 damage per shot, higher than its counterparts, the
and the
This makes it particularly effective against the Illuminate and Terminids, given the abundance of lightly armored, high health targets.

It is not especially effective against the Automatons due to their propensity to engage at range, their armor, and their small weakpoints that require precise aiming, something the Bullet Storm is not especially good at.

The high rate of fire means the Bullet Storm expends its 300 round capacity in ~14 seconds of continuous firing. It is recommended to only use sustained fire against groups of enemies and large unarmored targets to save ammunition.
The low recoil makes the Bullet Storm relatively accurate even in sustained fire or while moving, especially in first person view.
The Bullet Storm can be used as a supplement to a slower, Anti-Tank Support Weapon, being called down upon encountering hordes of targets, such as during a Bug Breach.
When calling down the Bullet Storm against hordes, "reloading" is as quick as picking up the second gun from the Hellpod.
If used in tandem with the
, Helldivers can call in 600 bullets and two anti-tank projectiles every 70 seconds, even without any Ship Upgrades.

The Bullet Storm has poor bullet drag and velocity for a machine gun, and no reticle or sight in first person view. It is less effective at longer range and difficult to aim precisely at individual targets and weakpoints.
The Bullet Storm can easily be aimed using its tracer bullets, but the weapon's ergonomics, though better than most machine guns, hamper the ability to adjust aim against distant targets.
In first person view, the Bullet Storm's muzzle flash can make it difficult to see distant enemies and bullet impacts.

The Bullet Storm’s quick cooldown means it is almost always available upon reinforcement of additional Helldivers. Even if a fresh Helldiver is called in far from their equipment, in a matter of seconds they can have another Bullet Storm at hand.
Because Bullet Storms arrive in pairs, they can be easily distributed to teammates who might need a support weapon.
The Bullet Storm’s quick cooldown also allows the Hellpod itself to be used as a weapon, dealing 2500 AP 10 damage upon impact.

s: The Commando's laser-guided function requires manual guiding via crosshair. This function can be turned off via the weapon wheel to dumb-fire mode for short-to-medium range engagements and the missile will behave like an unguided
rocket. You cannot save that setting, as you get a new launcher with each stratagem call down.

Prior to Patch 1.006.001, the Commando missiles would remember the last painted point of space and hipfired launcher missiles would automatically redirect. However this is no longer the case, and missiles will only guide while the laser pointed is actively being used and aimed.
Compared to the similarly disposable EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank stratagem:
The Commando has a roughly 71.42% longer cooldown (120s vs. 70s).
The Commando deals 45% less damage per shot (1,100 vs. 2,000) but deals 11% more total damage per support weapon (4,400 vs. 4,000).

Two missiles from the Commando (2,200 damage) will be able to deal with anything a single EAT-17 rocket (2,000 damage) can handle. Additionally, Cannon Turrets and Tank turrets have 2,100 HP, giving the Commando a major edge over the EAT-17 for these units.
The Commando's missiles have significantly slower velocity than other rockets.
The

However, they experience no drop and thus can be fired from extreme distances.
The Commando's rapid firing speed allows it to quickly respond to threats on the battlefield
It is possible to easily destroy Automaton Fabricators from a distance with 2 shots from a Commando, though firing directly into their vents will destroy them in one shot.
The Commando occupies an intermediate niche between weapons like the
and

This is most notable against Automaton heavy units, whose weakpoints still take substantial time and ammo to destroy with ballistic weapons.
It is also more appealing to destroy certain enemy parts or break armor, as the Commando can do this in one shot without wasting too much damage.

cannon turrets, Hulk legs, or the armor on

Orbital Precision Strike is unlocked by default upon completing training.
A basic but flexible and effective Stratagem, Orbital Precision Strike launches a single shot from the Super Destroyer at the targeted point, exploding on impact.

The explosion of the shell inflicts tremendous projectile damage, and is capable of instantly killing any non-heavy enemy within 4 meters of the impact point while also killing or greatly damaging anything within 12 meters. Additionally, if the shell itself impacts an enemy, it can kill anything smaller than a
or
The high demolition force of 50 from the explosion also allows this Stratagem to be used to destroy objective buildings, giving it utility beyond simply killing enemies.
With a low cooldown time that can be improved further with Ship Module upgrades, OPS can be available for regular use whenever the situation calls for it.
While the explosive radius of Orbital Precision Strike is respectably large, it is also quite limited due to other constraints on the Stratagem.

True to its name, OPS will attempt to exactly target the Stratagem ball's beacon. This means that the player must be precise with aiming their throw, as the Stratagem ball bouncing off of an errant surface can cause the strike to completely miss.

The Stratagem only impacts once at the target point, which makes it less useful when enemies are spread out over a wide area. As such, it cannot deal with large waves as effectively as wide-area Stratagem like

Be mindful of where the strike is occurring relative to the Super Destroyer's position. As the Super Destroyer is positioned at the edges of the mission map, OPS calldowns may come in at an angle and impact obstacles like cliffs, buildings, or trees.

Remember that there is a delay between the Stratagem ball landing and activating the calldown, and the shell impacting the target point. Take the shell's travel time into account when trying to strike moving targets, predict where they will be in 3-4 seconds and toss accordingly.
The heavy destructive power of the shell allows Orbital Precision Strike to kill most enemies and buildings close to the impact point.
In general, an unaware enemy patrol can be completely wiped out if an OPS can be called in directly on top of them, or at the least severely culled.
Beware that heavy enemies like
s,

s and Hulks will survive a strike if the shell does not directly impact them. As such, this Stratagem is not ideal for killing heavy targets from full health unless they can be rendered stationary (such as with the aid of a
or by maneuvering around them to bait them into performing attacks that lock them in place). Additionally,
s are protected by breakable armor that can easily absorb the majority of the damage from the shell even on a direct hit.
The
of OPS allows it to destroy almost any structure in a single strike. There are very few exceptions to this.

Certain objectives which require calling down a Hellbomb such as Detector Towers and Rogue Research Stations can be bypassed by using OPS instead. This can save time and ensure reliable destruction depending on the situation.
OPS is also very reliable for killing enemy spawners in a single shot, particularly Automaton Fabricators,
holes, and Illuminate Warp Ships even if their shields are up.

The only enemy structures that an Orbital Precision Strike cannot destroy are: Automaton Fuel Reserves, Automaton Air Base Control Towers, Automaton Gunship Facilities, Automaton Orbital Cannons and Illuminate Monoliths.

The Stratagem can be useful even when not used to kill enemies or destroy structures. Because of its low cooldown, it can be expended to destroy level geometry such as cargo containers in Minor Places of Interest or blow up walls/fences. This can be especially useful when fighting in urban terrain, as perimeter walls can be quickly destroyed to create an impromptu breach rather than walking along the wall trying to search for an opening.

The Orbital Walking Barrage hits the target point with a salvo of explosive shells, and then follows up with several additional salvos that "march" forward.
The shells fired by this Stratagem are the same as those used for
and SEAF Artillery's Explosive shells, making them among the strongest explosive ordnance that can be deployed.

A total of fifteen shells are fired by this Stratagem, in five three-shell salvos; with the More Guns Super Destroyer upgrade, six salvos are fired for a total of eighteen shells. Each shell in a salvo is separated by an interval of one second, followed by a three-second pause before the next salvo. Total barrage time is 27 seconds (32 seconds when upgraded).
Each salvo is separated by an interval of approximately 25 meters, meaning that the final salvo will land approximately 100 meters away from the first salvo (125 meters away when upgraded).

The marching direction of the Walking Barrage is the same as the throwing direction of the Stratagem ball. This means that the first salvo lands on the approximate location of the Stratagem ball, and then moves away from the player's original position.
The primary advantage of the Orbital Walking Barrage is that it moves forward, covering a large amount of terrain.

After the first two salvos, it is safe for players to move forward to the location of the impact point of the first salvo, to finish off any stragglers, engage enemies being bombarded by subsequent barrages, or to claim objectives. In particular, this allows players to actively move forward after 10-15 seconds instead of waiting for the full 27 seconds before they can act.

The wide area coverage of the barrage is useful for reaching faraway targets, as well as to inflict damage over a large enemy base, such as a Terminid Mega Nest or Automaton Fortress on the Super Helldive difficulty.

Beware that the Stratagem ball and beacon will remain at its original location for the duration of the barrage. So while it will keep track of the total duration of the barrage, it will not mark the location where the shells are falling.

The forward-moving nature of the Orbital Walking Barrage makes it a poor choice for defending ground, as the first two salvos may land on target but the subsequent salvos will land behind any approaching enemies. As such, it is not reliable for dealing with Bug Breaches and the like.

Be very judicious about when to deploy this Stratagem, as it has a very long cooldown. Try to reserve it for extremely tough enemy bases, or for reaching faraway enemy objective structures that are out of the way to save time.

The PLAS-45 Epoch is unlocked on the 1st page of the Control Group Premium Warbond for 75 Medals.

The Epoch holds 4 magazines by default, each containing 3 shots, which must be reloaded while stationary. In turn, it has AP 4 to AP 5 armor penetration and high explosion damage centered in a small area. Like the

, the Epoch must be charged before it can fire, risking the death of the user and destruction of the weapon if that charge is held for too long. The armor penetration only scales up to AP 5 armor penetration when overcharged; this state additionally grants the weapon +100% bonus projectile and +60% explosion damage.
The following are recognizable indicators to know the fully charged state of the weapon:
The charge meter that can be seen either under the sight in first-person or at the back of the gun in third-person. This meter enters the red zone when the gun is overcharged.
The muzzle flash that occurs only when the weapon reaches its overcharged state.
The rapid beeping noises that also occur to indicate to the Helldiver that the weapon is ready to fire.
The pins visible on the barrel of the weapon will retract into the barrel
Firing the fully-charged plasma bolt will also result in a visually larger explosion with a more powerful sound effect.
The explosion of the Epoch's overcharged projectile is largely cosmetic, as the actual damage radius is substantially smaller and is only marginally larger than the
or
As such, while the Epoch is capable of easily killing dense groups of
or
, the weapon's limited ammo, charge time, and relatively small blast radius makes it less than ideal for large crowds or spread out enemies.
The projectile the Epoch fires has a 0.6 second lifetime, meaning that it only has an approximate maximum range of 150m.
Unlike similar support weapons like the
or the
, the Epoch is severely impacted by enemy part
and

The Epoch's projectile does half as much durable damage as it does standard damage, meaning that the Epoch can lose up to a quarter of its damage when shooting at an enemy body part that is 100% durable.
Half of the Epoch's total damage is contained within its explosion, which means that enemies with high ExDR values like the
will receive significantly less damage than they otherwise would.
Conversely, enemies with body parts vulnerable to explosion damage will receive far more damage, as all of their parts caught in the blast will receive damage.
The Epoch has a 2-stage reload; ejecting the canister and loading a new one. One can animation cancel the reload the moment the HUD magazine shows as white/loaded.
In situations where you cannot afford to sit and fully reload your Epoch, a good method is to "reload" by first ejecting the canister, remove the threat at hand, then reload the Epoch somewhere safe.

The Epoch's uncharged plasma bolts only have a demolition force of 10. This demolition force increases to 30 when fully-charged, making it capable of destroying structures like Bug Holes, the vents of Automaton Fabricators, or Cargo Containers.

s: The RL-77 has two firing modes: Flak and Cluster. Its default mode is Flak.

Flak Mode uses a proximity fuse that detonates 0.2 s after the rocket detects a target or obstacle within 2 m. It has a 1.5 s lifetime fuse or maximum range of 375 m. The bomblets have random time fuses lasting no more than 0.7 s.
The minimum safe distance is ~30 m from the center of the explosion cluster in Flak mode.
The timed fuses of the bomblets mean it may not damage everything below if it disperses too high up. For example, if fired past a
main body, the
at its feet may survive some of the blasts.
Cluster Mode utilizes an impact fuse rocket with a 0.25 s lifetime and a maximum range of 62.5 m. The bomblets will detonate upon impact after dispersing.
The rocket's Cluster mode minimum safe distance varies by its altitude when its fuse expires. The higher one aims, the larger the area saturated by bomblets.

The maximum dispersion radius of a Cluster mode rocket on level ground is 60 meters if fired straight upwards. It should be noted that this does not disperse the bomblets sparsely enough to ensure safety for the Helldiver firing the rocket.

Cluster mode is ideal for uses in somewhat close quarters, such as urban environments, as the rocket can be fired past enemies to explode on surfaces behind them, neutralizing them without having the rocket prematurely detonate in close proximity. As an added bonus in urban environments, engagements will rarely occur beyond 62 meters, so unless a specific circumstance arises in which Flak mode is needed, Cluster mode will be just as devastating, without the greater risk portrayed by Flak mode.

The RL-77 Airburst is notorious for causing casualties to Helldivers and enemies alike due to its very wide area of effect. However, when used responsibly, it can be highly effective at clearing hordes or patrols of light and medium enemies with a single rocket.
Helldivers should account for travel time and projectile drop when aiming at distant enemies with Flak mode.
In terms of ballistics, the RL-77 projectile behaves identically to that of the

, and the two weapons share an identical sight. However, it is generally advised to aim slightly above the projected impact point with the RL-77; this way, the flak round can detonate above the target rather than in front of it.
Using Cluster as the "default" firemode can be helpful in preventing accidents. The lack of a proximity fuse will prevent premature detonations on enemies that the user does not intend to shoot.
However, the bomblets will only explode upon impact, meaning that they can fall further than intended and hit teammates.

The relatively short range of the Cluster mode can be used to the user's advantage. With the aid of enemy pings or the radar, the RL-77's rocket can be shot so that it detonates above or behind enemies.
This has the ability to kill enemy groups without needing line of sight of them, useful when fighting in Colonies or other low-vision environments.
With its high explosive damage, the RL-77 is capable of killing some heavier targets in a single shot.
This can be done by detonating the rocket next to or directly on a vulnerable AV 3 weakpoint.
can be effectively dispatched by switching to Cluster mode, and aiming the rocket to land under them. This will either outright kill them, or send them into a bleedout state.
Enemies like
or
, though technically vulnerable, have healthpools that are too large to effectively damage with the RL-77.
The RL-77 is highly effective against

, easily able to kill one or multiple with a single shot. This is due to their low protection more than offsetting their otherwise high HP. It is best to aim for their feet, or slightly in front of them, so they are hit with the greatest amount of clusters.
Like the
, the RL-77 has a backblast when fired, knocking down any unfortunate Helldivers standing behind the operator.
Like other backpack weapons, the RL-77 has a lengthy reload that can be alleviated by an assisting Helldiver.

The backpack on the assisting Helldiver can be obtrusive if firing in third-person, due to the rockets' length. Aiming down sights or using the "switch shoulder" keybind may make it easier to acquire targets.
It is possible to shorten the reload of the ABRL up to 0.8 seconds by animation cancelling via weapon swapping as soon as the weapon shows as loaded in the bottom left of the HUD.
The Flak mode is also triggered by friendly Civilians, SEAF Soldiers and both the
and Emancipator Exosuits.
The
and
do not trigger the Flak rounds.
Shooting the ABRL too close to the
(up to ~1x its height) will also cause the Flak round to explode. This used to occur to other sentries but has since been fixed.

s: The Railgun is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center for 10000 requisition at Level 20.
The Railgun can also be found at some Minor Places of Interest.
The Railgun fires projectiles using a charge-based mechanic, and primarily has two firing modes, Safe and Unsafe.

In Safe Mode, holding down the trigger builds up charge in the weapon and quickly readies a shot. While the charge is safely held at 60%, the player's movement is greatly reduced and releasing the trigger will immediately fire the projectile, dealing a high amount of damage. There is no inherent danger in holding a charge in Safe Mode besides the reduced movement speed, so the wielder may charge the weapon for as long as they desire.

In Unsafe Mode, holding down the trigger will overcharge the weapon, increasing the projectile's damage the longer the trigger is held. As with Safe Mode, movement speed is reduced for as long as charge is building up, and releasing the trigger immediately fires the weapon. Charging the weapon in Unsafe Mode can increase the additional damage dealt by up to 150%, causing the projectile to inflict up to 2.5 times the damage it would have in Safe Mode. When charged above 90%, which is after 2.5 seconds, the standard damage has been increased from 600 to 1500, same as the durable damage which increases from 225 up to 562.5.
If the charge meter reaches 100%, which is after 3 seconds, the weapon will explode and inflicting heavy explosive damage to the wielder.
The charge meter is visible on the weapon itself when aiming in first-person mode.
The Railgun is a high-damage low-fire-rate weapon that inflicts extreme amounts of damage per shot but is limited by its slow fire rate and the danger of self-destruction in Unsafe Mode.
With a total combat load of 21 rounds, it is important to avoid using it against weak and numerous enemies, instead targeting large, threatening targets.
Helldivers are advised to take caution when choosing to fire the Railgun, as their movement speed will become reduced, making them vulnerable to enemy attacks.
The Railgun must be reloaded after every single shot. Helldivers should immediately reload after firing to ensure it is always loaded.
Charging the Railgun for three seconds will cause it to explode, destroying the weapon and dealing fatal damage to Helldivers.
Wearing armor with the Fortified passive halves the damage of the weapon's self-destruct when overloading, rendering the explosion survivable.
The Railgun emits a constant sound while charging, increasing in pitch as it gets closer to full charge.
Additionally, there is a visible charging meter that will fill up from top to bottom and change in color from yellow, to orange, then red.
The Railgun is best utilized against large, heavily armored targets with fatal weakpoints.
Many larger enemies such as Hulks,
, and
have weak points that can be destroyed in a single shot with Unsafe Mode.
Automaton structures like the Anti-Air Emplacement, Mortar Emplacement and small Bunker Turrets can be taken out by a single overcharged shot.
The Railgun can take out Automaton Fabricators quietly, doing so in five fully charged shots.

A charged shot still fires a projectile without dealing explosive damage. The explosive damage listed in the weapon statistics refers to the explosion that occurs in the Helldiver's hands when the Railgun is overcharged.
Due to the high penetration of the Railgun, it is possible to take out the eye of the Hulk while shooting from behind it at a specific spot.
The Railgun, uniquely, does not lose velocity when it hits an enemy. This allows its projectile to take advantage of the overpenetration system and deal more damage to grouped-up enemies.

s: The S-11 Speargun is unlocked on the 2nd page of the Dust Devils Premium Warbond for 85 Medals.
The Speargun fires a projectile that can penetrate AV 5 armor before embedding itself and releasing a cloud of gas similar in strength to a
but with a smaller radius that grows over time.
The weapon is comparable to a
that has been set to Safe mode; however, a few quirks set it apart.
The Speargun fires instantly, no charge-up required. However, it has significantly fewer reserves, a longer reload time, and much higher projectile drag.
The spears can be shot at the ground to release gas and prevent the advancement of enemies much like G-4 Gas Grenades.
The projectile and explosion both have a demolition force of 30, allowing it to destroy spawners such as Bug Holes, Fabricators and Grounded Warp Ships as well as PoI containers and Lightning Spires.
A single spear has extreme stagger force and can interrupt heavy enemies like
from spewing or
during a charge. The gas will also confuse the Charger and make dealing with it easier.

but not
as Behemoths only have 50% to main on their rears, whereas the normal variants have 150%.
The gas released from the spears can force Rupture strain Terminids to surface themselves from a distance. They will also be blinded by the gas, making them much more manageable.
Much like the Railgun, a single spear can destroy a Hulk when shot directly at the eye.
If the user misses the eye, Hulks will frequently be stunned by the gas allowing easy access to their heat sink, or a second attempt at shooting their eye.

The Speargun excels at sealing Bug Holes compared to other options owing to the capability for the projectile to overpenetrate light to medium targets. In situations where a bug is emerging from the hole and could block other munitions from sealing it shut, the spear projectile can simply pass through the obstructed opening and detonate behind the enemy, sealing the hole on top of them.

s: To use the Ballistic Shield, the player must equip a weapon with the One-Handed trait, such as the
