Aiming the weapon will cause the player to raise the shield directly in front of themselves, granting forward coverage that protects most of the player's body.

When the shield is equipped, the weapon's sights are unusable and first-person aim is a view through the shield's viewport, requiring the player to aim using the weapon's laser pointer (if present) or otherwise eyeballing it.

Equipping or switching to a two-handed weapon, picking up a two-handed carriable object such as a SEAF Artillery shell, interacting with two-handed objectives such as the cranks on the Radar Station or E-710 Pumps, or picking up an objective that requires transport in the off-hand such as an SSSD Hard Drive, will collapse and stow the shield on the player's back.
The Ballistic Shield blocks projectiles at all times, including when stowed on the back or even left on the ground.
Crouch to minimize exposure to enemy fire. While prone, however, the shield is held nearly flat off to the side, severely limiting its effectiveness.
The in-game description is slightly misleading, as the shield will block any enemy fire, including the

flamethrowers, and the miniguns of a
The shield is capable of blocking the damage of some explosions if the player is in the outer radius of the explosion.
Explosive projectiles should be dodged entirely, for while the shield will technically block explosive projectiles, the explosion will still damage and ragdoll the player.
As it has health and armor, the Ballistic Shield can be eventually destroyed, at which point it will automatically drop to the ground, appearing warped and broken.
The Ballistic Shield cannot protect the wielder from fire or arc electricity.
While the Ballistic Shield does not protect the wielder from fire on the ground, it does protect the wielder from flamethrowers.
As of patch 1.002.101, the Ballistic Shield can now protect the user from melee attacks and, though undocumented, Terminid bile.
The shield is capable of absorbing melee blows that would otherwise instantly kill Helldivers like
and

The shield offers great protection against Illuminate enemies, foremost the

It is also capable of blocking a

The Directional Shield is unlocked on the 1st page of the Urban Legends Premium Warbond for 75 Medals.
The Directional Shield combines the properties of the
and
Functionally, the Directional Shield works the same as the Ballistic Shield in that it protects the wielder against attacks coming from the front, and requires wielding a One-Handed weapon.

Unlike the Ballistic Shield, the Directional Shield will only project a barrier when the weapon is being actively aimed. As such, the projection device offers no protection while being worn on the back and when not aiming the weapon.
While the Ballistic Shield protects against a mix of projectile and melee attacks, the Directional Shield can only protect against projectiles. This makes it nearly useless against the Terminids.
Like the Shield Generator Pack, the Directional Shield projects an energy barrier when active.
Because the Directional Shield is transparent, it offers a significantly better field of view in front of the wielder, especially when using first-person aiming.

The Directional Shield is also capable of recharging its energy, giving it more staying power than the Ballistic Shield. While a new Ballistic Shield must be called down when the currently wielded one is destroyed, the Directional Shield only needs to be called down once.
Like the Ballistic Shield, the Directional Shield requires wielding a One-Handed weapon in order to be able to brought to bear in front.
The selection of a strong One-Handed Primary Weapon offers the best way to utilize the Directional Shield. A Submachine Gun like the
or
offers rapid-fire capability, while the
grants considerable explosive firepower at the cost of fire rate.

While all Secondary Weapons can be combined with the Directional Shield, be mindful that melee weapons can be dangerous to use as enemies will fight back with their own melee attacks at point-blank range, and the Directional Shield cannot protect the wielder against them. As such, of the melee weapons the
is the safest option as its long range allows it to strike enemies before they can get close enough to respond.

One of the main characteristics of the Directional Shield is that it extends far to either side of the wielder, allowing them to protect teammates by standing next to them. Teammates standing next to the shield carrier are not restricted to using One-Handed weapons, and in fact can continue using their support weapons as normal.
As the Directional Shield relay (the physical part, not the energy shield) has a main health value, it can technically be destroyed, at which point Helldivers will no longer be able to use it.

The W.A.S.P. Launcher is unlocked at the Patriotic Administration Center for 12000 requisition at Level 20.
Similar to the

, the W.A.S.P. is incapable of being dumb-fired, and must acquire lock-on against targets in order to attack them. However, unlike the Spear, the acquisition time is very short and the weapon is capable of locking on to most enemy types rather than only buildings and elite enemies.

The weapon's default firing mode, Burst Mode, will fire up to seven missiles at the target. Quickly tapping the trigger will fire one missile, while holding down the trigger will continuously fire missiles until the weapon's magazine is depleted. The missiles will launch forward and in a random direction before re-orienting and homing in on the target.

The weapon's Artillery Mode consumes the entire magazine, simultaneously firing all remaining missiles as single projectile that flies upward and then strikes the target from a terminal angle, creating an overhead airburst explosion similar to the
. The more missiles there are in the magazine, the more powerful the strike.
The W.A.S.P. Launcher specializes in engaging medium-sized enemies at mid to very long ranges while also possessing the capability to inflict moderate damage to heavy targets.
With seven missiles per pod and five reserve pods carried in the backpack, the W.A.S.P. has a total combat load of 42 missiles.
An additional missile can be stored in the weapon, allowing for eight to be fired at once.
The W.A.S.P. is incapable of locking on to small enemies such as
s and
s.
The W.A.S.P. is capable of locking onto enemies 300m away.
Conversely, its missiles cannot properly track enemies that are too close to the user.
If the locked on enemies leave the 300m range the missiles will continue to track the enemy they are shot at, similar to the
. Use cases for this feature is minor and typically only applies to far Automaton
or fleeing Illuminate

The majority of the W.A.S.P.'s damage is concentrated within its explosion, with 3/4 of the total damage being AP 3 explosive damage. The physical projectiles are the only component that deals AP 6 damage.
As a result, the W.A.S.P. is particularly effective when fighting dense groups of medium enemies, killing several with only one or two missiles.
Smaller nearby enemies will also often be killed, depending on the positioning of enemies.

The random launch direction of the W.A.S.P.'s Burst Mode missiles makes the weapon significantly more inconsistent, as they may impact surrounding terrain or buildings while traveling to their target.
Against smaller, faster targets, the missiles may completely miss.
The W.A.S.P.'s relatively low AP 6 damage component, randomized launch angles, and inability to aim at weakpoints makes it a poor choice to fight heavy enemies with.
The user will typically be forced to expend a pod or more to dispatch such enemies if they cannot angle the rockets into a vulnerable area.
The weapon's Artillery Mode is best-suited for scenarios where one medium or large enemy is surrounded by a crowd of smaller chaff units.
However, the exact angle and position that the artillery missile decides to detonate at is highly variable.
The high ammo cost, low armor penetration, and general inconsistency make this a highly situational option.
Burst mode can do the same job if the user can spread out missiles to hit across an entire group.

s: The TD-110 Maelstrom was initially made accessible to Helldivers fighting on Marfark & Phact Bay for the duration of Major Order A3-9-6 as part of the Armored Eagle Campaign, later becoming available on all planets following its successful completion.
On October 4th, 2026, the TD-110 Maelstrom was awarded to all Helldivers who participated in any stage of the Armored Eagle Campaign.

The TD-110 Maelstrom is a Tank that is crewed by two Helldivers (a Driver, and Gunner) and can hold two Passengers: Driver - front-right side of the tank (facing frontally).

Able to use personal equipment, such as primaries, secondaries, support weapons, and stratagems. Also able to stim, and use throwables. Can use third person aiming, however, cannot aim down sights.

Voice communication is recommended, as it aids in effectively operating the vehicle.

The TD-110 Maelstrom possesses a set of dual AP 4 armor penetrating rotary guns. Each belt has 300 rounds, with 7 belts available, giving a of 2100 total rounds. This makes it highly effective against all but the heaviest of enemies allowing for a pair of competent operators to single-handedly deal with enemy reinforcements.
The high fire rate of the dual Gatling guns combined with identical rounds to the

give the main gun the highest damage per second of any weapon in the game, letting it shred through any enemy of low armor and durability. This means that gunners should sweep their fire across most enemies so as to avoid wasting ammunition on corpses.
When a belt is expended, it will need to be reloaded, similar to the cannon shells in the
tank. Reloading prematurely will discard any left over rounds in the belt.

The Maelstrom also has two AP 5 missile launchers on the back, each possessing 10 missiles for a total of 20 available. These missiles can either be launched rapidly, launching towards the gunner's crosshair at the point of launch, or manually guided to the target like the
The laser guidance system is placed on top of the rotary guns and are subject to the same arc/angle restrictions.
These missiles offer the Maelstrom significantly better burst damage compared to the
at the cost of worse sustained combat ability.
As they deal purely explosive damage, their performance against heavy enemies may be more inconsistent and generally less efficient.

While capable of dispatching dense enemy crowds with their modest blast radius, it is heavily recommended to conserve the missiles for harder targets, or for emergency use against unexpected close range heavy or tank units such as a Charger as the blast radius is more forgiving compared to a pointblank Bastion cannon shot.

The Maelstrom can destroy a Factory Strider with three missiles at any distance using laser guidance, provided all three impacts damage the torso and splash the same leg with their explosions. Aim at the selected Factory Strider, rapidly fire three missiles, then continue holding the fire button after the third shot to maintain laser guidance toward the desired impact point. The laser guides all missiles currently in flight, allowing the entire salvo to be directed onto the same target area.
The missiles fired by the launchers have a demo force of 40, allowing the missiles to destroy Automaton Fabricators, Bug Holes, and the city walls Colonies in a single missile to any part of them.
However, this is still not enough force to destroy structures such as Stratagem Jammers or Bulk Fabricators.
The driver can also activate a smokescreen around the vehicle. This should generally only be activated while retreating as it will block the gunner's vision.

The rotary cannons and missile guidance laser have a restrictive lateral aiming arc of approximately 40° (20° to the left and right of the resting position), requiring the driver to position the Maelstrom towards the target for the Gunner to fire at. Its front lights can be used to indicate the weapon's possible firing arc.
Both weapon systems are particularly sensitive to the movements of the tank, as both can require sustained tracking that can be easily thrown off by even small shifts.
The passenger positions can cover the Maelstrom's side and rear arcs; passengers should therefore focus fire on units to the Maelstrom's flanks.
The tank can also easily crush chaff units, even when turning, which is useful when surrounded or advancing.
Maelstrom crews should typically avoid trying to down

s while on the Automaton front as the missiles do not deal enough damage to destroy the fuselage quickly or ammo-efficiently. Destroying the thrusters also takes around 2 missiles each, which can be very costly over time for little benefit.
The Maelstrom may be difficult to drive in colony environments due to the tight streets and corners, as well as obstacles like parked cars for the driver.

The Maelstrom’s effectiveness in colony environments depends on crew coordination and positioning. Tight streets, corners, and obstacles can complicate maneuvering, but streets and alleyways also funnel enemies into predictable approaches that favor the twin rotary cannons’ limited traverse. A coordinated driver and gunner can exploit this by reversing along streets while keeping the frontal weapons aligned with pursuing enemies. The missiles’ vertical launch and U-turn flight path can also allow effective engagements at short range using this technique, while passengers in the side seats protect the tank’s flanks and rear as needed.
Most weapons perform well in the side gunner seats, with the exception of the
and the

when firing downwards, due to being held at the hip. Maxigun bullets can easily strike the tank but will not deal damage; the Belt-Fed Grenade Launcher's grenades will ricochet off and land in unpredictable locations.

The Bastion’s 120 mm main gun boasts twice the muzzle velocity of the

(on HEAT), and achieves AP 8 armor penetration—the second highest of any aimable stratagem, surpassed only by a direct hit from the
With a

of 40, the main gun can also destroy many enemy structures, except those that require a higher demo force, such as that provided by a Hellbomb. Examples of vulnerable structures include Shrieker Nests and Command Bunkers

The 120mm main gun also has significant explosion damage and radius, allowing it to effectively deal with groups of medium enemies. This is most relevant when facing enemy patrols of Automatons and Terminids, where slow kills can often mean reinforcements being called in.
The Bastion is loaded with 31 cannon shells and 2,000 rounds for the coaxial HMG, which is identical to its
in terms of fire rate, penetration, and damage while possessing little recoil.
The HMG's 2000-round capacity gives it the capability to continuously fire for extended periods, typically outlasting the strategem's long cooldown time before reaching empty.

The Main Cannon and HMG have a restrictive lateral aiming arc of approximately 40° (20° to the left and right of the resting position), requiring the driver to position the Bastion towards the target for the Gunner to fire at. s in one shot to the fuselage.
The Bastion performs poorly in colony environments due to the tight streets and corners, as well as several obstacles for the driver.
The Bastion has a listed top speed of 32 km/h, though it may achieve faster speeds driving at top speed downhill.
The Bastion can reach speeds of 18 km/h in reverse, making it slightly slower than a charging Charger or about the same walking speed as an Exo-Suit.
The Bastion can rotate its hull using its neutral steering at a speed of 4 km/h when in its drive gear, though it is often hindered by uneven terrain.
Drive gear has the highest overall top speed, and is the default gear when applying gas to the vehicle.
First gear has a lower top speed of 20 km/h, but much higher RPMs, meaning higher torque. This makes it better for climbing steep hills.
Second gear has the highest hull rotation speed in neutral steering, rotating the vehicle at up to 6 km/h.
The Bastion is significantly better at climbing steep hills or elevations in reverse as opposed to driving, due to the position of its engine and center of mass.

The Bastion appears to be roughly based off a mixture of a few real-life vehicles, those being the modern Swedish CV90120, a prototype light tank/ tank destroyer built as a technology demonstrator and for potential export, and the British FV3805, a prototype SPG from the Cold War that never entered service, and the Swedish Strv-103.

The Bastion's lack of a rotating turret is typical of a class of armored fighting vehicles known as tank destroyers. The casemate-mounted gun allows for larger, more powerful weaponry that would otherwise require a very large and heavy turret.

The Sterilizer is unlocked from the second page of the Chemical Agents Premium Warbond for 85 medal.
The TX-41 Sterilizer functions similarly to the
. It spews out caustic gas that slows and confuses enemies.
The Sterilizer has a range of 47 meters, measured in first person.
Gas expelled from the Sterilizer has a DPS and Durable DPS of 25, lingers for approximately 0.25 seconds in the air, and cannot stick to surfaces, unlike flames and napalm.
Unlike the Flamethrower, the Sterilizer doesn't have a firing delay due to the lack of a pilot light.

Enemies under the effect of the caustic gas are slowed by 25% and become confused, causing them to run into different directions while uncontrollably attacking anything nearby, potentially hitting their own allies.
The Sterilizer's canisters contain enough gas for roughly 16 seconds of continuous spraying.

With its low DPS and strong confusion effect, the Sterilizer is a purely crowd-controlling tool that is best used in short bursts - quickly spraying gas to inflict the effect, then engaging slowed and confused enemies with other weapons or stratagems.

The Sterilizer's spray is affected by wind, which can cause gas to drift away from the point of aim or even back toward the operator. Wind direction can be estimated by observing Helldiver capes, rainfall, or environment objects like foliage and flags.

Diving directly backwards while shooting the Sterilizer will deal damage to the Helldiver, due to their legs passing in front of the nozzle. This damage can be reduced by equipping armors with the Advanced Filtration passive.

Granted by their extensive augments, Cyborg Agitators have strength far beyond ordinary humans. Said units leverage their artifical vigor into inflicting grevious injuries onto human-sized adverseries, leaving them sprawled out on the ground in a daze.

Much like the zealous Radical, the Agitator is more than happy to engage in ultraviolent technology-powered martial arts against their hated foes. The end result for the foe is swift and highly lethal, often left as nothing more than a bloodied mess.

s: Agitators can be found on all difficulties on planets where the Cyborg Legion is present. Agitators can spawn from

Compared to Automatons, Agitators do not hesitate when detecting a Helldiver, and will immediately attack them. Agitators will often attempt to command nearby
s/other light humanoid Automatons,
s, and

s of any kind, granting them an increase in movement speed; this is signified by glowing yellow eyes on affected Automatons. Agitators can continue to command nearby Automatons as long as the commanding Agitator is alive. They prefer to fire their Plasma Charger cannon at range, utilizing Automatons as a frontline.

At range, Agitators will attack using their slow-firing Plasma Charger in two to seven round volleys, dealing moderate damage. They can also overcharge it, altering the projectile to deal higher damage and explode within a small radius; they will brace their cannon with their left arm when this is performed. After 20 shots, Agitators will cool down their Plasma Charger. When a Helldiver exits their line of sight, Agitators will throw a grenade at the Helldiver's last position.

During combat, Agitators can utilize cover, ducking behind waist-high objects and leaning out from corners to fire. Out of cover, they will occasionally sidestep to throw off a Helldiver's aim. Rarely, Agitators will perform a taunt.

At close range, Agitators utilize "techno-martial arts," which can be a frontal kick with either leg, a roundhouse kick with their left leg, and a swing or backhand strike using either of their upper limbs. These attacks will deal a moderate amount of damage and will knock a Helldiver off their feet. If a Helldiver is on the ground, Agitators can stomp on them.
The Agitator's command can notably enhance the lethality of

attacchi.descrizione: The ubiquitous weapon of the equally brutal Berserker unit. The Meatsaw befits its user by bringing weight of intimidation with obvious effectiveness, alongside promises of pain before death.
On account of their weight, most Devastator-sized units can simply crush structures, flora, and foes alike underfoot.

s: Berserkers can be first found on Difficulty 2 (Easy). They can spawn from Bot Drops, within patrols, and guarding Automaton Outposts and Objectives.
Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), they can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest.
On planets invaded by the Incineration CorpsIncineration Corps, the Berserker is absent.
Berserkers will simply path their way towards a Helldiver to get close enough to use their Meatsaws. If a Helldiver is on the ground or it is missing both of its arms, it will stomp on them.

While Berserker pose no threat outside of melee range, the true threat of Berserkers is that they often approach in swarms of three or more at a time, and can force Helldivers out of cover where they can be shot by the Berserkers' compatriots. Their meatsaws also inflict a significant amount of damage, being able to often maiming Helldivers with just one hit, and they can absorb an immense amount of ammo before being destroyed.
While Berserkers are much faster than

s, they are still slow enough that their movements can be anticipated. Helldivers can stay outside of reach by sprinting, diving away, or placing elevated terrain between themselves and the Berserker.
Their legs can be targeted to slow and destroy them before they can inflict fatal damage on their target.

Berserkers are protected by AV 2 armor on their upper torsos, which is also the only body part that possesses durability. This makes it the strongest part of the Berserker, and thus should be avoided with AP 2 armor-penetrating weaponry, and should be targeted with heavy machine guns like the
and
to quickly destroy them without wasting too much ammo.

The weakest parts of the Berserker are its AV 1 head and stomach. The head has the least amount of HP of all its body parts, but the Berserker's movements can make it a tricky target to hit. Its glowing stomach is the next weakest point, requiring more damage to destroy but is much larger and easier to hit.

Because Berserkers must get within melee range to be a threat, any weapon that can stagger or stun them is extremely valuable, as it can buy more time before they are able to attack. Alternatively, direct-fire weapons with high damage output can quickly destroy them even without precise aim.

Explosives are hit-and-miss against Berserkers. All of their body parts are explosive-immune, and their speed makes them difficult to pin down with fuse-timed grenades. However, due to their tendency to clump up with other Berserkers in an attempt to close within melee range, a single explosive can eliminate multiple Berserkers. As such, explosives should be an "all or nothing" proposition, as they can only damage the Berserker's main HP and require more raw damage to dispatch.

Devastator units are known to punch their foes. They often hit with enough force to crack helmets or even fully knock down Helldivers.
On account of their weight, most Devastator-sized units can simply crush structures, flora, and foes alike underfoot, clearing paths for lighter units to cross unimpeded.

s: Conflagration Devastators can be found on Difficulty 1 (Trivial) on planets invaded by the Incineration CorpsIncineration Corps. Conflagration Devastators can spawn from
, within patrols, guarding Automaton Outposts and Objectives, or from Bulk Fabricators.
Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), they can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest.
Like

, Conflagration Devastators will slowly but constantly push if a Helldiver is within their line of sight, firing their Conflagration Scattergun at a steady 40RPM fire rate, though can on occasion fire 2 shots at a more rapid 100RPM, quickly killing Helldivers who are not careful.
Conflagration Devastators can bash Helldivers with their shield if they're too close, knocking them down. They can also stomp on Helldivers if they are prone.
Conflagration Devastator

The incendiary shots from the Conflagration Devastator's Scattergun deal a significant amount of ballistic damage. Combined with its relatively fast fire rate, this Automaton is deadly at close range.
Though its scattergun damage is extremely high and can even one-shot Helldivers in Heavy armor, the Ballistic Shield is immune to its damage due to its AV 4 protection.
Helldivers should immediately go prone upon taking damage to minimize the burn effect, but should quickly reposition to avoid being caught at close range.
Unlike
s, Conflagration Devastators do not have a backpack, so Helldivers must pursue other means of destruction.
Explosives can stagger Conflagration Devastators, causing them to lower their shield and leaving themselves open, in addition to dealing some explosive damage.
Shooting their shield with explosive weaponry achieves the same effect.
Against the Incineration CorpsIncineration Corps, Helldivers can equip armor with the Inflammable and Acclimated armor passives to reduce their damage from fire.
Inflammable and Acclimated Helldivers should still be wary of the Conflagration Devastator's shotgun, as it will not reduce its ballistic damage.
Devastators
A significant number of weapons can destroy a Devastator with a single headshot, such as the
and
, so precision is highly rewarded; this is especially so with the

and their Incineration CorpsIncineration Corps variants. Their stomach and pelvis are still vulnerable to any weapon, but it is usually infeasible for Helldivers to aim at due to the ballistic shield.

As is the case with all Devastator variants, both the exposed arm and the gun of the Conflagration Devastator are AV 2 and AV 1 respectively, meaning several shots to either area will completely disarm the Conflagration Devastator, making follow-up shots significantly easier to land as the now disarmed Conflagration Devastator attempts to approach the Helldiver. This provides an alternative means of dispatching the Conflagration Devastator if the head weakspot is unavailable.
In Conflagration Devastator's case, this method is preferable, as the head weak spot often ends up covered by the shield and the gun model is significantly larger than other Devastator variants.

Devastator-sized units are known to punch their foes. They often hit with enough force to crack helmets or even fully knock down Helldivers.

Heavy Devastators will slowly but constantly push if a Helldiver is within their line of sight, firing a deadly volley from their Fusion Repeater for three seconds, before cooling down for two seconds.
Heavy Devastators can bash Helldivers with their shield if they're too close, knocking them down. They can also stomp on Helldivers if they are prone.
Heavy Devastator
The Heavy Devastator can be a nuisance even at a significant range, as their Repeater volleys can potentially hit and cause Helldivers to flinch multiple times.
This can most notably prevent Helldivers from stimming, making them extremely dangerous when Helldivers are surrounded by various Automatons.
They are also able to fire through their shields if walking towards Helldivers at a certain angle, meaning that staying on their left side does not guarantee safety.
Multiple Heavy Devastators can easily cover each others' Fusion Repeater cooldowns, leading to a nigh-endless amount of projectiles being fired.

Heavy Devastators are vulnerable to flanking, especially with the assistance of another Helldiver. Their backpack can be damaged by any weapon, and destroying it will also destroy the Heavy Devastator.
Explosives can stagger Heavy Devastators, causing them to lower their shield and leaving themselves open, in addition to dealing some explosive damage.
Shooting their shield with explosive weaponry achieves the same effect.
Shooting the Heavy Devastator's shield with ballistic weaponry will deal no damage to the Heavy Devastator.
Devastators
A significant number of weapons can destroy a Devastator with a single headshot, such as the
and

, so precision is highly rewarded; this is especially so with the Heavy Devastator and its Incineration CorpsIncineration Corps variants. Their stomach and pelvis is still vulnerable to any weapon, but it is usually infeasible for Helldivers to aim at due to the ballistic shield.

As is the case with all Devastator variants, both the exposed arm and the gun of the Heavy Devastator are AV 2 and AV 1 respectively, meaning several shots to either area will completely disarm the Devastator, making follow-up shots significantly easier to land as the now disarmed Heavy Devastator attempts to approach the Helldiver. This provides an alternative means of dispatching the Devastator if the head weakspot is unavailable.
In Heavy Devastator's case, this method is preferable, as the head weak spot often ends up covered by the shield and the gun model is significantly larger than other Devastator variants.

s: Jet Brigade Devastators can first be found on Difficulty 2 (Easy) on planets invaded by the Jet Brigade. They can be spawned from Bot drops and within patrols.

can spawn four Jet Brigade Devastators from its undercarriage.

Like regular
s, Jet Brigade Devastators are able to punch Helldivers if they're too close, knocking them down. They can also stomp on them if they are prone.

In the case that there is a large amount of distance between a Jet Brigade Devastator and the Helldiver it is targeting, they will use their jump pack to rapidly close the distance. Their jump pack can explode if damaged, significantly damaging and burning themselves and nearby AutomatonAutomatons or Helldivers.

Jet Brigade Devastators can cross large areas and quickly get into ranges where their weapons are far deadlier. They will prioritize getting into close quarters at all costs, limiting the player's ability to eliminate them at long range.

The jetpack of the Jet Brigade Devastator is more vulnerable than the Devastator itself, exploding and igniting enemies, itself, and potentially the player upon destruction. The jetpack will detonate posthumously if enough damage reaches the jetpack through the Devastator's chest or stomach.
Weapons such as the

can be used to detonate the jump pack from afar, dealing area damage around the Devastator and disabling its jump ability.

Jet Brigade Devastators have an alternate color palette with considerably fewer red accents than standard Automaton colors. Notably, their heads are plain black with stark white eyes.
Jet Brigade Devastators are referred to as 'Devastators' by the game, lacking a unique name.

attacchi.descrizione: This oversized energy shotgun fires a spray of bolts that are considerably more powerful than standard Automaton Fusion Weapons. They are more than capable of tearing a Helldiver into pieces.
Used exclusively by Radicals. These grenades make up for their non-lethality with their tactical usage, concealing Radicals and their robotic allies as they close in.

Like all Cyborgs, the Radical has their wrist and hands replaced with cybernetic counterparts. Such limbs allow them to land severe blows that can leave enemies sprawled on the floor, at the mercy of the Radical's other weapons.

The Radical swiftly delivers what its society calls "techno-martial arts", a highly agile and equally violent form of combat that takes advantage of their greatly superior strength. Most human foes stand little chance against such a flurry of metallic blows.

s: Radicals can be found on all difficulties on planets where the Cyborg Legion is present. Radicals can spawn from
, within patrols, and guarding Automaton Outposts and Objectives.

Compared to Automatons, Radicals do not hesitate when detecting a Helldiver, and will immediately attack them. Before attacking, Radicals will yell and will immediately throw a smoke grenade between them and a Helldiver, sprinting towards them while attempting to be concealed; their sprint speed can keep up with a sprinting Helldiver, even in light armor. Radicals can throw another smoke grenade about every 30 seconds to conceal and continue their pursuit. Occasionally during combat, Radicals can perform a backstep.

At close range (15m), Radicals will fire their Scattergun while approaching or chasing after a Helldiver. Radicals will often close the distance to perform techno-martial arts, which can be a frontal kick with either leg, a flying right knee strike, a roundhouse kick with their left leg, and a swing or backhand strike using either of their upper limbs. These attacks will deal a moderate amount of damage and will knock a Helldiver off their feet. If a Helldiver is on the ground, Radicals can stomp on them, or use their Scattergun to execute them.
Radicals have been seen destroying
strategems with their kicking attack, even while a Helldiver is nearby enough to fire at.
The Radical's head is vulnerable to high-damage weapons such as the
, and
, killing a Radical in one shot.
The Radical's main body has a large amount of health, but multiple parts can be hit by explosions.

The Radical tends to hyperfocus on closing the gap between it and the Helldiver it chose to pursue. Helldivers can dive out of the way of a Radical attempting to use its techno-martial arts, as Radicals will be vulnerable while finishing their melee attacks.
Radicals cannot ragdoll Helldivers using the
armor passive.

The smoke grenade thrown by the Radical can serve as a valuable warning that one is approaching. Note the direction from which an unexpected smoke grenade was thrown and prepare for the arrival of the Radical that threw it.
Keep in mind that the Radical’s smoke grenade also hinders the view of other Automatons, and functions very similarly to the Helldivers very own
Radicals may also use their smoke grenades against sentry stratagems, blinding them and allowing the Radicals to close the distance and destroy them uncontested.
Sometimes when killed, Radicals will raise their left fist over their head in a final act of defiance. They will also twist the dial on their mechanical heart when their health is low.
The Radical is one of three enemies in the game to have a single part with a higher health value than its main health, that being its torso. This is likely a bug.
Some of the Cyborgs are female, having entirely different voice lines and a slightly different physical appearance (longer hair, chest coverings)

attacchi.descrizione: One of the largest standard Fusion weapons in the Automaton arsenal. The Battle Cannon's explosive shots are such that entire squads of infantry may be annihilated and armoured vehicles are left crippled. Mounted on Annihilator-class Heavy Tanks.

Annihilator-class Tanks also have a co-axial weapon in the form of the Fusion Cycler. This modified Fusion Repeater is capable of firing even faster, perfect for either suppressing or cutting down infantry.
This Heavy Fusion Repeater benefits being connected to the Tanks powerplant to output a far longer burst of sustained fire. Its limited traverse mount limits its flexibility in combat.

Between its massive powerplant and volatile fusion battery load it uses to power its weapons, the Annihilator Heavy Tank is particularly volatile when finally knocked out. This culminates into a catastrophic explosion.

s: Annihilator Tanks first appear on Difficulty 3 (Medium) with a low spawning chance, where it may spawn in specific medium-to-large Automaton Outposts.

When they begin appearing normally starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), they can spawn from Bot Drops, within patrols, guarding Automaton Outposts, Fortresses, and Minor Places of Interest. They may also occasionally be found patrolling the map on their own.
Annihilator Tanks share a spawn chance with
, but starting on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission), they are both occasionally replaced by

When encountered outside of a Bot Drop, Annihilator Tanks can be found still or moving with patrols. When it notices a Helldiver, it will fire any of its armaments if a Helldiver is in its line of sight.

Its coaxial Fusion Cycler has a high fire rate but lower damage, while its hull Heavy Fusion Repeater has a slower fire rate but higher damage. Its Fusion Battle Cannon will flash a red light before firing two seconds later, before reloading for about six seconds.

Destroying its tracks will render it immobile. Destroying its back engine or turret will disable the Annihilator Tank, followed by it exploding. Significant amounts of damage will immediately cause it to explode.
Annihilator Tank
The Annihilator Tank is deadly if approached from the front, but is vulnerable at close range. Helldivers are advised to approach from its rear as its turret has a slow rotation speed.
Helldivers can also run around the Tank's armaments to avoid them, and can take advantage of the slow rotation speed of the turret to damage its vents.
The Annihilator Tank cannot harm Helldivers if you climb on top of its turret. However, direct contact of their tracks will cause severe and constant damage to a Helldiver.

The coaxial fusion repeater on the Annihilator Tank's turret appears as a "Fusion Repeater" when pinged.
Despite the fact that it can be pinged it cannot be destroyed.
During early development, the Annihilator Tank's design had a much more World War II era aesthetic, resembling a fusion of the Japanese Type 5 Chi-Ri medium tank and the German Tiger heavy tank.
It also bears a resembles to the Soviet Union's Rhino Heavy Tank from Command & Conquer: Red Alert 2 and Yuri's Revenge.
According to very early concept art by Tore Wesolowski, the Annihilator tank was initially conceived as a hexapedal walker and was much larger in size.

attacchi.descrizione: A Heavy Fusion Repeater modified to sustain a much longer salvo. The Heavy Fusion Cycler allows the Gunship to lay down a withering hail of fire. Accompanied by improved targeting packages to compensate for firing on the move.

Augmenting the Gunships arsenal are 2 Rocket Racks loaded with standard HEAT munitions. Such dual-purpose munitions are primarily an anti-infantry weapon, blasting apart entire squads, but they are also effective at cracking open vehicles.
attacchi.effetti: Anti-Vehicle / (Ballistic Damage Only) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion)

attacchi.descrizione: Being multiple tons of steel, ammunition and fuel, even a plummeting Gunship is equally dangerous to its targets as if it was still airborne, slamming the ground with great force and burying those too slow to escape the burning wreckage.

Downed gunships additionally crash onto terra firma with such force they break into multiple parts. In particular, the Engine Pods break off with considerable force, crushing or slamming into any unfortunate being in the way.

Even still-burning, crashed Gunships are a ticking time bomb before said flames ignite either unburned fuel or undetonated ammunition loads. Such explosions are both devastating to those nearby and supposedly spectacular who (safely) witness it.

s: Gunships spawn from Gunship Facilities on Difficulty 5 (Hard) and above. Gunship Facilities will begin spawning Gunships when Helldivers are within 150m from it, spawning up to two at a time, with a maximum of four per tower.
They may also spawn as patrols in groups of two to four if the Gunship Patrols operation modifier is active.

Upon spawning from a Gunship Facility, the Gunship will search for Helldivers in its immediate vicinity. If it's within patrols, it will fly across the map in a straight line. Any Helldivers that alert one Gunship within a patrol will alert the rest.

Upon locating a Helldiver, it will begin hovering over them from a distance, firing its Heavy Fusion Cycler. It will occasionally fire a six rocket salvo, up to four times. After exhausting its rockets, it will begin firing its Heavy Fusion Cycler only for up to eight seconds, varying in length based on the Gunship's line of sight to a Helldiver. Its Heavy Fusion Cycler has a one second cooldown between bursts.
When a Helldiver deals a lethal blow, the Gunship will crash land, before violently exploding. The Gunship itself can crush Helldivers during its crash landing.

Gunships are dangerous enemies, as unlike other AutomatonAutomatons, they are fast and difficult to hit. They also stay far away from Helldivers and are heavily armored, requiring substantial and accurate firepower to shoot down. In most situations, they should receive immediate targeting priority due to the threat they pose.

Gunships tend to strafe around any cover that Helldivers may be using to shoot at them from more vulnerable angles. This can leave Helldivers vulnerable to other Automatons as they reposition themselves.
Gunships are also armed with rockets that can inflict tremendous stagger and knock Helldivers out from behind cover.

Gunships will always fire directly at Helldivers with their rockets, or lead them if they are moving. When a rocket barrage is incoming, Helldivers should either immediately move away or quickly change their running direction.
Destroying any component of a Gunship will immediately bring it down. For this reason, Helldivers should focus on an individual part and not indiscriminately fire at it.
The main fuselage is more armored and is fully durable, on top of being explosive-immune, so it can be harmed only by direct projectiles that inflict high durability damage.

The weakest parts of a Gunship are its thrusters with less HP and durability. The rear thrusters are slightly less durable than the forward thrusters, but as Gunships tend to be constantly facing Helldivers, the rear thrusters end up being more difficult for Helldivers to hit.
Certain AP 3 armor penetrating Primary Weapons such as the
and the
can quickly take down Gunships, requiring nine and two fully-charged shots respectively to a thruster.
Support Weapons, such as the
and
, can take down a Gunship with two shots to a single thruster. Notably, the
is capable of shooting down a Gunship with one fully-charged unsafe shot to any of its thrusters, or two to its fuselage.
The
is also a good choice, as it can bring down a Gunship fairly quickly without the need to finely aim given the beam.
The
needs to put at least eight shots into a single thruster to bring down a Gunship. This can be difficult for Helldivers due to the Heavy Machine Gun's recoil and handling.
The

high fire rate can shoot down Gunships with raw damage to their fuselages if needed. Its emplaced nature also means that it is well-suited for Helldivers to call down next to a Gunship Facility, destroying Gunships as they spawn. Helldivers can also place them in preparation of an incoming Gunship Patrol to the same effect.
Any anti-tank weapon is capable of destroying a Gunship in one shot, regardless of where it hits. The

is capable of locking on and firing, requiring minimal effort from a Helldiver. However, it can be considered overkill for a weapon that can only carry four missiles at a time. A better alternative is the

which can lock on to a gunship and destroy it with either a single lucky hit on a thruster or 2 to the fuselage and can destroy up to 4 gunships if the last missile hits a thruster before needing to reload. The
is theoretically capable of shooting down four Gunships in rapid succession, but is the most difficult to aim due to the slow speed of its rockets.

Activating a SEAF SAM Site provides an easy and reliable way of taking down Gunships. Any that come within range of the site will be automatically fired at and shot down, provided that level geometry, like cliffs, do not get in the way.
They were quietly introduced to the game on April 2nd, 2024 in addition to the
during Phase III of Operation Swift Disassembly.

This Rotary Munition Launcher fires the common HEAT rocket-propelled grenades, albeit now capable of unloading salvos of said munitions at unprecedented rates. Commonly mounted on Bruiser-class Hulks.

attacchi.descrizione: Hulk units are able to use their immense bulk to clear difficult terrain, obstacles (natural or human-made), as well as the occasional unfortunate with ease. Often also clears paths of dangers for lighter units during patrols as a result.

Layering the Hulk units back are 9 massive cooling vents, designed to ensure the Hulk does not overheat during combat. Rupturing these often results in a violent blast that severely injures all those nearby.
The massive reactor that powers the Hulk is as volatile as it is powerful. Should the Hulk fall in combat, the Reactor goes critical before finally erupting.

s: Hulk Bruisers can be first found on Difficulty 4 (Challenging). Hulk Bruisers can spawn from Bot Drops, within patrols, guarding Automaton Outposts, Objectives, and Minor Places of Interest, or from Bulk Fabricators.
If a planet is invaded by the Jet Brigade Jet Brigade,
will be equipped with a jump pack.
Hulk Bruisers do not appear on planets invaded by the Incineration Corps Incineration Corps, and are instead replaced by

Upon noticing a Helldiver, Hulk Bruisers will either fire their Fusion Autocannon or Rotary Launcher. The Fusion Autocannon fires a 20 round volley and the Rotary Launcher fires a seven rocket salvo. They will fire from a distance if a Helldiver is in their line of sight. Hulk Bruisers can raise and slam one of their arms if a Helldiver gets too close to them. If they are missing their arms, Hulk Bruisers can perform a stomp with their leg.
Hulks
Heavily armed and armored, Hulks are powerful enemies that demand special attention due to their durability and heavy weapons payload, as they are capable of killing Helldivers in short order.
Hulks are covered in AV 4 armor, but they do have two weak spots: the glowing heat sink on their backs which are AV 1, and their Head, which only has 250 health and will kill a Hulk if destroyed.

A Hulks vents can be damaged by any weapon, but are rather durable. It is advised to use higher-damage Support Weapon to more easily destroy the vents. Destroying its vents will cause the Hulk to go into a bleedout state, where they can be seen hobbling and flailing its weapons.

The Hulk's slow movement speed make them particularly vulnerable to dedicated anti-tank weapons such as the

Due to their poor mobility, Hulks can also be easily destroyed by most offensive explosive stratagems such as the

A single
will inflict enough damage to destroy a Hulk no matter where on its body it is placed.
While more durable than its weak spots, the Hulk's limbs can often be valid targets for destruction depending on the situation.
The Hulk's arm joints can be shot and destroyed, causing them to drop that arm's respective weapon. Once both arms are destroyed, Hulks attempt to stomp on Helldivers instead.
Shooting an Hulk's arm with a
will kill the Hulk instantly. This will not happen with the
The Hulk's legs can also be shot and destroyed; destroying one leg cripples its movement, and destroying both legs will kill the Hulk.
The Hulk's legs are often much more convenient targets than its head or heat sinks. Destroying a leg will stagger it for several seconds and significantly slow its movement speed.
The Hulk appears to be inspired by various Imperial Dreadnoughts used by Space Marines in Warhammer 40,000.
Oddly, Hulk Bruisers fire their rockets out of what appears to be the Hulk Scorcher's flamethrower.

Hulk Bruisers after patch 1.001.100 received an energy cannon, but were reverted back to a rocket launcher in the following patch 1.001.104. According to the patch notes, a Helldiver by the name of "John Helldiver" was responsible for sabotaging their production.

"John Helldiver" is a popular name in the Helldivers community originating from the John Darksoul meme, which popularized naming protagonists as "John (Game Series Name)." The same patch notes also references the opening quote of the A-Team television series.

Hulk Firebombers will sprint towards Helldivers, firing two White Phosphorus Shells, once every two seconds; these shells will leave lingering fire where it lands. It will then pause for five seconds before firing two more Shells again. Hulk Firebombers will often aim their Rotary Launcher up into the air, allowing the Phosphorus Shells to arc over cover and terrain.
At 25m and closer, Hulk Firebombers will use their Heavy Flamethrower; they can also use their Heavy Flamer right after firing their Rotary Launcher if Helldivers are within range.
If they are missing their arms, Hulk Firebombers can perform a stomp with their leg.
Hulk Firebomber
It is highly recommended for Helldivers to move opposite of where they were initially running after a Hulk Firebomber fires its shells to avoid them.
Due to this, Firebombers are extremely dangerous within groups of Automatons, as they can significantly disrupt a Helldiver's movement, or can lead to their deaths.
A direct hit from a Phosphorus Shell can instantly kill Helldivers. It can also trip Helldivers and cause them to burn to death within the lingering fire.
Against the Incineration Corps, Helldivers can equip armor with the Inflammable and Acclimated armor passives to reduce their damage from fire.
If the Hulk Firebomber is within range to use its Heavy Flamethrower it will stop using its Rotary Launcher entirely, making it relatively safer to deal with up close with
or other means if Helldivers dive through the flames.
The Hulk Firebomber also has a different melee attack where it does a backhand with its Heavy Flamethrower. This attack is slower compared to other Hulks and is easier to dodge.

Jet Brigade Bruiser Hulks are essentially unchanged from their standard counterparts, but are equipped with a large jump-pack that covers their rear vent. The jetpack is covered in AP 3 armor.

When initially detected, Jet Brigade Bruiser Hulks at medium to long range will use their jump-pack to close the distance to Helldivers, firing either its Fusion Autocannon or Rotary Launcher in an attempt to blast its foe. When a Helldiver exits their range, they will reengage by using their jump-pack.
Jet Brigade Hulk Specific

Destroying the jump-pack will instantly kill the hulk instead of causing it to bleed out, as well as exploding and damaging nearby enemies. It may be preferable to target this jump-pack to turn the Hulk into an improvised explosive against other Automatons.

As the jetpack is not immune to explosion damage, multiple sources of damage that would otherwise struggle to kill a Hulk from the front can successfully destroy the jetpack from the front due to their large explosion radius.

The upper vents of the Hulk's jetpack also stick out atop the front profile of the Hulk and can be targeted with any weapon of Armor Penetration AP 3 or above to these spots, though targeting them may prove tricky, particularly when shooting from a lower elevation.

The jetpack armor completely covers the unarmored vents found on standard Hulks. Therefore, on Jet Brigade missions it is advised to bring at least one weapon of Armor Penetration AP 3 or above to have a way to deal with them.

On planets invaded by the Cyborg LegionCyborgs, the Reinforced Scout Strider is absent and is replaced by
and

Reinforced Scout Striders will quickly approach Helldivers once alerted to their presence. It will fire its heavy fusion repeater three times before cooling down for four seconds. It will also occasionally fire one of its four rockets, usually after being alerted to a Helldiver's presence; before firing a rocket, it will briefly remain still, with the prepared rocket releasing exhaust before it is fired.
The Reinforced Scout Strider can stomp on a Helldiver if they get too close.

Without its pilot as a weakpoint, the Reinforced Scout Strider is harder to kill than its open-backed counterpart. However, it is still very vulnerable to attacks on its AV 2 armored rockets, which will instantly kill the Strider upon detonation. (This is currently bugged and won't kill the strider, but will greatly weaken the legs).
These rockets have both the lowest amount of health of any critical body part as well as being 0%
. This means that the rockets should be the primary target for the majority of weapons when facing this automaton.
The waist should also be considered a target for helldivers possessing AP 3 armor penetrating weaponry due to its large size, moderate health, and lack of
. This is a good option for Helldivers equipped with primary weapons such as the
or
that can take out the waist quickly without having to aim at the smaller rockets.

Even with all of the rockets expended, AP 2 penetrating weaponry can still deal with the Reinforced Scout Strider, although slower than weapons with more penetrative power. This is due to the AV 2 armored legs having more health than the waist while possessing 75%
Offensively, the Reinforced Strider is a much larger threat than its regular counterpart due to the side rockets. These will instantly kill any diver hit by one, with the sole exception of heavy
armor unless the Helldiver is prone. Near misses are almost as deadly due to the 9-meter shockwave carrying a push force of 100. This will send any helldiver flying off at high speeds (even with the
armor passive) to slam into terrain for often fatal damage.
Helldivers bringing vehicles should take extra care of the rockets due to their extremely high
making them do high damage to these vehicles.

The rocket launches are telegraphed by the strider standing still and the combustion of the end of the rocket being launched. These rockets aren't very fast and can be easily avoided when fired from long distances away. At closer ranges, a helldiver should dive out of the way as soon as they see the rocket launch. The additional explosive resistance of going prone will be the only chance of survival.
Given that its
pilot is sealed inside, there is no risk of being ambushed after destroying the Strider.
The Reinforced Scout Strider was first revealed in the Escalation of Freedom Announcement Trailer on July 23rd, 2024, and began appearing in-game on the update's release on August 6th, 2024.

The Reinforced Scout Strider resembles the AT-ST Walker from Star Wars. Most versions of the AT-STs seen in Star Wars related video games come with extra armaments, such as missile launchers on their sides.

Destroying its tracks will render it immobile. Destroying its back engine or turret will disable the Shredder Tank, followed by it exploding. Significant amounts of damage will immediately cause it to explode.
Shredder Tanks
The Shredder Tank's turret is deadly, even at close range, due to its high rate of fire, relatively short reload, and fast rotation speed that can easily track and kill Helldivers.
Climbing onto a Shredder Tank is ill-advised due to its turret's rotation speed and height; it is only safe to be on top of the turret itself.

attacchi.descrizione: A powerful weapon mounted onto the massive War Strider. Paired, these weapons have enough output to break apart armoured vehicles and completely obliterate anything smaller.

The Fusion Culverin is as incredibly powerful as it is worryingly fragile. Where damage to its frame can be enough to cause a misfire, violently bursting the barrel, releasing volatile energy and rendering the weapon completely unusable.

Loaded with HE Grenades similar to those thrown by Troopers, the Projector can unload said munitions at a massive rate, range and quantity. Firing in a parabolic arc, the Projector completely saturates an area with high explosive ordinance.
Much like the smaller Hulks, the War Strider is capable of simply crushing whatever happens to be underneath it, albeit now with far more force, to the point where it can create shockwaves.

s: Appearing at Difficulty 6 (Extreme) and above, the War Strider can spawn in Automaton Outposts, from Bulk Fabricators, or within
. They also spawn in patrols outside of the Metropolis biome.

Certain mission types are devoid of War Striders unless they take place in an urban environment such as a Metropolis. These missions include Emergency Evacuation, Retrieve Valuable Data, Conduct Geological Survey, and Spread Democracy.
During a mission, War Striders replace Automaton Tanks slots.

Upon spotting Helldivers, the War Strider will fire volleys of grenades and lasers if at range, or will stomp if a Helldiver gets too close. Their Culverins are fired in bursts of 8 before cooling down for about 4 seconds.

War Striders are slow and will not often pursue Helldivers, instead launching a salvo of 10 grenades at them with their Grenade Projectors if at a sufficient distance and generally firing their Fusion Culverins. Such grenades are fired on a steep arc, allowing them to potentially ignore cover.
The War Strider is a heavy unit with AV 4 armor and high-powered weapons. Any weapon with AP 4 armor penetration or higher can damage any part of it except for the greaves on the back of its Legs.
The hip joints on the War Strider have a lower armor value of AV 3, allowing for weapons such as the
to take it down.
The Eye and Rear Vent are the War Strider's main weak spots; though highly durable, they are the lowest health parts that are fatal.
A single shot from the
in unsafe mode or three shots from the
can destroy either of its eyes.
The crotch and legs are more suitable targets for dedicated anti-tank weapons, as they have significantly more health.
A single shot from the
or
missile can kill the War Strider regardless of which body part it hits, making it the most effective weapon system against them.
Two shots from the
to the torso will kill a War Strider, which the automated aiming always targets.
A single hit from the
, or the
to the crotch, hip joints, or legs will destroy the Strider.
The
and
can eliminate the Strider with two shots to the crotch or legs, or a single shot to the hip joints.
A single
can kill the War Strider when thrown at its torso or crotch.
The
can stagger the War Strider, causing it to temporarily cease its attacks. In a pinch, 2 shots to the eye or hip joint will destroy the Strider.
Eagle strike stratagems such as the
, and
can take advantage of the War Strider's low mobility to deal heavy damage. The
is also a very effective option, being capable of one-shotting the War Strider if all 6 rockets land.
The grenades fired from its Launchers will ignore the shield generated from
and
Consequently, engaging War Striders requires players to not only find cover but also reserve a safe exit route in case the War Strider attacks with grenades.
These grenades can be tossed away, akin to a
's, but this is ill-advised due to the sheer volume of grenades.
Simply strafing horizontally is an effective way to dodge fire from the War Strider.

During a mission, the Helldivers may hear the unique "howling" of nearby War Striders. This audio cue enables Helldivers to detect the presence of War Striders and reconsider their tactics for further actions.
If Helldivers are close enough to War Strider, they can hear their usual chatting instead of howling.
The design of the War Strider is reminiscent of the "ED-209" bipedal robot from RoboCop (1987)

Landed Dropships encountered during the "Destroy Dropships" objective of a Sabotage Air Base mission have a different health and armor pool compared to their flying variants, which is detailed on that dedicated mission page.
During a mission, Dropships always come from the same direction. Helldivers can keep an eye on this to intercept them.
The
, and
main gun can destroy and cleave the fuselage of Dropships, guaranteeing the destruction of any AutomatonsAutomatons loaded onto it.
The Dropship must be destroyed before it begins to drop its payload.
The thrusters of the Dropship are its weak points.
Destroying any one of its four thrusters will knock it out of the air, likely causing it to fall onto its payload and explode.

If the SEAF SAM Site objective has been completed, it will attempt to aid in shooting down any Dropships and other Automaton aircraft during the mission. However, depending on the location and flight path of the Dropship, it may not be able to destroy the Dropship before it can drop its payload.

As they are hanging from the underbelly of the Dropship, it is possible to damage and destroy any Automaton Automaton passengers before and while they're being deployed. Weapons with high splash damage such as the
can accomplish this most effectively, as this may be more effective than trying to land several shots on the same thruster before the Dropship can escape.
The Dropships have twelve available spaces to carry Automatons (six on each side). Each Automaton unit takes up a different amount of space on the Dropship.
All Troopers and all Devastators take up one slot.
Both the normal Scout Strider and the reinforced variant take up only one slot despite the visual size of them.
All Hulks take up four slots.
The War Strider takes eight slots.
All tank variants and the Factory Strider take up all twelve slots.
Dropships in Metropolises will descend from the sky like
s instead of take their usual flight entry, increasing the difficulty of interception.
The Dropship may accidentally drop in reinforcements onto their own contact mines, potentially killing them.

attacchi.descrizione: A heavily-modified Battle Cannon. The Fusion Repeater Cannon takes advantage of massive generators upon the Factory Strider to cycle up to three devastating shots in a single salvo. Only the hardiest of fortifications can hope to withstand such firepower.

Whilst lacking the stopping power or accuracy of the larger Heavy Fusion Repeater, the Fusion Gatling Gun makes up for this through sheer volume of fire, proving especially effective against lightly armored infantry and providing suppressive fire.
The fusion generators powering the Factory Strider dwarf even the Automaton Heavy Tanks, supplying the demands of its many systems. The meltdown of its reactor is nothing less than cataclysmic.

s: Factory Striders can be first found in the Eliminate Automaton Factory Strider Mission starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging). Starting on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission) (and on Difficulty 6 (Extreme) when the Cyborg LegionCyborg Legion is present), they begin spawning from Bot Drops or guarding Heavy Automaton Outposts.

The secondary objective Intercept Convoy spawns five Factory Striders, patrolling from one end of the map to the other. One of them uniquely carries a Stratagem Scrambler that resembles a miniature Stratagem Jammer.
On planets invaded by the Cyborg LegionCyborg Legion, they are replaced by
s starting on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission), including on convoy secondary objectives. The objective icon, however, does not change.

Upon being alerted to a Helldiver's presence, the Factory Strider will audibly roar, and the Factory Strider's armaments will fire independently at the Helldiver as long as they are in the Factory Strider's line of sight. As its cannon can rotate 360° and independently from the Factory Strider, it will often be the first to fire. It can fire up to three rounds as long as a Helldiver is in its line of sight and not too close to the Factory Strider. Its Fusion Gatling Guns have a limited rotation, mainly tied to the Factory Strider's head, but fire at a deadly 1200 RPM. The Factory Strider can also knock down and damage Helldivers as it walks.
The Factory Strider, pertaining to its name, will also spawn four Devastators every 50-55 seconds, and makes a sound akin to a mechanical door opening when it is doing so.
Upon taking a lethal blow, it will let out a shriek before violently exploding. As it is dying, its body can crush Helldivers near it.
The Factory Strider's massive health pool allows it to take a significant amount of damage, even from offensive Stratagems. The
, and
are examples of stratagems that can destroy or soften up the Factory Strider for AP 5 armor penetrating Support Weapons.
Two support weapons that can easily destroy a Factory Strider regardless of where it hits are the
and

The Factory Strider's gatling guns are deadly at close range, especially if Helldivers are in front of it. Helldivers can destroy its gatling guns using AP 3 armor penetrating or higher Support Weapons such as the
, or the
Helldivers can stim themselves to survive its fusion gatling guns, unless it manages to hit their head.
Oddly, the Factory Strider's fusion gatling guns do not fire at Exosuits. However, its cannon will still fire at them.

The Factory Strider's "eye" is a fatal zone, requiring AP 4 armor penetrating weaponry. It is vital for Helldivers to take out their fusion gatling guns first, as the exposed part of the head is small and requires precise aim.
Helldivers can destroy their head armor with a single shot from an
, or 2 shots from an
or
. The armor's destruction exposes the entirety of the head to AP 4 armor-penetrating support weapons, making it much easier to destroy.

The Factory Strider's undercarriage is another weak spot. Destroying it only requires AP 3 armor penetrating weaponry, and it has slightly lower health than its eye. Note the constitution has 0 decay, therefore it behaves as hp for a total of 2,400 effective health. However, this requires the Helldiver to be under or near the Factory Strider, and may leave the Helldiver open to its newly-deployed Devastators. Similar to its eye, it is also important for Helldivers to destroy its fusion gatling guns first before going for its undercarriage.
Helldivers should aim at an individual undercarriage door as they have separate health pools.
When using machine guns for this method, it is recommended to set their fire rate to its highest.
The Commando is able to deal 2,316 damage with two missiles, allowing any AP 3 or higher armor-penetrating weapons to easily finish the panel off.

The Factory Strider's feet are also a weak spot. Note the constitution has 0 decay, therefore it behaves as hp for a total of 3,500 effective health. It can be destroyed in 3 shots from the E/AT-12 Anti-Tank Emplacement, 2 shots from the
or
, and only requires one shot from the Bastion's main cannon. The
are also a viable strategy, especially so against Factory Striders in a Convoy, as they follow a predictable path, only taking 2-3 mines to bring them down.
The Factory Strider's cannon requires AP 5 weaponry to take out, such as the
and GR-8 Recoilless Rifle. As the
or

automatically target the center of an enemy, it will sometimes end up destroying the cannon first. If the destroyer is not directly above the Factory Strider, the Railcannon Strike will usually successfully strike the main body instead.

The Factory Strider's cannon is powerful enough to destroy demo 50 threshold structures. Smart Helldivers may use this to their advantage to destroy Automaton Fabricators, Bulk Fabricators, Detector Towers, Stratagem Jammers, and Rogue Research Stations.
Despite their size, Factory Striders will die immediately if the
carrying them is shot down by destroying the fuselage before the deployment window.

If a SEAF SAM Site is active, it will attempt to engage the Dropship carrying it. However, if the missile approaches at an improper angle (like from underneath), it may destroy the Factory Strider directly instead of the Dropship carrying it.
The E/AT-12 Anti-Tank Emplacement, EAT-17 Expendable Anti-Tank, and LAS-99 Quasar Cannon can quickly kill a Factory Strider in 2 shots to the exposed head or 1 shot from the GR-8 Recoilless Rifle.
Brave Helldivers can use the
to destroy Factory Striders within range.
Factory Striders were quietly introduced to the game on April 1st, 2024 in addition to the
during Phase III of Operation Swift Disassembly.
The Factory Strider may be inspired by Star Warss AT-M6 or AT-AT Walkers.

The Icarus Launcher Pod allows the Vox Engine to unload dozens of powerful, guided HEAT missiles, brutally decimating infantry and battering armoured vehicles into dented, blasted wrecks.

attacchi.descrizione: Upon fatal damage being dealt to whatever reactor powers this war machine, the once mighty Vox Engine undergoes a chain of fierce explosions as its reactor melts down before finally erupting into a truly massive explosion that throws flaming debris about.

Chief amongst the debris thrown by said explosion is the now destroyed sarcophagus which, while functionless, still presents a danger as the heavy object plummets from the sky like a meteor, crushing any unfortunate who happens to be in its path.

s: Vox Engines are part of the Cyborg Legion sub-faction of the Automatons and can only spawn on worlds where the Cyborgs are present. They begin spawning on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission) missions, either as part of a patrol, reinforcements, or in enemy-occupied locations. The secondary objective Intercept Convoy on a cyborg-present planet will instead spawn five Vox Engines, patrolling from one end of the map to the other.
Vox Engines replace
s on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission) and above on planets where Cyborgs are present.
Vox Engines can be heard spewing Cyborg propaganda, allowing Helldivers early warning of their approach.
Vox Engines have three sets of two weapons each:
Plasma Macro-Culverins mounted on each side of its torso.
Plasma Duster Miniguns mounted on each side of its undercarriage.
and Icarus Missile Launcher Pods mounted on the back of its Torso, right behind its Macro-Culverins.
When alerted, Vox Engines will blare an alarm from the loudspeakers atop the units as they begin to approach Helldivers, engaging with their various weaponry depending on distance.
The Vox Engine has a massive health pool of 9,000 and potent firepower, making head-on attacks ill-advised.
The Vox Engine has 6 glowing yellow heatsinks. Three are located on the rear chassis and underside of the Vox Engine. Three more are located on the upper portion of the rear torso.

Destroying the three heatsinks found at the top will cause a hatch to open on the top of the Vox Engine, whereas destroying the three found at the bottom will cause a hatch to open up on the back of the Vox Engine. Throwing a grenade into either vent will instantly destroy the Vox Engine.
This method works ONLY with Throwables regardless of damage or
, except
This method does not work with explosive projectile weapons like the
or

Destroying a Vox Engine's heatsinks will deal an additional 700 damage to its Main health per heatsink. With each vent having 300hp to start with, destroying all 6 does at minimum 6,000 damage to main health. In addition, 100% of the damage dealt to an intact heatsink will be transferred to its Main health.
Because of this, high-damage, non-explosive, single-shot weapons such as the
and
(on Total mode) will deal massive damage to its Main health when targeting the vents.
When faced head-on, a quick way to destroy a Vox Engine is to either plant two
charges, 2
grenades or 2
shots on its undercarriage.
Alternatively, Helldivers can outright destroy a Vox Engine with a single
or
with a shot to the body. Or with three
is shots to the front (within 150m).
One use of the
will instantly destroy the Vox Engine.
Sometimes the Orbital Railcannon Strike may hit the speaker which has overflow cap, and will prevent the Vox Engine from being one shot.
Two uses of the
can destroy a Vox Engine.
If one does not have these stratagems one can use the
to shoot the trackpod latches, tracks and torso flaps to destroy the Vox Engine via Main health depletion.
Note that the tracks can continue to take damage even when destroyed.
The Vox Engine is equipped with three weapon systems, each of which can be disabled by destroying them.
Helldivers are recommended to first destroy the miniguns to flank the Vox Engine. Weapons with high durable damage such as the
and
are ideal for this task.
Destroying a Macro-Culverin does 2,000 explosion damage (5,000 total reduced by 60% due to ExDR) to the Vox Engine.
Destroying both Macro-Culverins will instantly kill the Vox Engine. Their 3,500 health pool allows for the
or the
's main cannon to instantly destroy them, while other Anti-Tank weapons take two shots. The
and
need 3 shots, while the

needs 4. The players can also use any AP 4 armor-penetrating weapons to destroy the Macro-Culverin guns, as they are AV 4 armor. Though this is ill-advised due to the high durability and colossal health pool.
At longer ranges, the Vox Engine will fire out a volley of missiles at Helldivers. The missile impact locations will glow yellow on the ground, indicating the areas that should be avoided.
If the missiles cannot be avoided, it is advised to lie prone to reduce the explosion damage taken.
Destroying either missile launcher will disable the Vox Engine's ability to launch missiles.
The Vox Engine's Macro-Culverin guns have unrestricted gun depression and can fire directly down, allowing it to damage and kill Helldivers below it.
The Macro-Culverins also have a demolition force of 50, so they can be baited to fire at Stratagem Jammers and Detector Towers to destroy them.
When the Vox Engine explodes, some of its debris will be launched into the air and can fall on Helldivers, crushing them.
During the Vox Engine's explosion, its sarcophagus will be ejected in the direction it was facing at the time of death.

The Vox Engine is manned by a high-ranking Cyborg officer, and it will try to eject its sarcophagus out of the machine upon imminent destruction. Despite its efforts, the Cyborg will die alongside its machine, regardless of being ejected or not.
This can be seen by Helldivers, in which the ejected sarcophagus and the Cyborg housed within will remain motionless on the ground.

The Vox Engine bears some resemblance to the Siege Mech from Helldivers 1. Despite this, the Vox Engine does not fill the same niche as the Siege Mech, with the former simply being another heavy unit, while the latter is a boss encounter akin to the
The Vox Engine’s appearance seems to be inspired by the Hunter Killer (HK) tanks from the Terminator franchise.
When throwing a grenade in its hatch to destroy a Vox Engine, even grenades with 0 damage, such as the
, or even
, will destroy the Vox Engine.
This is because the Vox Engine's unique fatal weak spot will trigger a kill for any grenade that is coded with an explosion, regardless of damage or demo force.
Snowballs can be used for this purpose as well.
Vox Engines are able to climb or be dropped on top of tall buildings, making them far more deadly.
When shooting the side Torso vents, the Missile Launchers may not render properly and block Helldivers shots without their knowledge.
The Gatling guns can get shoved through walls and still be able to fire at any Helldiver hiding behind them.
The Vox Engine sometimes runs through raised defense gates or scales over entire defense walls.
Collision with various parts of the Vox Engine (such as the tracks) is not enabled properly, allowing the engine to phase through areas far too small for it to physically pass.

attacchi.descrizione: The pilot within the Gatekeeper may occasionally use the Gatekeeper's Starcannons as primitive clubs which, while clearly not their intended role, are still effective in swatting away foes that draw too close.

s: Gatekeepers are part of the Appropriators Appropriators sub-faction of the Illuminate and can only spawn on worlds where the Appropriators are present. They begin spawning on Difficulty 4 (Challenging) and above.
Gatekeepers rarely spawn, and typically present less of a threat than more commonly spawned
on higher difficulties. When they do arrive, they typically are positioned between
at the front and Harvesters at the back, occupying a suppressive midline role on the battlefield.
They have two attacks with their twin Plasma Starcannons, which project blue guiding lasers at their target:
A two-shot, concussive plasma burst that is capable of ragdolling a Helldiver behind cover. After the attack, the ends of the barrels will flare out, closing back in while preparing another attack.
A much longer plasma volley that can very easily shred apart a Helldiver if they do not take evasive maneuvers. This is preceded by the Starcannons "pumping", and the barrels rapidly winding up.
Gatekeepers, unlike
have AV 4 armor and prefer to stay further away. They have two ranged attacks.
A charged, large AOE Plasma Starcannon blast with immense damage that can ragdoll from a distance.
A telegraphed moderate damage, rapid-fire volley that slowly tracks the targeted Helldiver, similar to a Gazer.

The cockpit is similar to Veracitor cockpits, but it instead has AV 4 armor. It is also protected by a rechargeable energy shield. When destroyed, the pilot is vulnerable to gunfire and when killed, will also destroy the mech.
Note the pilot is 50% durable, unlike the Veracitor's pilot, so they may require several more rounds to kill.
Similar to
and their sibling enemy
, Gatekeepers are highly resistant to pure explosive damage, as all limbs are immune to explosive damage.
The horn on the Gatekeeper's forehead is the unit's shield generator, similar to a
. When destroyed, the pilot's shield is permanently disabled. It is, however AV 4 armor.
Gatekeepers have a melee attack, but its use is uncommon and is easily avoided.
Firing a single high-damage shot (such as from the
or
) to the connecting stump that holds the Pilot's Cockpit can instantly destroy said cockpit, killing the machine with it.
If a Gatekeeper is hit with a stun effect such as that from a
or
, then the Overseer pilot can be seen angrily smacking at the controls to try and boot it back up.
According to its description, the Gatekeeper is a variant of the
that is made for combat.
