attacchi.descrizione: Fitted onto the ever numerous Obtruder. The Plasma Torch is an unremarkable weapon, yet very effective when fired en masse by multiple Obtruders, capable of reducing any human-sized foe into a burnt-out heap of flesh and bone.
Much like its Watcher relative, a knocked out Obtruder can still be a hazard to any underneath it. Its weight is capable of crushing any unfortunate that happens to be below it.
The Obtruder has an alarming tendency to violently explode upon crashing onto solid ground, killing infantry and even capable of severely damaging vehicles.

s: Obtruders are part of the Appropriators sub-faction of the Illuminate and can only spawn on worlds where the Appropriators are present. As a relatively weak unit, they spawn and are usually encountered in groups during missions.
Obtruders resemble
s but differ in that they cannot call for reinforcements and spawn in extremely large groups of up to 18(tbd), either in fast-moving patrols or directly from

s. They act as a flying chaff unit, quickly closing in over any type of terrain to surround a Helldiver at close range before firing. They can fly quite high in the air and tend to gravitate very quickly towards nearby suspected Helldiver activity, so caution should be exercised if trying to avoid Obtruder patrols.
Obtruders fire single energy blasts from their Plasma Torches towards their targets instead of an electrical arc like the

uses. They have an extremely slow fire rate, display a charging animation before each shot, and are highly inaccurate. It will usually require several or even dozens of Obtruders to pose a threat to Helldivers, but since they fly and spawn in groups, their numbers can quickly add up if a Helldiver draws too much attention.
The low damage, slow fire rate and clear telegraphs makes individual Obtruder attacks near-ineffective.
As such, it is often best to focus on more dangerous enemies unless you find yourself becoming surrounded by Obtruders.
Obtruders can be easily dealt with using weapons with a high rate of fire and good handling, letting the shooter snap from target to target.
Arc weapons and explosives can also be useful when engaging several Obtruders, due to their tendency to coalesce and form dense groups.
In particular, the
in Flak mode is very effective against them.
Any explosives with a slower projectile(s) may have difficulty directly hitting Obtruders due their tendency to bob and weave in the air.
Due to their tendency to rush down Helldivers and engage them in close proximity, Obtruders are susceptible to the Guard Dog lineup. The
and
have little trouble tracking and dispatching them as they approach, while the
can lock down groups of them with well-placed arc chains.
Obtruders (like
) are a medium size enemy, and so the

will lock onto them. This is detrimental to the weapon's overall effectiveness, as Obtruders spawn in such high numbers that they can make it all but impossible for the W.A.S.P. to secure a lock-on against more dangerous enemies behind them.
Similarly, the
will have a hard time locking onto important targets like a Watcher about to call in reinforcements, or an
, when it's surrounded by Obtruders.
The strong lights and similar silhouettes of Obtruders can make it difficult to pick out Watchers in combat, however, Obtruders entirely lack the cone of light that Watchers emit.
Obtruders also make the same noises that Watchers do.
Due to overlapping hitbox, 2 shots to the eye with ~90 dmg weapons or 1 shot with a 200 dmg such as the
, may kill the Obtruder because 3 hitboxes are damaged: the Eye, Body, and Main with a single shot.
Like
, Obtruders explode on death and subsequent ground contact, dealing near if not lethal damage to Helldivers it lands extremely close to.
This explosion affects other, nearby Obtruders, causing large groups to potentially chain-react.
Correzioni
Fixed issue where Obtruders were not attacking players while mounted behind a Grenadier Battlement.
Will now collide correctly with Helldivers.
Reduced clipping between Obtruder and Helldivers' Vehicles.
Modifiche non annunciate
Projectile angled armor penetration increased
Slight Angle armor penetration increased from AV 3 to AV 4
Addition

attacchi.descrizione: Once supposedly used in a more logistical role, the Veracitor's gigantic claws are just as capable of tearing apart foes that stand against them. Even light vehicles are not safe from its razor sharp talons.

Alternatively, the Veracitor will settle with simply crushing its foe by slamming its fists upon them. The machine's strength is such that it often reduces any humanoid foe to a bloodied mess and can even flatten armoured vehicles into smoke-belching wrecks.
The Veracitor may occasionally use its mass to plow through whatever obstacle or vehicle stands in its way. The few who survive will then have to contend with being crushed underfoot.

s: Veracitors are part of the AppropriatorsAppropriators sub-faction of the Illuminate and can only spawn on worlds where the Appropriators are present. They begin spawning on Difficulty 4 (Challenging) and onwards from
s or patrols.

Veracitors will pursue Helldivers by charging and approaching them with their leg-like appendages. Once close enough, they will swipe with their claws to deal damage. At range, they will cross their arms in order to protect the piloting
. The pilot will also sometimes do a charge if far enough from the Helldivers.
The cockpit is protected by a rechargeable energy shield, when destroyed, the pilot is vulnerable to gunfire and when killed will also destroy the mech.
Unlike normal overseers, the pilot is a unified AV 2 hitbox, so there is no need to aim for particular weakpoints when shooting the pilot.
Similar to
and their sibling enemy
, Veracitors are highly resistant to pure explosive damage, as all limbs are immune to explosive damage.
The arms of a Veracitor are AV 3 armor, leaving them vulnerable to the
, or other weapons capable of penetrating medium armor. The
with its AV 3 penetrating flak is extremely effective when aimed at the cockpit, due to that area's close proximity and line-of-sight to all of the limbs.
Destroying the head of the Veracitor exosuit will permanently disable the shield covering its pilot.

Destroying the armor surrounding the "head" of this enemy will reveal an AV 1 weakspot that can be destroyed to destroy the entire enemy. Holding the highground allows you to dispatch the Veracitor with this method even easier.

The Veracitor features several AV 1 weakspot blue vents on its body. Destroying these destroy the body part they are attached to. The Cockpit Weakspot however is Fatal, instantly eliminating the Veracitor.
Anti-tank weaponry such as the
and
should generally target the unshielded parts of the cockpit as it is far easier to hit and eliminate target.
Unlike other enemies, a patrolling Veracitor can detect and engage Helldivers from 100 meters.
If a Veracitor is stunned with an EMP attack such as a
or
, then the Overseer pilot can be seen angrily smacking at the controls to try and boot it back up.

The Veracitor is likely a reference to the Yale Veracitor forklift. This suggests that the primary purpose of the Veracitor is excavation, a theory further supported by it’s appearance alongside Illuminate ruins
This is further reinforced by its description, which states that it is "an overly complicated forklift".
Modifiche
Veracitors now guard Outposts
Increased melee force strength from 25 to 40
Conformed Exomech melee's attacks to all correctly be Anti-Tank.
Correzioni
Fixed a bug where the Veracitor's melee attack could clip through Helldivers holding the SH-20 Ballistic Shield Backpack
Fixed an issue where the Veracitor clipped through buildings and obstacles while charging. It should now destroy anything in its path and stop when hitting a wall.
Correzioni
Fixed Veracitor patrol animation
Veracitor will not trigger its charge within a narrow path, reducing instances where they'll clip through destructible obstacles.
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: Once human hands, now corrupted and mutated beyond recognition and reformed into hardened claws, something the Voteless use to bludgeon, leap and tear their foe apart in mindless frenzy.

s: Voteless are the most prevalent Illuminate unit and are present in virtually every settlement, patrol, and enemy reinforcement. They additionally emerge frequently from Grounded Warp Ship.
On planets where the Appropriators and Vote Snatchers subfactions are active, the Voteless are completely absent.

Voteless attack by running towards Helldivers, attacking with a swipe of their claws when within melee range. Voteless are able to lunge a short distance towards targets that are slightly out of reach of their default attacking range.
The primary tactic of the Voteless is to overwhelm Helldivers with sheer numbers and speed to soak up fire for the more dangerous Illuminate enemies.
Voteless are slightly more resilient than other chaff units like
s and
s.
Weapons with a high volume of fire or large area of effect are well-suited for cutting down Voteless hordes.
Effective examples include the
, and

effects are particularly effective against massive hordes of Voteless due to their confusion effects. The poisonous Gas damage itself will also neutralise a Voteless within 4 to 7 seconds, depending on their size.
Setting a Voteless on
is sufficient to kill them outright even without other sources of damage, but does not confuse them.
Beam weapons such as the
and incendiary shotguns like the
are notable for being able to set Voteless ablaze at ranges farther than they can run before burning down.
The
and
are effective against hordes of Voteless because of their area-of-effect capabilities.
Some Voteless may continue to crawl and attack after losing their legs.
If they survive losing a leg, Voteless will collapse to the ground and then spend a couple of seconds examining their legs before they resume their advance at a reduced speed.
The majority of fully automatic weapons can destroy a Voteless' leg in a single shot. Doing this can significantly reduce their mobility.
Voteless' heads are a weak point that can be targeted to eliminate them quickly.
Upon death, blue particles and smoke seem to seep out of the Voteless, with their eyes being drained of their blue shine.
Death by
or single, precise hits to their head may result in the Voteless showing strange behavior before dying:
Their body stiffening straight and performing a rough Super Earth salute.
Looking around in a confused or clueless manner.
Frantic, fearful glances in different directions before kneeling down and perishing.
Catching a final glimpse of their unsightly form by looking at their now disfigured arms.
The aforementioned behaviors do not occur in crawling Voteless.

If a leg-shot is damaging enough to kill a Voteless instead of sending them into their crawling state, the Voteless may gesture incredulously at their injured leg before losing their balance and dying.

attacchi.descrizione: The heaviest portable weapon in the Overseer's arsenal. The Plasma Bombard is capable of discharging violent bolts of superheated plasma that are capable of reducing armoured infantry to nothing more than molten slag and vapourised flesh.

attacchi.descrizione: Crescent Overseers can additionally turn their Plasma Bombards into terrifying artillery pieces. Here, they loose rapid salvoes of plasma bolts that are akin to a hail of flame, exploding in superheated fury upon impact.
attacchi.effetti: Anti-Vehicle / (Ballistic Damage Only) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion)

attacchi.descrizione: The Crescent Overseer can also land a fearsome punch upon any Helldiver that draws too close, often with enough force to crack their helmets outright with devastating results.

s: Crescent Overseers appear naturally throughout a map, in patrols, and can be summoned via reinforcements. They're the least plentiful Overseer variant, being limited to 1-2 instances in a given spawn condition.
On planets where the Appropriators Appropriators or Vote Snatchers Vote Snatchers subfactions are active, the Crescent Overseer are completely absent.

Crescent Overseers slowly roam the battlefield and stop to aim their Plasma Bombard and lob plasma projectiles in an arcing trajectory once they detect enemies in their effective range. These attacks are able to cover a massive range and flush Helldivers out from cover and behind tall structures.
Should a Helldiver confront them up close, they will instead shift their stance to hold their Bombard with both hands and aim directly at their target, firing projectiles in a manner similar to the
At point-blank range, they'll free up one hand to punch enemies in front of them.
Crescent Overseers are functionally very similar to
s, being able to provide indirect artillery fire from long ranges but also attack in close-quarters scenarios.

Unlike Spewers, Crescent Overseers cannot inflict lingering Crowd Control effects via Acid damage, are much smaller in size, have no prominent weakspot, and possess Ablative armor like their fellow Overseer variants.
Crescent Overseers can shoot very quickly while using indirect-fire attacks, and attempt to predict Helldiver movement by leading their shots.

When confronted at close to medium range, their alternate firing stance cannot fire projectiles as frequently, and they shoot less accurately. With practice, Helldivers can dodge a Crescent Overseer's forward shots by going prone.

Crescent Overseer possess the same body type and armor as standard Overseers, but given their less effective combat capabilities once in direct line of sight, they're the least durable Overseer variant.

Given their massive effective range, Crescent Overseers may stay in the same spot they were reinforced from without moving, resulting in groups that can bombard Helldivers with constant barrages of plasma. However, once found, they are susceptible to being taken out all at once via explosive weapons, stratagems, or sustained fire.
Similar to the
s' jetpack, the Crescent Overseer's backpack is a weak spot; destroying it will instantly kill the Crescent Overseer.
While grounded Overseers have a stagger resistance of 35, the flesh underneath only has a resistance of 20.
As a result, hitting their flesh with weapons like the
, and
will stagger them, interrupting their attacks.

attacchi.descrizione: Utlilising advanced Illuminate technology, the Plasma Storm Rifle rapidly unloads salvos of glowing, baseball-sized plasma projectiles. Exclusively wielded by Elevated Overseers to lend fire support.

Used by Elevated Overseers, these containers are built with a time fuse that, when expired, will unleash a blast of heat and light that bursts forth with plasma, burning any target caught in the blast.
Despite their advanced technology, the Elevated Overseer's Jetpack explodes all the same when sufficiently punctured, oftentimes outright killing the user and anyone nearby in the process.

s: Elevated Overseers are often seen accompanying patrolling hordes of
on their own. Additionally, they may spawn naturally on specific objectives throughout the map, via Grounded Warp Ship, and via
reinforcements.
On planets where Mindless Masses Mindless Masses or Vote Snatchers Vote Snatchers subfactions are active, Elevated Overseers will be completely absent.

Elevated Overseers move by flying above the ground and taking sharp turns to evade attacks. They otherwise slowly advance towards Helldivers while firing quick, 7-round bursts from their Storm Rifles.
Elevated Overseers will intermittently throw Plasma Detonator grenades between attacks.
An Elevated Overseer will attempt to maintain a 10-meter distance from the closest Helldiver.
Due to their flight maneuverability and frequent dodging, Elevated Overseers can be difficult to hit.

Helldivers can manipulate a nearby Elevated Overseer's movement by diving toward them while applying suppressive fire. The dive both forces their retreat and reduces the accuracy of their plasma projectiles.
The
, and
(with stun rounds) can stun them repeatedly and halt their strafing, allowing Helldivers to finish them off without difficulty.
Once stunned, a Helldiver can quickly line up a headshot with the
or the
to kill them instantly.
Being stunned also causes them to drop their Detonator grenades they were about to throw, significantly reducing their threat.
Since the AX/AR-23 "Guard Dog" and AX/LAS-5 "Guard Dog" Rover both have perfect accuracy, they can strip away their armor plating for Helldivers to shoot their exposed flesh.
The

is a very simple yet effective counter against them, as they can be killed within a single magazine. The weapon's built-in target tracking largely trivializes the Elevated Overseer's evasive aerial maneuvers.
Destroying their jetpacks will detonate them, killing them outright.

Often the jetpack detonates on its own after an Elevated Overseer has been eliminated by fire/burning damage. All Helldivers and any other lightly armored entities caught in this explosion will also be eliminated.
Care should be taken near corpses with intact jetpacks until they are despawned or destroyed, as they remain detonatable.
Unlike their
, Elevated Overseers possess unique voice lines with a different-sounding filter.

attacchi.descrizione: Overseers will alternatively use their Lightspears in melee combat, swinging and spinning the staffs with immense strength and grace, able to quickly knock Helldivers onto the ground.

s: Overseers spawn via patrols, specific mission objectives, Grounded Warp Ships, and
reinforcements. They do not spawn on planets where the Vote Snatchers subfaction is presented.

Overseers fire single, high-damage projectiles from their Lightspear when at range, after a minor charge-up delay. When receiving heavy fire, Overseers raise their collapsible energy shields, which cover their upper and middle body.
When facing Helldivers at close range, Overseers will charge toward them and use their Lightspear as a melee weapon, swinging in quick, wide sweeps that ragdoll targets.
Upon first noticing a Helldiver, they will point towards them with their Lightspear and order nearby
to attack.
It is possible to the Overseer Lightspear's slow projectiles by manuvering around.
Overseers are formidable at close range; their melee strikes will knock Helldivers to the ground; follow-up hits usually kill before targets have a chance to recover.
If enough armor plating has been stripped away, the Helldiver's own melee will stagger Overseers.
For more consistently successful staggering, proper stun-capable melee weapons such as
and
are highly recommended. Only one connecting melee hit with either of these weapons will stun an Overseer long enough to allow repositioning to a safe distance, allowing a finish with explosives like
Weapons that deal explosion damage, such as the
are highly effective against Overseers because it directly damages main health and can damage them through their shields.
High-fire-rate weapons like the
or the standard
are very effective at shredding their armor and flesh once exposed.
Overseers cover the weakest part of their body: their head, with a AV 3 armored helmet. Weapons with AP 3 armor penetration value or higher can damage this weak point.
Examples include the
, and
The Overseer's shield is not large enough to cover its legs, allowing Helldivers to continue dealing damage to it while the shield is active.
Alternatively, any SEAF asset closing in within 10 meters forces an Overseer to lower/deactivate the shield.
Overseers have a stagger resistance of 35; the flesh underneath only has a resistance of 20.
As a result, hitting their flesh with weapons like the
, and
will stagger them, interrupting their attacks.
The fins on an Overseer's helmet resemble the head fins of real-life cephalopods, in line with the sea creature aesthetic shared by most Illuminate units.

attacchi.descrizione: This device is capable of building up a charge and releasing it as an arc, inflicting painful electrical burns and disorienting the foe in the process.
A plummeting Watcher remains a hazard to any underneath it. Its weight is such that it is capable of crushing any unfortunate that happens to be below it.

It is unknown if it is by design to prevent capture or because it is simply fragile, but Watchers violently explode upon crashing onto solid ground, killing infantry and even capable of severely damaging vehicles.

s: Watchers can be found on all difficulties, spawning throughout the map. They do not spawn on planets occupied by Vote Snatchers.

Watchers fly around the map and scan its surroundings with a luminescent blue light, visualizing its point of view. Once alerted, through direct line of sight of a Helldiver, attacks directly at them, or near them, it will shine a bright pink light and begin investigating.
Upon spotting Helldivers once more, or while being continuously attacked by them, Watchers will typically halt and emit holographic flares that call in
for reinforcements.
They may also attack with its Tesla Suppressor, firing debilitating
of lightning when Helldivers are close to it.
As the only unit of the Illuminate Illuminate that can call in reinforcements, Watchers should be quickly dispatched to prevent them.

Visually, Watchers sends out several blue flares upwards to signal reinforcements, but the actual signal gets sent before this occurs, indicated by the "Illuminate Ships Incoming" event message at the top of the screen.
The
and
are able to destroy Watchers in a single hit to the main body.
The
and
are effective weapons for stunning Watchers. This will interrupt their reinforcement calls and leave them floating still for a moment.
Watchers can survive having multiple of their "fins" torn off; Helldivers should prioritize aiming at center mass.
Its lightning discharge deals low damage, but temporarily slows and slightly drains a Helldiver's stamina. This makes it especially dangerous near a horde of
or a group of
s.
Upon death, Watchers will fall to the ground. And with enough velocity, its carcass will explode once colliding into anything. The blast radius is small, but lethal.
The carcass of Watcher can stay intact when touching the ground when the falling velocity stays low enough. This is most often achieved with the fatal-hit being either
or

overtime-damage while the Watcher is floating less than 2-meters of height. Any kinetic last-hit or a fall from greater than 2-meters of heigh will always end up increasing the falling velocity threshold to explosion being crossed.
The intact carcass of Watcher can be rolled around the ground and even flung around with light/medium ballistics, or powerful enough melee strikes (E.G. with
). However, the carcass will explode once there is enough velocity when once more colliding into a surface.
Modifiche

Correzioni

attacchi.descrizione: Taking the form of 2 additional limbs sprouting from what was once its shoulders, each ending in a metallic spike, The Wretch has little trouble impaling, dismembering and overall butchering whatever victms happen to be in its way.

Whilst nowhere even remotely as potent as their upper scythe-tipped limbs, the Wretch is still capable of swiping at foes with what was once its original arms, which are still more than capable of wounding and disorienting foes with quick swipes.

s: Since there are no
to call reinforcements on a planet occupied by Vote Snatchers, Wretches will only spawn naturally as patrols and guarding points of interest.
However, they spawn in much greater numbers comparatively.
They, along with
, are spawned from
during Repel Invasion Fleet missions on planets where the Vote Snatchers are active.

When a Wretch spots a Helldiver they will generally approach in a straight line, but will sometimes dart around cover to try and flank the Helldiver. It is not uncommon to be firing at a pair of Wretches only for another to attack from behind. They can move surprisingly fast and once in range they will pounce at Helldivers, dealing significant damage. This pounce attack also strongly tracks a moving Helldiver which makes it difficult to dodge.
Wretches are fast enemies that will pounce at Helldivers with razor-sharp claws, somewhat mimicking the behavior of a

When a Wretch pounces at a player, the main ways to avoid damage are to kill it mid-jump, slide, crouch, or immediately go prone, as they will track the targeted Helldiver's movement during their pounce and deliver a sideways slash that can easily hit a player mid-dive.
Pouncing Wretches can easily pass through shield of a
and hit a wearer directly from certain angles.
Wretches will prioritize sentries and emplacements over Helldivers and SEAF Troops.
When facing a group of Wretches and Voteless, weapons with a high amount of DPS such as the
and
are highly effective at killing them.
Alternatively, crowd control options such as Fire or Gas weapons can disrupt Wretches, preventing them from closing the distance to Helldivers.
, and
are effective, even against groups of Wretches.
Wretches have a very high stun threshold of 20, can still be staggered, and will be slowed by Gas and Fire.
When a Wretch’s head is removed, it will begin wildly slashing its claws in the general direction it was facing at the time of decapitation.
Helldivers are advised to aim for the Wretch’s limbs instead of its head, particularly its bladed arms in order to neutralize the threat quickly, preferably when there is less enemy pressure.
However, the Wretch's rampage is quite easy to avoid, as it adopts a visible bipedal position while walking slowly until it is killed or is far enough away that it is no longer a threat.

Due to their hunched posture, targeting the body in a chaotic close range fight may prove difficult. For this reason, Helldivers are advised to crouch and aim low to instead cut down their legs, stopping them from effectively attacking and pursuing.
The Wretch is likely inspired by the Slasher Necromorph from the Dead Space Franchise.

Both enemies feature a zombified humanoid appearance with a destroyed/distorted jaw, large bladed upper arms jutting out of the shoulders, and a lower pair of secondary grasping arms. The Wretch's eyes also glow similarly to an Enhanced Slasher's eyes.

In the Deep Dive: Battle for the Gateway Planet video, the overview mentions that their limbs need to be shot instead of their head, which is a direct nod to the franchise's famous quote "Cut off their limbs."
When the Wretch's head is destroyed, the way it stands up and wildly swings its blade arms is extremely similar to a decapitated Slasher.
Due to Host-side latency, the Wretch's leap has a significantly lower chance of hitting non-host players, even if all players have perfect internet connections.
Correzioni
Fixed an issue where Wretches and Crushers could clip through the floors of certain structures.
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: Swinging with the force of an artillery shell and with the ferocity only a Crusher could provide. The massive Cudgel is capable of reducing any human-sized foe into a mashed paste, as well as crushing even lightly armoured vehicles to pieces completely

Alongside their mighty cudgels, the mutated Crusher is also simply capable of stomping surviving foes beneath its massive "feet", often landing with such tremendous force that they create disorienting shockwaves around them.

s: Since there are no
s to call reinforcements on a planet occupied by Vote Snatchers, Crushers will only spawn naturally as patrols, and guarding points of interest.
However, they spawn in much greater numbers comparatively
They, along with
es, are spawned from
s during Repel Invasion Fleet missions and Warp Ships spawned by
during Take Down Overship missions on planets where the Vote Snatchers are active.

Crushers naturally walk around with their club dragging behind them. When a Crusher spots a Helldiver, they will sling the club over their shoulder and approach in a straight line until they are in range to attack with their club. Crushers produce an audio cue when engaging in combat that sounds similar to a loud horn or ringing bell.
Crushers will lunge forward when swinging, giving them deceptively long striking range.
Crushers are very durable and have very high health, meaning conventional attacks will often take a large amount of ammo and time to bring down a crusher.

Crushers possess the ability to regenerate health for all limbs and Main, except for their helmet and head, at a rate of 30 health per second 0.5s after taking damage, incentivizing Helldivers to deal with the threat quickly lest they become a problem later.
Using single-shot, anti-tank weaponry is ill-advised as Crushers are capable of withstanding a direct hit from weapons like the
or the
Crushers have a low health, AV 4 armor helmet that is able to deflect most attacks.
When the helmet is broken, the Crusher's weak head is revealed, allowing fatal headshots that eliminate them quickly.
Ballistic weapons with AP 4 armor penetration or higher (such as the
, and
) are all effective at destroying a Crusher's helmet, destroying it in one to two shots.
The Railgun is a particularly effective choice, with one Safe Mode shot destroying the helmet, allowing for either another Railgun shot to the head, or follow-up fire from a primary weapon.
Crushers primarily attack Helldivers by slamming their massive club to the ground; this will instantly kill Helldivers that are hit directly, and ragdoll those in a small radius around it.
A Crusher's arms can be severed; if its right arm holding the club is severed, it will use its left arm to smack down Helldivers; upon losing both arms, it will resort to stomping.
Despite the ExDR on its limbs, Crushers are weak to explosive weaponry; a single
grenade or brick from the
is capable of killing a Crusher. Additionally, the
, and
are highly effective against Crushers.

The AC-8 Autocannon is capable of staggering the Crusher out of its slam attack, giving Helldivers a brief moment to reposition. The Autocannon's Flak rounds are also capable of killing Crushers in five to six shots.
Crushers are vulnerable to the crowd control effects of
, and
, giving Helldivers time to reposition and engage from a safer distance.
The
is capable of shrugging off up to 5 strikes from a Crusher before breaking, making it a viable method of consistently surviving attacks when within melee range.
Blocking a strike directly still ragdolls the Helldiver, so it is not advised to do this while being swarmed by multiple enemies.
Due to their long attack animation (which does not track their target), Helldivers can run out of the impact zone before the attack hits. This makes running right past Crushers surprisingly safe.
Helldivers should ensure they stay moving to prevent Crushers reaching them.
The Crusher is unique since it is the first Illuminate enemy that can regenerate health for its individual limbs. The only other enemy that can regenerate health is the Terminid
Crushers may take inspiration from Pyramid Head from Silent Hill 2, particularly in their helmet design.
Crushers hands and feet are made up of multiple smaller human hands and feet.
After its helmet is destroyed, it will sob loudly, then throw a violent tantrum like a child.
Crushers constantly weep when idle.
The Crusher can be heard emitting a noise similar to laughter after its death.
The Crusher was first featured in the “Face the Unknown” trailer, with it barely visible in the reflection of Private Teddy Snuggles's eye.
Correzioni
Fixed an issue where Wretches and Crushers could clip through the floors of certain structures.
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: All Fleshmobs generally have massive appendages one can call "arms". It uses them to bludgeon, rip or crush beyond recognition any living being that it happens to see.
Fleshmobs, seething mounds of bone and blubber, will often charge at the nearest foe, using their immense weight to trample infantry to paste and smash aside vehicles as if they were toys.

s: Fleshmobs spawn naturally throughout the map near POIs, in patrols, and via enemy reinforcements. Their quantity in a given spawn condition increases with higher difficulties.
On planets where the Appropriators and Vote Snatchers subfactions are active, the Fleshmobs are completely absent.
Fleshmobs lumber aimlessly throughout the map alongside Voteless and
s, can be found guarding certain areas, or appear via reinforcements. Upon detecting any SEAF asset or Helldiver, based on their current proximity, Fleshmobs will initiate one of three behaviors:
<15 meters: Slowly walk toward targets and swipe at them when in range.
15-30 meters: Enter an aggressive state, moving quicker toward targets whilst constantly flailing their numerous arms around, knocking back Helldivers and destroying nearby objects.
30+ meters: Perform a short windup in which they roar with their arms spread out and begin charging at their target at high speed, similar to a
. This ragdolls and heavily damages Helldivers.
The Fleshmob is an incredibly durable enemy that should be killed through pure DPS due to its very large health pool and having no fatal parts.

The upper head flesh chunks of the Fleshmob's body transfer 150% damage to main. As overkill damage can transfer through these heads, high alpha damage application to these head hit-zones can result in significant boosts in damage applied. This is most applicable on weapons such as the
on TOTAL mode, where a single well-aimed salvo can "one-shot" the Fleshmob.
When factoring the 25% durability and 150% damage multiplier of the Fleshmob's head flesh chunks, a Variable in TOTAL mode would deal 5,047 damage.
The Fleshmob is immune to flinching via gunfire and has an extremely high stagger resistance that cannot be matched by any loadout weapon.
Destroying all the Fleshmob's heads will not instantly kill it, but it does deal bonus damage to the main body, accelerating its death.
The Fleshmob has incredibly high stun resistance. This resistance is pushed even further during its charge state; the only armaments that can stun a Fleshmob during this state are the
and
Whilst not charging and with no SEAF asset within 15 meters, the Fleshmob can be stunned by the
(Stun Ammo) and
The

grenade, when stuck on a Fleshmob, is able to interrupt a charge and stun it for almost the full grenade stun duration time; after the last grenade blast, the Fleshmob will continue its charge unless the Helldiver dives to the side to cancel it.
Breaking a Fleshmob's arms disables its swing attack, forcing it to resort strictly to charge attacks.
Breaking its legs will not slow it down or disable its charge.
High-damage, explosive, and shrapnel weapons are the most effective at dealing with Fleshmobs. Examples include the
(Flak Ammo), and
While slightly less deadly, the
can kill a Fleshmob in 4 shots.
The
possesses high explosion damage and can kill a Fleshmob in 3 shots. With perfect accuracy, one magazine can kill two Fleshmobs and deal healthy damage to a third.
For primary weapons, options include the
and
The lack of armor and the large size of Fleshmobs allows many high rate-of-fire (ROF) weapons such as the
, and
to excel at dealing large amounts of burst damage.
weaponry can be particularly effective as it can divert its attention away from Helldivers, even while charging.
Fire damage weapons are very effective against it due to its x1.80 fire damage vulnerability.

Like other large enemies, Fleshmobs are completely immune to impact from the M-102 Fast Reconnaissance Vehicle. Running into one will stop the vehicle and sometimes deal enough damage to make the FRV explode.
The Fleshmob has a unique attack animation that flips the FRV upside down when the vehicle is too close to it.
While charging, the Fleshmob will continue to chase the FRV even after Helldivers have exited the vehicle; this can be a useful diversion in some situations.
It is possible to dive out of the way of a Fleshmob’s charge. However, the Fleshmob can still occasionally hit the Helldiver even if said Helldiver has dived out of the way.

A day before its official release, the Fleshmob was teased by Major Truth, an Arrowhead affiliate roleplaying as an in-universe social media user, who posted camera footage of a Fleshmob roaming the streets of a Colony.
Fleshmob are the only Large-class enemy that spawns on Difficulty 1 (Trivial).
What appears to be a cow skull is embedded into the front of the Fleshmob. This may be a reference to the common trope of aliens abducting and experimenting on cows.

As of version 1.003.000, a bug affects Fleshmobs which causes them to phase through terrain and appear at the topmost geometry through walls. This is most noticeable in Megacity biomes where there are many sharp angles present in map geometry.
Modifiche
Increased durable damage
Durable damage of Swing and Bludgeon increased by 25
Correzioni
Fleshmobs are no longer able to clip through various objects when charging.
Fleshmobs now can deal damage to vehicles.
Modifiche
Targeting the faces deals extra damage to its main health, effectively creating weak spots

Main health decreased from 6,000 to 5,000
Most health zones are slightly more durable
Main durability increased from 25% to 40%
Arms durability increased from 25% to 40%
Legs durability increased from 25% to 40%
Stomach & Lower Back chunks durability increased from 25% to 40%
Slightly less vulnerable to fire to balance health decrease
Fire damage multiplier reduced from 200% to 180%

Slightly harder to set on fire
Minimum ignition threshold increased from 4 to 4.5
Arc damage multiplier reduced from 200% to 180%

Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: Feared greatly, the Disintegration Beamer is a devastating weapon that fires a rippling beam of blinding blue light from its eye, vaporizing infantry and tanks alike, leaving only charred and torn-up terrain in its wake.

The Disintegration Beamer is connected to the eye of the Harvester, which, when shattered, amplifies the beam it fires as it becomes unstable, which serves to highlight the sheer danger this living engine presents.
The Tesla Ripper fires an arc of searing electricity from the Harvester's eye which rips apart its targets upon impact.

s: The Harvester may be encountered in patrols, guarding Monoliths, and can be summoned as part of Illuminate reinforcements. They do not spawn on planets occupied by Vote Snatchers.

Harvesters do not deploy their shields until alerted. In combat, their main attack is a sweeping disintegration beam which they charge for a small moment before firing, near-instantaneously killing Helldivers. At close range, Harvesters will instead discharge an equally deadly arc of electricity from their eye-mounted Tesla Ripper.
Although they are not as healthy as other towering units such as
and
, Harvesters are extraordinarily durable in their own way: they are protected by a regenerating energy shield.
Their energy shield is guaranteed to absorb any single instance of damage and can regenerate after breaking. High damage output is necessary to remove this shield and damage the Harvester directly.
The prongs located above and below the Harvester's eye are its shield generators; only one needs to be removed to disable a Harvester's ability to shield permanently.

The eye and the hip joints are the main practical weak points. In general weapons with higher durable damage will see better performance from aiming at the hip joints, whereas ones with lower durable damage can favor aiming for the eye, in particular weapons with heavy penetration and especially ones with spread/recoil since missing the small eye will still yield damage to the main health pool through the carapace and chasis. Anti tank weaponry such as the EAT-17 and
should generally target the eye/head as it is far easier to hit. The
, however, can benefit from a hip joint target since it requires only one missile, rather than two to the head.
Destroying the eye will empower the Disintegration Beamer's damage to 1,800 DPS, from 1,400 DPS, and allow it to taper off into a thinner beam at the end of the Beam's duration.
However, since overkill damage transfers to main the
or
in total-fire mode can 1 shot a Harvester to the eye. But even if you miss and hit the carapace it'll kill the Harvester.
Explosive weapons that produce shrapnel, such as the
and the
in flak mode, are especially effective at cheaply removing a Harvester's shield with only one or two shots.
It is important to note the complete explosion immunity that Harvesters have across their exterior body parts. This renders them highly resistant to stratagems like the
and immune to damage from purely explosive weapons whose AP is below AP 4, until their carapace is broken.

The Harvester possesses some of the deadliest weaponry of any enemy in the game; even a graze from their Disintegration Beamer can bring any Helldiver to death's doorstep, and its Tesla Ripper's arc attack is capable of killing multiple teammates with one shot.
Said arc attack has far better targeting, but can only be used at close range, and Harvesters cannot easily close the distance to their target.
The M-102 Fast Reconnaissance Vehicle and
or
exosuits are more vulnerable to Harvesters due to their large frame, though their large health pool is enough to survive a few seconds of direct fire.
Even after being eliminated, the corpse and especially the detached legs falling onto Helldivers can be fatal.
Continuous
attacks are capable of halting the fighting capabilities of a Harvester, provided the shield has been broken.
Same however cannot be said when using
: Harvester will continue moving around and is also capable using its laser in close range. (NOTE: Support ticket pending to inquire if this intentional.)
The legs have several fatal weak points (hip joints, thighs, shins, feet) all which are only protected by AV 3 armor. Destroying any of these limbs is enough to eliminate a Harvester.
Any anti-tank weapon such as the
, or
will destroy a joint with one rocket.
Both the
and
in APHET mode will destroy a joint with four shots.
Automatic support weapons such as the
, and
do not take long to destroy a joint.
The

armor passive is extremely valuable against Harvesters for its ability to resist lethal amounts of arc damage. This allows the user to remain near Harvesters, who will only use their Tesla Ripper's arc attack for minor damage.
The arc discharge still applies the "Slowed" effect on Helldivers; this effect cannot be negated.
While a stagger force of 40 can stagger the Harvester from anywhere, the Eye and the Carapace Weakspots only have resistance of 30.
As a result, you can interrupt their attacks by using weapons such as the
and
The Harvester appears to be successor to Tripod and its stronger version Strider from Helldivers 1.
However, unlike the versions from the First Galactic War, the Harvester takes the role of an enemy elite, not frontline infantry

Currently, it is unknown whether the name refers to actual harvest process of something. Or if the name is referencing to their uncanny resemblance to Opiliones aka. "harvest spiders / daddy longlegs". Or alternatively to Pholcidae aka. "gyrating (long-legged) spiders".

The Harvester has a resembling appearance to "Fighting Machines/Tripods" from the H.G Wells Novel; War of the Worlds. The design is more or less derived from the Tripods seen in Steven Spielberg's adaptation of War of the Worlds (2005) as it has a more squid-like design and it shows a more recent version of its signature heat ray/laser attack and the energy shields. Players are also calling it Tripods for that reason as well.
Despite its general resemblance to the 2005 movie, the Harvester also shares many design aspects of the 2019 BBC miniseries adaptation of War of The World's depiction of the Tripod
The Harvester appears to be a cybernetic organism rather than a robot, as players can observe what seems to be a destroyed brain when it dies.
Modifiche
Various limbs have had their percent (%) damage transfer to Main increased.
Carapace, Carapace Weakspots, Internals, and Leg Armor.
Hip joints
Durability increased from 50% to 70%.
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: The Plasma Destructor is capable of unloading tens of Plasma Bolts every second, with each Bolt capable of blowing a molten hole the size of a human head into armoured vehicles and reducing anything lesser into burnt vapors.
attacchi.effetti: Anti-Vehicle / (Impact + Blast Damage) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion and Maelstrom)

attacchi.descrizione: A downed Stingray can still present itself as a significant danger as it comes plummeting back down to earth, crashing with such speed and force it can plow through buildings before finally disintegrating.
The Stingray will signify its death with one final, cataclysmic explosion, engulfing anything and everything in superheated gas and molten shrapnel, leaving only smoldering remains.

s: Stingrays spawn intermittently throughout a mission, coming into range from beyond the mission area. They are unable to naturally spawn as part of an enemy patrol, and cannot spawn at the beginning of a mission.
On planets where the Appropriators Appropriators, Mindless Masses Mindless Masses, or Vote Snatchers Vote Snatchers subfactions are active, the Stingrays are completely absent.

Stingrays passively fly around the map at blinding speeds, encircling Helldivers at distances of over 800+ meters. They can be spotted while flying thanks to their bright blue plasma trails that briefly follow behind them. They initially fly 2-3 loops around the entire map before engaging enemies.

They attack by slowing down and descending to an advancing hover, telegraphing a long, bright blue column on the ground which they then progressively bombard with sweeping plasma munitions through their Plasma Destructors, akin to an
. Once this is finished, they resume high-speed flight and attack again once enemies are in its range.
The strafing path of a Stingray is shown by the blue highlight they leave on the ground after descending.
The blue highlight doesn't render on all surfaces, such as caved in terrain from explosions or destroyed buildings that are low to the ground.

Stingrays are extraordinarily fast and fly far outside of the range of most weapons, making them nearly impossible to hit when in-flight. However, their strafing attack slows them down enough to be easily targeted.
The
and
's missiles can lock on to and chase Stingrays seemingly indefinitely. They will not be able to catch up to them mid-flight however, only when the Stingray slows down to attack.
Notably, the
can be used to destroy Stingrays in flight, thanks to its 1000m range, and its hitscan nature. Simply track the Stingrays in first person and pull the trigger. Leading the target is not required.
Explosive or AP 4 armor penetrating Support Weapons such as the
, and
excel at destroying stingrays during their strafing run.
AP 3 armor penetrating support weapons, such as the
or
, are highly efficient at destroying Stingrays.
Activating a SEAF SAM Site is a viable method for shooting down Stingrays, but it is inconsistent and subject to several environmental constraints.
SEAF SAM Sites have a relatively short effective engagement range and cannot target Stingrays during high-speed flight.
SEAF SAM Sites may also be blocked by environmental factors like tall buildings or mountains.

Stingrays are capable of friendly fire, and their sweeping bombardments can be utilized to take out large numbers of Illuminate if lured carefully. Even Grounded Warp Ships can be damaged/destroyed if they are in the target area. But caution should be taken that all 3 types of
are completely IMMUNE to stingray's plasma bolts.
Mobility backpacks such as the
or
allow Helldivers to reliably avoid Stingray bombardments.
Helldivers looking to avoid a Stingray’s Plasma Destructor barrage should run towards the side as this allows for the quickest escape.
A large portion of the Stingray's damage is categorized as explosive. Wearing explosive-resistant armor and or going prone can save you if you don't have time to move out of the way.
By extension, the
or going prone with the
on your back can also save you from these strafing runs.

Anything killed by a Stingray's Plasma Destructor barrage are completely vaporized, leaving no corpse behind. Helldivers killed in such fashion will still drop whatever equipment and samples they had.
Prior to Version 1.003.002, due to a bug, the Stingray was called the "Interloper" when tagged by a player or when killed by one.
Helldivers used to refer to the Stingray with Automaton voicelines when tagging it.
Modifiche
Improved cooldown mechanism of Stingrays when there are a lot of enemies, making their spawn frequency work a bit more as intended.
Modifiche non annunciate
Plasma Destructor Gunpods slight angle armour penetration value increased from AV 3 to AV 4
Modifiche non annunciate
Plasma Destructor Gunpods direct angle armour penetration value increased from AV 3 to AV 5
Correzioni
Fixed two cases where the Stingray enemy would appear to stop or teleport on death
Correzioni
Fixed an issue where Stingray strafing attack sounds could get stuck for a while
Undocumented Fix
Stingrays are no longer called Interloper when tagged or killing a player.
Addition
Added to the game.

Illuminate Overships were first encountered as part of The Great Host, a massive Illuminate invasion fleet that emerged from the Meridian Black Hole shortly after its movement was stopped by Super Earth. While their presence was not felt in the Great Host's advance towards Super Earth, they began descending upon Super Earth, forcing SEAF forces to respond accordingly.
Illuminate Overships spawn in the Take Down Overship Mission. They also appear as part of the skybox on the Void Source Planet.
When the Illuminate Overship is shot, it summons
s on Helldivers. It currently has no other effect on ground assets.
Aiming the barrel of the Planetary Defense Cannon at the closest Port hole of the Overship enables Helldivers to 1-shot the target once the shields have been disabled.

The Overship's Shield can begin to regenerate if the Helldivers assigned to it's assault take too long rearming and firing the Planetary Defense Cannon between shots, which will require additional shells to be fired in order to deactivate the shield again.
While the shield is still intact, if 20 seconds pass without the shield taking damage, it will begin to regenerate at a rate of 500 health per second.
Once the shield has fallen, it will reappear after 60 seconds and start to regenerate, assuming the Overship hasn't been destroyed by then.
Overships are the first enemy capital ship with an in-game model, with the first one shown being the unnamed Automaton spaceship.
Overships are the first enemy in the game to have an Armor Value higher than AV 6.
Overships vaguely resemble jellyfish in their anatomy and movement, similarly to the rest of the Illuminate's "sea creature" thematic.
It is possible to use either support, primary, or secondary weapons to destroy the shield on the overship, provided the weapon has enough range.
By extension, shooting the overship with lesser weapons will still make it call Warp Ships to the location of the player who did that.

The glowing ports under the cap of the ship are weakpoints, comparable to the glowing doors on landed warp ships. Shooting this glowing port with the Planetary Defense Cannon will instantly destroy the ship.
Modifiche
Illuminate Overships can now only be destroyed by the Planetary Defence Cannon.
Main armor increased from AV 8 to AV 10
Port armor increased from AV 8 to AV 10
Modifiche non annunciate
Main health increased from 6,001 to 18,001
Port health increased from 500 to 1,500
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: Each fitted with a powerful spotlight, the ventrally-mounted Disintegration Culverins, upon detecting a target, unleash sapphire-coloured beams towards it, scything up streets and swiftly immolating infantry and vehicles alike.

With ten such Generators dotted across the Leviathan. These devices are capable of dropping gigantic, unstable Plasma Bombs which fall upon any target the Leviathan passes over, flattening even fortified structures.

s: Leviathans spawn beyond the mission area, similarly to the
. Up to 5 Leviathans may appear at any time on Difficulty 8 (Impossible) and above.
They will exclusively spawn within the Megacities of planets with the Leviathan Blockade Operation Modifier.

The Leviathan hovers above the battlefield at a variable altitude. It attacks any Helldiver, SEAF Soldier, or Civilian with four ventral Disintegration Culverins and ten Plasma Bomb Generators. Said Generators only drop their payload on enemies directly below or near the Leviathan.
A Leviathan's Disintegration Culverin turrets can be destroyed by any AV 4 AP or higher Support Weapon, drastically lowering the Leviathan's lethality.
The
and
are very effective at this, destroying the turrets in a single shot.
Given their tough armor and massive health pool, Anti-Tank options such as the
, and
are favorable against Leviathans.
Destroying the Fins or Tail of the Leviathan will expose its internals (marked by spewing blue flames), which are AV 4 armor, and can be damaged by Heavy Armor Penetrating weaponry like the
or

The Leviathan's Disintegration Culverins are extremely lethal, doing 400 damage per second. A single one is capable of killing a Helldiver within half a second, and multiple beams often focus on the same target. Therefore, it is advised to stay on the move when under fire from it.
While difficult and requiring precise positioning, it is possible to destroy a Leviathan with a single
or
Smoke Strategems such as the
or
can be very useful to block a Leviathan's line of sight, preventing them from targeting Helldivers.
If a beam is already targeting a Helldiver, then it will continue doing so, even if the line of sight is blocked by smoke.
As with other large enemies such as the
, the falling wreckage of a Leviathan can damage or kill Helldivers caught underneath it. Helldivers should be prepared to quickly move out of the way if shooting at one directly overhead.
Using Exosuits, M-102 Fast Reconnaissance Vehicles, and Emplacement Stratagems is ill-advised due to how easily they can be destroyed by a Leviathan, very likely killing the Helldiver in the process.
Leviathans bear resemblance to certain Artiopods, also known as Trilobites (and close relatives), like for example Aglaspis or Pseudosaukianda.

The Leviathan's namesake is derived from the Bible, in which it is described as a fire-breathing sea monster clad in impenetrable scales, in line with its in-game portrayal of having tremendous aerial artillery power and being heavily armored.
It is possible, after strenuous effort, to climb onto the back of the Leviathan; the player won't receive any damage when standing above it.

The Leviathan appears to be a cybernetic organism. When their head weakpoint is destroyed, organic-looking appendages can be seen jutting out of it, rather than the hull cracking or catching fire. Additionally, rather than mechanical sounds, it appears to wince in pain whenever its weakpoints are destroyed, or it is killed. Additionally, when it dies, blue fluid similar to Illuminate blood will burst from the Leviathan.
Modifiche
Now equipped with beam-based weaponry
Leviathans will not show up in missions outside of cities
Modifiche
The Leviathans no longer cause ragdolling and deal less impulse damage to vehicles.
Adjusted spawn rates, so you encounter less per mission.
Added an additional 1 second delay between shots for target locking.
Leviathan cannons can now be destroyed.
Modifiche
Projectile damage was reduced from 1,500 to 350.
Explosion damage and radius from turret shots increased.
Modifiche
Leviathans no longer targets power generators in defense missions.
Addition
Added to the game.
Warp Ships come in three variations: Grounded, Airborne, and Landing.
Grounded Warp Ships, which act as enemy spawners, have their own dedicated page.
Airborne Warp Ships function similarly to Automaton
, flying in once reinforcements have been called in by a
, and projecting a tractor beam from their circular underside that directly teleports Illuminate forces to the ground.
Landing Warp Ships are similar to Airborne Warp Ships, but after landing reveal a door weak-spot similar to Grounded Warp Ship. They are only found in Repel Invasion Fleet.
Reinforcement Warp Ships are significantly weaker, and can be neutralized in manners similar to Dropships.
One rocket from the
or
will immediately destroy an unshielded airborne Warp Ship. (The latter is limited to direct hits to the fuselage)
Warp Ships have armor on the sides which can be stripped away after sustaining enough damage. Hitting the sides of an airborne Ship is highly ill-advised.
An airborne Warp Ship's shields are identical to its grounded counterpart. They must be destroyed before the main body can be damaged.
Activating a SEAF SAM Site is one possible method of destroying a Warp Ship.

Prior to the 1.002.200 update, SEAF SAM Sites were capable of destroying a Warp Ship with a single missile hit, regardless of the impact location. After this update, Warp Ships in flight were granted protective shields similar to those deployed during landing, which prevents most single-shot kills. As a result, SAM Sites generally require one missile to disable the shield and another to inflict lethal damage.
In the current version, a single-hit destruction of a Warp Ship is still technically possible under specific conditions:
The missile must impact the shield section that spatially overlaps with the antigravity ring (The ring identified in the Anatomy table as the Fuselage).
The direct hit damage will first deplete the Illuminate shield. Since the Warp Ship does not experience a stun effect after shield break, it continues advancing.

The missile’s explosion point then resolves inside the model of the Warp Ship. Because the antigravity ring possesses an ExDR of 100%, only internal explosions are effective. The overlap results in the explosion damaging the antigravity ring, instantly destroying the Warp Ship.

Note: When SAM Sites are positioned too far away to reliably hit the antigravity ring, it is recommended that Helldivers employ handheld anti-tank weapons. These can capitalize on the brief vulnerability window created after the SAM breaks the Warp Ship’s shield to take down Warp Ships.
Modifiche
Now have the same shields that their grounded counterparts have.
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: The result of Terminid exposure to toxic chemicals. The mouth of the Bile Spitter has mutated to an almost crossbow-like mechanism, allowing them to fire highly corrosive globules at any unfortunate foes in its way, melting holes in even steel armor.
attacchi.effetti: Acid / (1.5x Damage to Exosuits) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion) / 3/s Acid DPS (4.0s) / (Via Blast Damage)

attacchi.descrizione: Their entire stomach dedicated to the production of baleful bile, it is perhaps not shocking that Bile Spitters are effectively dog-sized water balloons ready to violently burst at the slightest puncture, showering anything nearby with highly corrosive bile.
attacchi.effetti: Acid / (1.5x Damage to Exosuits) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion) / 3/s Acid DPS (4.0s) / (Via Blast Damage)

s: Bile Spitters can be found on Caustic Strain-invaded planets, where they replace
s and
s, spawning from Bug Breaches, within patrols, or from Bug Holes. They can also be found guarding Bug Nests, Minor Places of Interest, and Objectives,

Bile Spitters will simply approach Helldivers, climbing over terrain and obstacles in an attempt to spit their bile. Bile Spitters will spit every three seconds once a Helldiver is within 15m of them. Their bile slows Helldivers' movement speed while dealing a mild damage-over-time effect. Upon death, Bile Spitters will cause a small explosion of bile, dealing damage to nearby Terminids and Helldivers.
Bile Spitters are able to release a cloud of pheromones into the air that causes a Bug Breach.
Due to their low health, Bile Spitters can easily be dispatched by any weapon.
The
and explosive weaponry can be effective against swarms of Bile Spitters or other small Terminids.
Groups of Bile Spitters can easily be killed by one exploding, causing a chain reaction.
Bile Spitters, along with
s and
s, will almost always appear on Terminid Launch ICBM Missions.

We broke out the bug strain that spawns Bile Warriors, Spewers, Scavengers, which could randomly become active on a mission, into its own bug strain that now is controlled by the Game Masters and will have its own visualization to show when it’s active just like other bug strains like Rupture, Spore Burst etc.

Bile Spit angled armor penetration increased
Direct Angle armor penetration increased from AP 3 to AP 4
Slight Angle armor penetration increased from AP 3 to AP 4
Large Angle armor penetratoin increased from AP 3 to AP 4

attacchi.descrizione: Larger and far more refined than those of the Pouncer, the Hunter's mantis-like arms are more akin to talons, slashing through armour like paper whilst its serrated edge leaves gaping wounds and shattered bones upon the hapless victim.

Much like the Pouncer, the Hunter uses its highly developed legs to leap great distances and to ambush unsuspecting targets. Such attacks are quick and violent, using its mass to drive its oversized talons into the victim.

Hunters have developed long, weaponized tongues. Said tongues are coiled within their mouth with great tension and additionally laced with corrosive toxins. These tongues then spring out like a whip and lash the target with envenomed burns.

s: Hunters can be first found on Difficulty 2 (Easy). They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, guarding Bug Nests and Objectives, or from specific Bug Holes.
Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), they can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest.

Hunters will mainly attempt to flank and surround Helldivers, moving faster than other Terminids. While approaching Helldivers, they are able to quickly strafe sideways or perform short jumps, which can throw off a Helldiver's aim. Upon reaching about 15-20m from Helldivers, they will pounce onto them, dealing damage, and can quickly follow up with another attack from their claws or tongues.
Hunters can use their tongues at short-medium range, which causes an Acid burn that will slow Helldivers; they can use their claws at extremely close range, usually when next to a Helldiver.
Hunters are able to release a cloud of pheromones into the air that causes a Bug Breach.
Hunters are relatively weak when compared to
s and other medium-sized Terminids. Shooting their heads will quickly dispatch them.
As the Hunter's Health Pool is very low, a single ignition from any source will kill them within seconds. Hunters are easily ignited at long range with the use of the
, and
, thus giving a Helldiver the ability to wipe out a large Hunter Patrol with a short sweep of the laser across the patrol.
Shooting the legs of a Hunter will greatly slow them and prevent them from performing a pounce.
This can also be done by shooting off their wings.
Hunters are weak if encountered alone, but should be prioritized within swarms over other medium-sized Terminids, due to their ability to quickly approach and pounce Helldivers.
Using a melee attack will momentarily stun the Hunters and knock them back. Though difficult, Helldivers can melee Hunters mid-pounce to prevent their attack.

attacchi.descrizione: Living up to their name, the Scavenger's pincers are capable of pinning down and picking apart the remains of prey that had already been mauled by larger Terminids with alarming efficiency, easily stripping flesh from armour and bone alike.

s: Scavengers can be found on all difficulties, spawning from Bug Breaches, within patrols, guarding Bug Nests and Objectives, or from Bug Holes.
Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), they can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest.
Scavengers will simply approach Helldivers, climbing over terrain and obstacles in an attempt to attack with their claws. After striking, they will retreat a short distance before approaching again.
Rarely, and when a Helldiver is out of its reach, they will dig underground, only to suddenly emerge and attack the Helldiver.
Scavengers are able to release a cloud of pheromones into the air that causes a Bug Breach.
Due to their low health, Scavengers can easily be dispatched by any weapon.
Individual Scavengers can be safely killed with a single melee attack to the head, which conserves ammunition.
When encountering a patrol or group of Terminids, it is recommended to kill Scavengers quickly before they can cause a Bug Breach.
The AX/LAS-5 "Guard Dog" Rover and explosive weaponry can be effective against swarms of Scavengers or other small Terminids.

attacchi.descrizione: Taking to the skies, the Shriekers act akin to ancient harriers, swooping down towards their prey at great speed. They use their sharpened claws and wingtips to slice and slash their way through their target, at times even causing outright decapitation.

s: Shriekers can be found spawning from Shrieker Nests, which begin appearing on Difficulty 4 (Challenging). Helldivers that are roughly within 150m will cause a Nest to begin spawning Shriekers.
Starting on Difficulty 5 (Hard), operations may have the Roving Shriekers Operation Modifier, which spawns groups of Shriekers that patrol the map.

Once a Shrieker has marked a Helldiver as their target, they circle and dive into fly-by-slashing Helldivers with their razor-sharp claws. Generally, these blade-winged Terminids always target and hit the arms and torso of Helldivers, but they have been known to decapitate as well.
Upon death, a Shrieker's corpse will deal damage to anything it falls onto.
Shriekers lack any sort of armor and can be taken out by most weaponry.
Energy-based laser weaponry, such as the
and the
, have extremely long range and instant damage, allowing them to easily track and damage Shriekers.
Shotguns with spread, such as the
and the
, can damage Shriekers at close to medium range. With the
being one of the best weapons in the game to shoot them down individually.
The
's flak ammo can be used to kill multiple Shriekers at any distance.
The
and
are effective at taking out swarms of Shriekers.
Rocks or physical objects can be used to break line-of-sight from Shriekers, preventing them from attacking in the direction of said obstruction.
Lying prone on the ground will make a Helldiver harder for Shriekers to hit.

Killing a Shrieker in the middle of its dive attack will cause it to plummet directly towards the Helldiver that killed it. Helldivers are advised to move or dive to avoid a Shrieker's corpse dealing unnecessary damage.

Shriekers began to slowly appear during the deployment of the Terminid Control System, a network of Termicide-dispensing towers established across the Barrier Planets as part of Operation Valiant Enclosure. Once the Terminid Control System had been fully activated across all four planets, the presence of Shriekers and Shrieker Nests on Terminid planets increased as a result, without any official acknowledgement by Super Earth.

It would not be until late into the ensuing Major Order to liberate Zagon Prime and Fori Prime that Super Earth would acknowledge the new strain of Terminid. The acknowledgement came in the form of a dispatch where it was claimed that the Termicide had averted a worse evolution, blaming dissidents for their radio silence.

Shriekers were quietly introduced to the game on March 12th, 2024 after the successful completion of Phase III of Operation Valiant Enclosure, and would officially be acknowledged via an in-game intelligence brief on March 21st, 2024.

attacchi.descrizione: Spewer-strains can also rely on their enlarged forelegs to swing and slam would-be-attackers. While not their most devastating attack, they are still more than capable of crushing bone and tearing flesh with each blow.

Much like their cousins, the fluids within the Bile Spewer's rump are highly volatile. When finally punctured, the Spewer will explode violently, showering foes with extremely corrosive bile that reduces them to goo puddles in seconds.

s: Bile Spewers can be found on Caustic Strain-invaded planets. They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, and guarding Objectives, Minor Places of Interests, and Bug Nests.
Bile Spewers approach Helldivers and, at 11- 20 m, will spit their bile at them. At 10m, Bile Spewers will resort to using their front leg to attack Helldivers.

A lethal shot to a Bile Spewer's butt region will cause it to explode, dealing damage to nearby Terminids and Helldivers. Dead Bile Spewers with their butts intact can still explode once enough damage is dealt to them. Destroying legs will slow them down, further slowing them for each leg destroyed.
Starting on Difficulty 6 (Extreme), at around 30m, Bile Spewers will begin firing two bile bombs into the air, which can potentially fall and explode on Helldivers.

Bile Spewers are best dealt with by shooting their head, as that is considered their weak spot, though this requires weaponry with medium armor penetration on difficulties Difficulty 6 (Extreme) and above. They can also be killed efficiently by targeting their spinal plates or butts with explosives. Ballistic weapons can damage their butts, but will require many shots to destroy it as it is very durable.
The mouth is unarmored and vulnerable to any weapon, and for weapons with light penetration this is the optimal way to kill it.
Weapons that stagger, such as the
and
, can interrupt their spewing attacks.

Bile Spewers are almost always present on Launch ICBM mission types, but also have a chance to be present on several other mission types. These include Retrieve Valuable Data, Blitz Search And Destroy/Terminid, and Eradicate Terminid Swarm.
The butt of the spewer has a high durable rating but no explosive resistance. This means explosive or plasma weapons can prove very effective against them.

s: Hive Guards can be first found on Difficulty 2 (Easy). They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, and guarding Objectives and Bug Nests.
Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), they can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest.

Hive Guards will approach Helldivers, climbing over terrain and obstacles in an attempt to attack with their claws at close range. They can strafe sideways, and will attempt to cut off Helldivers trying to run past them. Upon being shot a few times, be that nearby or directly, they will hunker down into a crouching stance, bringing their front legs closer to their body for about three seconds. If a Helldiver continuously fires their weapon, Hive Guards will continue to crouch until the Helldiver stops firing.
Similar to

s, Hive Guards can go into a "berserk" state after their heads begin to bleed out (specifically, when it releases green fluids from its head). This will briefly increase its movement speed before they die.
Hive Guards are able to release a cloud of pheromones into the air that causes a Bug Breach.
Naturally, AP 3 Medium armor penetrating weaponry and explosives are the best for dispatching Hive Guards.
If hitting its AV 1 body is not a viable option in a situation, AP 3 armor penetrating weaponry and explosives are the best for dispatching Hive Guards.
Two Helldivers with AP 2 armor penetrating weaponry can easily exploit the Hive Guard's defenses by firing at its head to suppress it while another Helldiver flanks it.
The Hive Guard is still vulnerable from the front while crouching; there is a small gap between its front legs and head, where the main body may be struck.
Hive Guards can also be killed by destroying their 2 claws.
Its "berserk" state is rarely seen, as Hive Guards will prioritize crouching after being shot multiple times in the head.
When it isn't crouching, its legs can be amputated by shooting the unarmored section behind armor, lowering its protection.

attacchi.descrizione: Spewer-strains can also rely on their enlarged forelegs to swing and slam would-be-attackers. While not their most devastating attack, they are still more than capable of crushing bone and tearing flesh with each blow.

As they are filled to the brim with nutrient fluids, should the surprisingly thick skin of a Spewers rump be punctured, one should expect to be showered in gallons of highly corrosive stomach contents that inflict severe burns.

s: Nursing Spewers can be first found on Difficulty 3 (Medium). They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, and guarding Objectives and Bug Nests.
Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), Nursing Spewers can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest.
Occasionally, Nursing Spewers will replace Bile Spewers.
Nursing Spewers
Nursing Spewers act similarly to Bile Spewers. However, upon spawning in, they will emit a thin spore cloud around them, obscuring smaller Terminids such as
s. Killing them will dissipate the spore cloud. Unlike Bile Spewers, Nursing Spewers are unable to fire bile bombs into the air on any difficulty.
Nursing Spewers have AV 2 armor on all difficulties, unlike Bile Spewers' AV 3 armor on Difficulty 6 (Extreme) and above.

They are best killed by shooting their head, which is their weak spot. As they have light armor, every weapon can deal damage to it, with Support Weapons being especially effective at killing them quickly.
A single well-placed grenade near or under the Spewer will often one-shot or nearly kill it. The
grenade is especially effective, and can even kill 2 adjacent Spewers with a well-placed throw.
The butt has a high durable rating but no explosive damage resistance, making any weapon that is explosive or plasma based a good choice against spewers.
Weapons that stagger, such as the
and
, can interrupt their spewing attacks.

s: Rupture Spewers first appear on Difficulty 6 (Extreme) on planets with the Rupture Strain Rupture Strain present, replacing all
s and some
s. They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, or guarding Bug Nestes and Objectives.
The Rupture Spewer acts similarly to

s before detecting enemies. Once engaged in combat, if far enough away from Helldivers, it will burrow into the ground and loosely follow its target before re-emerging its head and shooting either a short-range bile breath, or a longer ranged three-round burst of bile projectiles if close/far enough from its target, respectively.

Rupture Spewers can burrow underground to remain hidden and avoid non-explosive ordnance. They typically engage in hit-and-run tactics against their enemies. As a result, they can be difficult to pin down and eliminate.
Explosives forcibly flush Rupture Spewers out of their burrowing state, proving highly valuable in preventing Rupture Spewers from further advancing and attacking.
Rupture Spewers that expose their head upon emerging aren’t affected by stagger effects such as the
, and will continue attacking unimpeded unless killed.

As with other Spewer variants, Rupture Spewers often spawn in patrols with one another, making it possible to quickly dispatch such groups by detonating their sacks and damaging each other in a chain reaction via their death explosion.

Rupture Spewers are best dealt with by shooting their head, as that is considered their weak spot, though this requires weaponry with AP 3 armor penetration. They can also be killed efficiently by targeting their spinal plates or butts with explosives. Ballistic weapons can damage their butts, but will require many shots to destroy them, as they are very durable.
The mouth is AV 0 and vulnerable to any weapon, though it can be difficult to hit due to its size. Weapons such as the
or
can damage it with less difficulty.

and
The Rupture Spewers can still be hit by gas, fire, and explosions while underground.

s: Rupture Warriors first appear on Difficulty 6 (Extreme) on planets with the Rupture Strain Rupture Strain present, replacing Warriors completely. They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, guarding Bug Nests and Objectives, or from specific Bug Holes.
The Rupture Warrior is capable of burrowing and emerging from the ground, often taking Helldivers by surprise if they aren't paying attention.
Rupture Warrior Specific

Rupture Warriors that are burrowing will emerge from the ground within moments of closing within ~3m of a Helldiver, often directly under said diver's feet, and immediately deal damage if the player is in front of them when this happens.

If a Helldiver is within range of the Rupture Warrior to start to surface but then runs away, the Rupture Warrior will immediately lunge at them to try and close the distance, making it harder to avoid damage if said player remains roughly in the direction they were tunneling.

Rupture Warrior that are surfacing deal 2 separate instances of damage, the first immediately upon protruding their front claws out of the ground, the second approximately upon pulling their hind legs out. This later point does not visually indicate an attack and may cause players attempting to melee the unit to take unexpected damage.
It is possible to evade their burrowing attack if the following conditions are met:
They have fully burrowed and are underground for at least ~3-4s.
The player sprinted right above and past them.
Perform this too early, and they will stay burrowed and then will hit the player with rigorous tracking.
Helldivers can either trick or force Rupture Warriors into surfacing by sprinting past them or by shooting explosive ordnance on top of them, such as a

It should be noted that Rupture Warriors often burrow in groups, and it can be difficult to differentiate a single burrowing unit from a clustered group, potentially causing unattentive or overly eager divers to take significant damage.

Rupture Warriors are more dangerous towards mission hosts, emerging from the ground and attacking much closer to the hosting Helldiver than non-hosting Helldivers. Therefore, it is recommended to bring either heavy armor,
passive armor, or wear an
General
Rupture Warrior, unlike their normal
counterparts, have AV 3 armor on their heads and claws in exchange for less main health.
The front legs and tail (part of Main in the Anatomy section) of a Rupture Warrior protrude slightly above its head and are vulnerable to AP 2 penetration.
Their burrowing animation exposes their entire body/tail for a moment, offering a brief chance for Light penetration Ballistic weapons to disrupt or kill.

The fastest way to kill a Rupture Warrior is by destroying its head, though destroying it will cause it to enter a "berserk" state and increase its movement speed before bleeding out. Helldivers can shoot the Warrior more to fully kill it, or they can avoid it until it fully bleeds out.
Destroying any of its legs will prevent its movement speed increase.
