s). They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, guarding Bug Nests and Objectives, or from Bug Holes.
Spore Burst Warriors behave identically to regular
s. However, upon death, they will explode, causing damage to Helldivers who are near them.
Spore Burst Strain Specific
Upon death, Spore Burst Terminids will release a cloud of spores, damaging nearby Helldivers, disrupting vision, and buffing nearby Spore Burst Terminids.
When entering a cloud of spores (created by another Spore Burst Terminid’s death or through the
’s bile spew), Spore Burst Terminids will gain a significant increase in speed, allowing them to close the gap on Helldivers.
Gas and Fire weapons such as the
, and
can slow and deter Spore Burst Terminids from a Helldiver's position, allowing them to more easily avoid attacks and spore explosions.
Spore Burst Terminids do not release their spores if they die while burning. This makes continuous laser weapons (such as the
) and Fire weapons useful to avoid enraging a horde of Spore Burst Terminids.
The Spore Burst Warrior specifically will also not release spores if bleeding out kills it after its head is destroyed.
Crowd control Stratagems such as
, and
are especially effective at slowing down Spore Burst Terminids, preventing them from using their increased speed to engage Helldivers.
Using melee weapons against Spore Burst Terminids is not recommended, as repeated spore explosions will stagger and eventually kill an ignorant Helldiver.
Despite its passive effect,
with the
or
passives are not very effective against Spore Burst Terminids, as they provide limited utility against the already low damage spore explosions.
General
Spore Burst Warriors can be killed with any weapon, but high fire rate or explosive weaponry can quickly take out groups of them.

The fastest way to kill a Spore Burst Warrior is by destroying its head, though destroying it will cause it to enter its "berserk" state. Helldivers can shoot the Spore Burst Warrior more to fully kill it, or they can avoid it until it fully bleeds out.
Destroying any of its legs will prevent its movement speed increase.
Spore Burst Warriors are capable of causing Bug Breaches even without their head, though they will likely bleed out before fully calling it in.
Spore Burst Warriors are generally slow, but Helldivers should remain wary of their strafing capabilities, which may hinder a retreat from other Terminids.

Warriors will simply approach Helldivers, climbing over terrain and obstacles in an attempt to attack with their claws at close range. They can strafe sideways, and will attempt to cut off Helldivers trying to run past them. When their head is destroyed, Warriors will enter a "berserk" state, where they gain increased movement speed but continuously bleed out.
Rarely, and when a Helldiver is out of its reach, it will dig underground, then suddenly emerge and attack the Helldiver.
Warriors are able to release a cloud of pheromones into the air that causes a Bug Breach.
Warriors can be killed with any weapon, but high fire rate or explosive weaponry can quickly take out groups of them.

The fastest way to kill a Warrior is by destroying its head, though destroying it will cause it to enter its "berserk" state. Helldivers can shoot the Warrior more to kill it, or they can avoid it until it fully bleeds out.
Destroying any of its legs will prevent its movement speed increase.
Dealing enough damage will cause the Warrior to explode in a shower of green goo, destroying its corpse. This can be seen when using grenades, Arc weapons, or some stratagems.
Warriors are capable of causing Bug Breaches even without their head, though they will likely bleed out before fully calling it in.
Warriors are generally slow, but Helldivers should remain wary of their strafing capabilities, which may hinder a retreat from other Terminids.

Much like a bull, the Alpha Commander is capable of aggressively charging the foe. Those unlucky enough to not get out of its way will find themselves knocked down and brutally trampled underfoot.

Alpha Commanders behave similarly to

Alpha Commanders can be taken out with the same tactics used against the

While any weapon is capable of killing Alpha Commanders, AP 3 armor-penetrating weapons and explosives are more effective against them due to their AV 2 armored heads and high durability.

The charge will deal damage upon contact and can knock down Helldivers, potentially inflicting a concussive effect onto them. The Brood Commander's charge can be dodged or can be stopped by colliding with terrain or a larger entity, like a

attacchi.descrizione: Living up to its name, the Charger can simply use its immense, multi-ton mass to knock down, trample and crush foes, often doing so with such force that not even vehicles are safe from its wrath, being staggered or knocked aside as it rampages through.

Alteratively, the Charger may instead leverage its mass to simply crush whatever being (or thing) happens to be in front of it, leaving humans as nothing more than crumpled heaps and vehicles akin to crushed drink cans as it bears its entire weight.

s: Starting on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), Chargers can spawn from Bug Breaches, patrolling the map with other Terminids, and guarding Objectives. Higher difficulties will increase how often they can spawn. In addition, they can be found guarding Minor Places of Interest, where they can be sometimes found burrowed.

Starting on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission), Chargers can be found guarding heavy Bug Nests and Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive)'s mega Nests. In addition, Chargers have a chance of being replaced by its variants, the
and the
. Higher difficulties will increase this chance.
When the game attempts to spawn a
on missions with

es active, such as through Bile Titan Bug Holes, a normal Charger is spawned instead. This makes it possible to encounter regular Chargers on Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive), where their spawns are otherwise replaced entirely by their tougher variants.

When encountered outside of a Bug Breach, Chargers will usually remain still. Upon noticing Helldiver movement or sounds caused by them, they will turn to face where a Helldiver or the sound was. Chargers will signify when they will begin attacking with a roar, and will often immediately begin charging towards Helldivers. In patrols, they will also stop moving to turn towards any nearby movement or sounds. When spawning from a Bug Breach, they will immediately be aggressive and seek any nearby Helldivers to trample.

Upon initiating a charge, Chargers will not stop until it charges past a Helldiver, collides with solid terrain, or even other Chargers. Helldivers hit by a charge will be knocked down/sent flying and will often be inflicted with a concussive effect. Chargers will also attempt to attack Helldivers up close with its front legs.
Helldivers that destroy a Charger's rear or blow off its torso armor will cripple it, slowing its movement and causing it to bleed out.
The Charger can be dodged by moving or diving perpendicular to its movement direction or diagonally towards it as it approaches. Beware of moving too early, as the Charger can make tight turns.
The most straightforward way to dispatch a Charger is firing an anti-tank weapon, such as the
and
, at its head, which will instantly kill it. However, a direct shot to anywhere on its torso with the
or GR-8 Recoilless Rifle will crack open its armor and either kill it (butt shot) or cause it to slowly bleed out.
The exposed flesh from this will also allow any weapon to deal damage to the Charger; damage dealt to the inner flesh has a 300% multiplier to main.
Alternatively, shooting a leg will reveal the Charger's weak flesh. Any weapon can damage the leg flesh, dispatching the Charger fairly quickly.
By positioning behind the Charger and aiming in the direction of its inner flesh, weapons such as the
, and
can fire rounds that penetrate the butt region and inflict direct damage to the inner flesh. This method enables rapid elimination of the Charger.

Destroying a Charger's AV 0 rear will cause it to bleed out over the course of a few seconds. It can be damaged by most weapons, but it is 80% durable with high hp. The best way to get a clean shot on its butt is to wait for them to charge at you and while they're in their recovery animation you unload into their butt.
Due to the high durability the best weapons are explosives.
If one cannot bait the charger to charge one can use the
and "bounce" the grenades underneath it to hit the rear from the front.
With the Charger's AV 4 armor covering most of its body, support weapons such as the
and
can penetrate it for reduced damage. While this is a rather slow way to dispatch a Charger, it can work if no other options are available.
The
APHET rounds can stagger a Charger out of its charge. This can be used to either save a teammate from an untimely demise or to set up an easy kill shot with an
or
if the Charger in question spotted the 'diver.
The
grenade, if stuck to a Charger's head or torso, will instantly kill it upon detonation.
The recommended tactic when using the
is to aim at the Charger's leg armor as it takes fewer total shots to both break the armor and destroy the leg flesh than to aim at the head.
The
is an effective yet risky method of dispatching a Charger, as it can penetrate the Charger's armor as well as the Charger having a 150% fire damage multiplier.
Dropping Hellpods of any kind can strip the armor off a Charger's back, and a direct hit will kill it outright, though this requires some luck or sticking Stratagem beacons onto it.

Chargers tend to hone in on one member of the team at a time. Consider coordinating with other Helldivers to bait a Charger into exposing its head to a squad mate with an anti-tank weapon, or to focus on a specific leg to open up its weak spot.

Leading a Charger into ramming a wall or large rock will cause it to be briefly stunned, providing time for Helldivers to attack or retreat. However, they can traverse smaller rocks and walls, so caution must be exercised. Armor may be damaged and fall off with sufficient amounts of ramming.
While piloting an
, it's generally best to fire a rocket at the head as it will 1 shot.
Hitting a Charger with an
, or

will instantly kill it if it is near the epicenter of the stratagem, or otherwise deal heavy damage to it. Doing this after being noticed by the Charger is incredibly difficult, however, as the Helldiver will need to estimate where the Charger will be after the call-in period is over.
or
can completely stop Chargers in their tracks, allowing for an easy direct hit from an
or the
If a Charger knocks a Helldiver down, it will attempt to finish them off by crushing them with its front legs. This can be avoided by diving out of the way in time.
Using the Eagle Napalm Strike far in front of the Charger and/or leading the Charger through fire is a good strategy to take off much of its health.

Intimidating as they are, it's easy to treat Chargers as the highest threat on the field. However, they attack infrequently, and with enough skill, are easy to dodge. Oftentimes, the true threat of a Charger isn't getting killed by it directly, but by other Terminids, especially
s or
s. Helldivers should consider clearing out or moving away from other smaller Terminids before killing a Charger.
There is an achievement for killing a Charger with a Resupply pod, named "Caught them by Supplies!"
Chargers in Eliminate Chargers missions have an unique idle animation of them digging into the ground using their two front claws

attacchi.descrizione: Befitting their aggression, the Behemoth is capable of cutting open even heavily armoured vehicles with their scythe-like forelegs, such is their weight and strength. Anything lesser than a tank will often be reduced to an unrecognisable mass.

Ultilising their prow-shaped head, the Behemoth Charger is equally capable of doing serious damage by simply ramming whatever is in front of it, knocking down, trampling or swatting aside humans and exosuits alike like mere toys.

, will have a chance of replacing Chargers. Higher difficulties will increase this chance. Like the Charger, Charger Behemoths can spawn from Bug Breaches, patrolling the map with other Terminids, and guarding Objectives. They can also be found guarding heavy Bug Nests, Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive)'s mega Nests, and Minor Places of Interest, where they can sometimes be found burrowed.
Charger Behemoths
. They have slightly more health and durability compared to Chargers.
Charger Behemoths can be dispatched with the same
Despite its increased health, the Charger Behemoth shares many of the same anti-tank weapon breakpoints as the Charger: a direct shot to the torso from the
will instantly dispatch it, while other anti-tank weapons require a headshot. The exposed torso bonus damage that the Charger has also applies to the Charger Behemoth.
The G-123 Thermite grenade, if stuck to the torso, will not instantly dispatch the Charger Behemoth upon detonation. Aim for the head to guarantee an instant kill.

AP 4 penetrating support weapons will deal reduced damage to a Charger Behemoth on most areas of the body, but this is an even slower endeavor than dispatching a regular Charger via this method due to the Behemoth's increased health and durability.
The Charger Behemoth, being a variant of a
, does actually count for the Caught Them By Supplies! achievement. This has been tested on an Eliminate Chargers mission on Difficulty 4 (Challenging) difficulty.

attacchi.descrizione: Striking with the force of an artillery shell at times, the Impaler's chitin-hardened Tentacles are more than capable of tearing a human target into mere chunks and puncturing even tanks with immense force, all with unerring accuracy.

While prefering to strike from afar with its specifically evolved tentacles. Impalers are not unaware of their immense size and strength, which they will happily (and quite clumsily) leverage should the foe get too close to comfort.

s: Impalers can be first found on Difficulty 5 (Hard) as the mission target of the Eliminate Impaler mission.
Starting on Difficulty 6 (Extreme), Impalers can spawn from Bug Breaches and can be found patrolling the map on its own. Higher difficulties will increase how often they can spawn.
Starting on Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive), Impalers can be found guarding Mega Nests.

When encountered outside of a Bug Breach, Impalers will usually remain still. Upon noticing Helldiver movement or sounds caused by them, they will turn to face where a Helldiver or the sound was. When in a combat or encountered in a Bug Breach, Impalers will often immediately burrow its "head," using its three tentacles to attack Helldivers in its line of sight. The tentacles can be damaged to force them to retract. After some time, losing sight of Helldivers, or upon death, Impalers will retract all of their tentacles.
When patrolling, Impalers will also stop moving to turn towards any nearby movement or sounds.
At close range, Impalers can use its frontal weight to crush anything in front of it.
When the Impaler burrows its tentacles to attack, it will expose its unarmored head, which is a weak point that Helldivers should take advantage of to quickly kill it.

Impalers can be easily killed in this state, so locating them is essential in defeating them. Some of the best weapons to dispatch them in this state are support weapons with high durable damage and firepower such as the
, or offensive stratagems such as the
, and

. This can be hard to manage, as Helldivers will have to avoid their tentacles whilst entering the stratagem input, and will have to avoid being knocked over, as this will cause you to drop the stratagem ball on your position.
High DPS weapons such as the
and
can quickly incapacitate an Impaler by targeting their legs once the armor has been destroyed.
When a tentacle has breached the ground to attack Helldivers, it can be damaged. Enough damage will make the Impaler retract the tentacle
This is most useful in emergency situations where a hit is unavoidable or would kill the Helldiver.
Flames are effective at forcing Impalers to retreat their tentacles, and chipping away at their Health, allowing Helldivers to focus on larger threats.
Sentries can target their tentacles, which can force the Impaler to retract them.
The Impaler has a unique interaction when destroying the head armor; it will destroy the RIGHT side torso armor exposing the inner flesh.
The Impaler's legs are covered in armor which can be broken, exposing the vulnerable flesh underneath. If an Impaler does not reveal its head, destroying a leg is the next best way to exterminate it.
Additionally, Helldivers shoot their unarmored underside. However, this part has much more health and typically requires heavy weaponry to be effective.
Impalers are especially dangerous towards vehicles like the M-102 Fast Reconnaissance Vehicle,
and
as their large frames have a hard time avoiding tentacles, and exosuits can easily be dismembered by their attacks.

If Impalers don't expose their faces, Helldivers can walk up to them and bait a melee attack. During the melee animation, the Impaler will lift its head and reveal its mouth—hitting this weak spot with weapons like the
or
can quickly kill it.
While the Impaler itself has a stagger resistance of 50, the tentacles themselves only have a resistance of 30.
As a result, weapons like the
and
are capable of interrupting their attacks.
The Impaler was revealed in the Escalation of Freedom Announcement Trailer on July 23rd, 2024, and appeared in-game on August 6, 2024.
The Impaler shares the same musical theme as the
if it is in combat.
The Impaler has twenty seven eyes hidden behind its tentacles. Thirteen on its right side and fourteen on its left, making it one of the few asymmetrical Terminids in the game.

attacchi.descrizione: Hyper-specialised in stalking and viciously dispatching prey. The Stalker's unique, mantis-like talons are capable of striking with blistering speed, sometimes even bifurcating human targets.

s: Predator Stalkers can be first found on Difficulty 4 (Challenging) on planets invaded by the Predator Strain. Unlike Stalkers, Predator Stalkers do not require a Stalker Lair to spawn, instead spawning normally with other Terminids. They can spawn from Bug Breaches, within patrols, guarding Bug Nests, Objectives, and Minor Places of Interest.

Unlike Stalkers, Predator Stalkers cannot camouflage or attack with their tongues, and instead solely use their claws. They also do not retreat when taking enough damage, and will continuously pursue until it or Helldivers die.
Despite its menacing prefix, Predator Stalkers are individually weaker than Stalkers. However, they, alongside
s, can make any patrol or Bug Breach significantly more dangerous due to their aggressive nature.
Predator Stalkers are unable to inflict the potent knockback of Stalkers, as they are missing their tongue attack. They are able to constantly attack using their claws instead.
Weapons with high stagger are particularly useful against Predator Stalkers, preventing them from attacking.
The
is a very effective weapon against Predator Stalkers, as it deals a high amount of stagger and also deals 25% more incendiary damage to Predator Stalkers.
Explosive weaponry should be carefully used, as while they can stagger Predator Stalkers, they can close the distance too quickly for explosives to be safely used.
The
, and the
can all quickly deal with swarms of Predator Stalkers as long as they have a vantage point.
AX/TX-13 "Guard Dog" Dog Breath can be helpful against Predator Stalkers, as it can confuse and damage any that come near the Helldiver.

Increased durable damage
Addition
Added to the game.

attacchi.descrizione: No less deadly than their unmutated counterparts, the Rupture-strain Charger is capable of smashing aside even reinforced colony walls with its shield-shaped head, as well as any remaining garrison forces unfortunate enough to be in its way.

Leveraging its heavier carapace plates lining its forelegs, the Rupture-strain Charger is more than capable of reducing human-sized targets messy pulps, with anything larger being reduced to scrap as it slams with the force of its immense weight upon target.

Whereas smaller Terminids of the Rupture-Strain merely emerge from the ground in order to ambush their foes, the Rupture-strain Charger bursts out with immense force, throwing about rubble, loose debris and people around like toys.

s: Rupture Charger appear exclusively on planets with the Rupture Strain Rupture Strain present.
The Rupture Charger behaves similarly to a regular Charger with the capability of burrowing and charging Helldivers from underground.
Rupture Chargers can be dispatched with the same
Rupture Chargers have stronger armor values on their head and front legs than any other
variant; AV 5 instead of AV 4.
Rupture Chargers can burrow underground to approach a Helldiver, typically surfacing within 3m of their target before attacking.
Burrowing disturbances caused by Rupture Chargers are larger than other Rupture strain units, making them easy to identify while underground.
Helldivers can trick a Rupture Charger into surfacing at an inopportune angle of attack by quickly sprinting toward/past its burrowed form when close enough.
Burrowing units can be forced to surface by any explosive effect. This includes primary weapons with the 'explosive' trait. such as the
, or
, secondary weapons such as the
or
, and most (but not all) grenade types.
The Rupture Charger can be damaged while burrowing, but only by grenades, gas, and sometimes fire.

attacchi.descrizione: Living up to its name, the Charger can simply use its immense, multi-ton mass to knock down, trample and crush foes, often doing so with such force that not even vehicles are safe from its wrath, being staggered or knocked aside as it rampages through.

Alteratively, the Charger may instead leverage its mass to simply crush whatever being (or thing) happens to be in front of it, leaving humans as nothing more than crumpled heaps and vehicles akin to crushed drink cans as it bears its entire weight.

Its body festooned with pressurized, fruiting spores, the death of a Spore Charger can trigger a secondary reaction to the spores, which all spontaneously release at once, resulting in a massive eruption of mildly corrosive spores around the area.

s: Spore Chargers can be found on planets invaded by the Caustic Strain. Like the Charger, Spore Chargers can spawn from Bug Breaches, patrolling the map with other Terminids. They can also be found guarding heavy Bug Nests, Objectives and Minor Places of Interest, where they can sometimes be found burrowed.
Spore Chargers

Upon death, Spore Chargers will cause a spore explosion, damaging any nearby entities. This doesn't always happen, though. Spore Chargers are slightly more vulnerable compared to Chargers and Charger Behemoths, as their spore flesh can be damaged by any weapon, and it has less armor compared to the regular Chargers and Charger Behemoths. However, damaging it will only transfer 20% of the damage dealt to its main health.
Spore Chargers can be dispatched with the same
Since Spore Chargers will often explode on death, it is advised to stand as far as possible from them to avoid death or critical damage.
Spore Chargers will not explode if they bleed out.
A well-placed
can kill a Spore Charger relatively quickly; however, they can sometimes survive Thermite Grenades if they are thrown at certain parts of the legs and body.
It's easy to tell when a Spore Charger is nearby due to the green spores it emits, but hard to pinpoint its exact location from a distance.
The ping system can be used to mark it through the fog, facilitating the tracking of its position.
Stratagems like the
and
will automatically target the Spore Charger, as long as nothing larger is nearby.
The Spore Charger was first revealed in the Escalation of Freedom Announcement Trailer on July 23rd, 2024, and began appearing in-game on the update's release on August 6th, 2024.

attacchi.descrizione: Hyper-specialised in stalking and viciously dispatching prey. The Stalker's unique, mantis-like talons are capable of striking with blistering speed, sometimes even bifurcating human targets.
Functioning akin to a spring-loaded harpoon. The barbed tongues of the Stalker impact with such force and speed that they knock human quarry to the ground, leaving them easy prey to their talons.

s: Stalkers spawn only from Stalker Lairs, an optional objective that begins appearing on Difficulty 4 (Challenging). Stalker Lairs will contain Bug Holes, up to two, and will periodically spawn Stalkers until they are destroyed. Certain Stalker Lairs will also include a normal Bug Hole that spawns
s and
s.

Stalkers will begin pursuing while camouflaged once a Helldiver is roughly 150m away from a Stalker Lair; actively pursuing Stalkers will make a distinct chittering noise. From their Lairs, they will move directly towards Helldivers, and attempt to flank Helldivers and attack from the rear when possible.

Stalkers will reveal themselves once they are roughly 20m away from a Helldiver or take enough damage. If they are attacked as they reveal themselves, they will retaliate with their tongue attack before switching to their claws at close range; their tongues are able to knock Helldivers away from them. After taking at least 50% of their Health (~400HP), they will jump while retreating and camouflage, regenerating health (about 50/s) while camouflaged. After a brief amount of time, they will restart their pursuit.
Stalkers are among the most dangerous Terminids and should be a priority target once spotted. Their tongue attack can knock Helldivers over, and their claws swipes are quick with high damage.
Despite lacking armor, Stalkers are significantly more durable than
s and other medium-sized Terminids, and have health comparable to a
. Precision is of the utmost importance as their heads have very little health.
Stalkers that are on fire, gassed, or have Terminid Blood/Bile on them will be partially visible when camouflaged.
Stalkers take 25% more fire damage, making incendiary weapons such as the
or
effective against them, and can counteract their health regeneration.
Weapons that can stagger, such as the
or
can prevent Stalkers from attacking.
Weaponry that can stun, such as the
or
, are even more effective and can leave Stalkers vulnerable to Support Weapons.

It is presumed that Stalkers are genetically modified Hunters, sharing their tongue attack and appearing similarly to them, only larger. Despite not using their wings in combat like Hunters, Stalkers will use them at the beginning of their retreats.

attacchi.descrizione: Acting on a scale far above Bile Spewers, the Bile Titan is capable of regurgitating many gallons of caustic byproducts upon the foe that melt through nearly any material in a matter of seconds and reduce its unfortunate victims to steaming piles of goo.
attacchi.effetti: Acid / (Impact + Blast Damage) / (1.5x Damage to Exosuits) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion) / 3/s Acid DPS (4.0s) / (Via Impact/Blast Damage)

attacchi.descrizione: Should dousing foes in gallons of caustic fluids somehow fail, the Bile Titan is also simply capable of crushing whatever is left with its multi-ton "pikes", impaling and skewering exos, cars and even tanks and outright obliterating anything smaller.

s: Bile Titans can be first found on Difficulty 4 (Challenging) as the Mission Target of the Eliminate Bile Titans mission.
Starting on Difficulty 6 (Extreme), Bile Titans can spawn from Bug Breaches and can be found patrolling the map on its own.

Starting on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission), Bile Titans can be found guarding certain heavy Bug Nests layouts, and Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive)'s Mega Nests; these Nests can also contain a Bug Hole that Bile Titans can spawn from.
On planets invaded by the Spore Burst Strain, Bile Titans are replaced completely by
starting at Difficulty 5 (Hard).
Bile Titans cannot spawn on missions containing
es; in situations where a Bile Titan would normally spawn, a
is spawned instead.

When encountered outside of a Bug Breach, Bile Titans will usually remain still or follow a fixed patrol path. Upon noticing Helldivers, they will turn to face them. Bile Titans will signify when they will begin attacking Helldivers by roaring and slamming their front legs into the ground — the background music will also change. When spawning from a Bug Breach or Bile Titan Bug Hole, they will immediately be aggressive and seek any nearby Helldivers.

A Bile Titan spews its bile when it is 25-30m away from Helldivers, with a 10 second cooldown between bile attacks. Helldivers that are directly in front of a Bile Titan can be attacked by a right leg slam. If Helldivers are under a Bile Titan, it will attack using both of its front legs, rapidly stomping the area in front of it. The legs of the Bile Titan can also damage and kill Helldivers while the Bile Titan is moving. Near-miss leg attacks can cause Helldivers to be knocked down.

With AV 4 armor and massive damage, Bile Titans are one of the most dangerous Terminids that Helldivers will face, requiring teamwork and/or strong Stratagems. Helldivers are advised to maintain a safe distance and engage Bile Titans with offensive stratagems.
Offensive Stratagems such as the
, and
are all capable of killing Bile Titans with one use, but this can vary due to positioning.
Support Weapons such as the
can kill a Bile Titan anywhere, while other explosive Anti-tank weapons such as the
and
can kill with a single shot to the head.

If available, a Hellpod can deal significant damage to a Bile Titan. The Power Steering module can greatly increase the chances of landing on the Titan, as it can be difficult to land directly on the body or head.

The bile-spewing attack will deal extreme damage to any Terminids in its path; including other Bile Titans. This can be exploited to eliminate other Terminids, as anything smaller than a charger will almost instantly die from a direct hit of its Bile attack.
Destroying a Bile Titan's sacs will prevent it from using spew attacks, instead engaging Helldivers only with its legs.
Bile Titans are IMMUNE to any stun & confusion effects. However, Gas DoT still affects them.

A Bile Titan's death ragdoll can potentially crush Helldivers underneath it, and its legs may swing around widely, killing Helldivers that come into contact with it, as well as other Terminids including
s and
s.
Ironically, Bile Titan bodies have sufficient demolition force to destroy Bile Titan Bug Holes.

Bile Titans and Impalers have their own music theme when they notice and engage a Helldiver. It overrides the standard Terminid combat music until all engaged Bile Titans or Impalers are killed. This is useful for determining if a Titan is aware of the presence of a Helldiver or not.
Bile Titans may be inspired by the Hierophant Bio-Titan employed by the Tyranids in Warhammer 40,000.

attacchi.descrizione: Somehow evolving to spray flammable venom instead of caustic filth. The Dragon Roach's firey breath is capable of spreading far and wide as it hovers, saturating the ground in chemical flame and immolating anything within it.

s: Dragonroaches can only spawn in solitary patrols that can be spotted from long range. They do not have fixed spawns at Objective locations or POIs, nor can they be spawned through Bug Breaches.
Bile Titan and Dragonroach spawns are mutually exclusive (except on the Spore Burst Strain, where Dragonroaches spawn alongside
); in situations where a Bile Titan would normally spawn, such as Bile Titan Bug Holes, distant patrols, and Bug Breaches, a
is spawned instead. Notably, this makes it possible to encounter normal Chargers on Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive) missions, where their spawns are otherwise replaced entirely by
s and
s.

On Evacuate High-Value Assets missions on planets where Dragonroaches are active, they can spawn before the pre-mission timer finishes counting down; therefore it is advised to prepare for its attacks immediately.

The Dragonroach eerily soars across the skies of the Hive World when not alerted. Upon spotting a Helldiver or being shot at, the Dragonroach will begin to perform a strafing run towards its target and will spew its fire breath over a large linear area. After which it will hover low in midair behind its target for a moment, before performing another concentrated fire breath attack and returning to higher altitudes. Once engaged in combat with a Helldiver, the Dragonroach will circle its target at high altitude between attacks.
Like Bile Titans, Dragonroaches have a heavily armored carapace, and their main weak spot is their head.
Dragonroach Specific
While in the open, Helldivers should be vigilant in scanning the sky to avoid an ambush by a Dragonroach's strafing run. Pinging its position for your team can help prevent unnecessary deaths.
Trying to attack the Dragonroach during its diving breath attack will likely result in death if the creature is targeting you.
The Dragonroach's fire-breathing attack will ignite the player so a Helldiver should go prone if they are hit or are likely to be hit.
The Dragonroach exclusively uses fire damage for all it's attacks. Because of this, using armor with
, or
passives can greatly reduce their lethality.
Helldivers may find a use for the
as it is capable of completely blocking the fire spewed. This is helpful for defending teammates as they line up a headshot with anti-tank weapons.
The Dragonroach will always repeat the following attack sequence:
It spots valid targets such as Helldivers and Sentries, making an audible screech.
Proceeding to glide and circle the selected target for a moment. Before the dive, it will make an audible flap noise.
It then proceeds to dive and unleashes a strafing breath attack.
After diving to avoid this attack, there is ample opportunity to charge up weapons like the
and
to line up a shot.
Hovers for its final tracking breath attack.
This stationary state is the easiest moment to hit the Dragonroach. While highly risking death.
It is possible to take minimal chip damage by waiting until the last moment to dive out the way and staying prone.
As the breath particles will be focused on your last position, and the fire puddles are not able to set you aflame while prone.
Unlike its grounded cousin, the
, Dragonroaches are quite susceptible to being staggered if hit. Sustained fire from any high-stagger explosive weapons, such as suppressive fire from
autocannons, can prevent a Dragonroach from attacking or fleeing, effectively stunlocking it in midair.
When hit with sufficient stagger force while breathing fire, the fire breath will continue as the Dragonroach flails in mid-air and can hit divers who were not originally in the line of fire.
It is worth noting the hitbox of the Dragonroach's fire attack extends beyond its visual appearance. Helldivers even outside of the apparent strafe path of the Dragonroach should take evasive action.
General
The Dragonroach has high health, high mobility, and a wide-area flame attack. As such, it should be the highest priority target when on the battlefield.

The Dragonroach boasts an abundance of AV 4 armor as well as near-universal 50% Explosive Damage Resistance. It therefore requires specific tactics to kill efficiently. Here are several recommended methods:
1. Shoot the head with anti-tank weapons for a guaranteed one or two-shot kill.
The head has AV 4 armor and only 1.5k HP, identical to that of the Bile Titan.
Dedicated AT weapons such as the
will one-shot if hitting the head.

A Hive Lord may spawn during any Mission rated Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission) or higher regardless of any ongoing objectives or enemy reinforcements, should a planet feature them. The Democracy Officer will announce its presence after it emerges, should a player face it for the first time.

Although the conditions for a Hive Lord emerging from the ground are unknown, it seems they are most likely to respond to Bug Breaches when they occur. When one happens, it is most probable that the Hive Lord will show up soon after. Multiple explosions in one place can also summon the Hive Lord, such as orbital barrages. If the Hive Lord "retreats" and stops attacking or appearing, it will retain the damage it has taken if it returns to the surface.
There is only one Hive Lord per mission. Once it has been slain, another will not replace it.

By default, Hive Lords will stay underground, appearing as a massive wave of trembling earth that kicks up clouds of dust and slowly approaches Helldivers. Hive Lords will often follow a specific Helldiver until they are within range of an attack. When approximately 100 meters from a target, it will emerge from the ground before performing an attack. Hive Lords can attack multiple times before re-burrowing.
If it takes enough damage, the Hive Lord will attempt to retreat, sinking back into the ground. It randomly opts to forgo attacks to roar instead.
Attacks

Surface: The Hive Lord's emergence inflicts a slowing effect within its vicinity due to the tremors it creates, launches any entities if they are too close, and boulders into the air that deal damage upon impact. Helldivers standing too close to the emerging Hive Lord are likely to be launched high up into the air.
Burrow: Partially emerging, the Hive Lord will continue burrowing forwards instead of fully surfacing upright, This move can still injure and knock away Helldivers if they are caught in the motion.

Body Slam: The Hive Lord will throw itself forwards, attempting to crush its target under its body. It will remain in a lying position for a moment afterwards before burrowing back into the ground. This attack can destroy or clip through terrain.

A variation of this attack can be performed by the Hive Lord by immediately slamming down upon emerging, and momentarily afterward burrowing back. When it slams it lands on it's back, allowing for a brief moment of exposure to fire.

Bile Rain: The Hive Lord will lean forwards, before shaking, shuddering, and releasing an enormous quantity of bile in three sweeps. The area of effect this attack creates covers a wide area and slows Helldivers, but there are gaps between each sweep that allows a careful Helldiver to survive.

There is a variation of this attack where the Hive Lord will do one large stream of bile straight in a line, a bit easier to avoid but higher potential for large damage on uncareful Helldivers, mechs or emplacements. It has a longer range than its counterpart.
Upon taking lethal damage, the Hive Lord will surface if previously burrowed, spew large amounts of Terminid blood before collapsing to the ground in spectacular fashion.
After successfully killing a Hive Lord, Helldivers are rewarded with a completed objective and 222 experience.
The Hive Lord has the largest Main health pool in the game by a significant margin, at 150,000. But all body parts are 0% durable so it takes full standard damage from all sources.
Due to its extremely large health pool and wide sweeping lethal attacks, it is advised that the entire squad either avoids the Hive Lord entirely, or coordinate to take it down.
The Hive Lord's body is completely encased in AV 5 armor, with the exception being AV 6 armor on the head and it's AV 2 armored open mouth.
Its body armor can be broken with sustained anti-tank fire, revealing the AV 2-armored flesh beneath. When a plate of armor is close to being destroyed, it will visibly show cracks and breaks.
The inner flesh is completely immune to explosion damage, so explosive weapons like the
should be avoided.
Most of the toughness of the Hive Lord's plate armor comes from its massive, non-decaying bleedout pool. It behaves as extra health, for a total of 50,000 effective health per section.
Helldivers who wish to take down a Hive Lord should consider bringing as much AP 5 firepower as possible in the form of Stratagems and Support Weapons.
and
are both highly effective against the Hive Lord, as they can damage multiple spinal armor plates due to the Hive Lord's massive size.
The
, and
allow for focusing on breaking armor plates between orbital and Eagle cooldowns.
The

is one of the most effective tools against a Hive Lord. Its missile arm can help strip an armor plate with rockets, dealing up to a total of 17,500 damage to an armor plate, allowing it's Gatling arm to quickly inflict massive damage upon the stripped section. With a full magazine, the chaingun can deal up to 121,500 damage in this manner.
However, due to their limited mobility and large frame, Exosuits are vulnerable to the Hive Lord's large attacks.

The Bastion is likewise effective against a Hive Lord due to its high HP pool allowing it to withstand multiple bile attacks and its large cannon and HMG ammo reserves being capable of destroying a plate and dealing enough damage to take out the Hive Lord with ease. However, the driver must maneuver the tank away from burrowing Hive Lords to prevent the Hive Lord from flipping the tank.
The

can potentially be even more effective than the Bastion and Patriot Exosuit, although its method would be more akin to the Patriot due to its missiles and dual gatling guns. The missiles can potentially deal 30,000 damage to a plate (accounting for explosive damage resistance) and the high DPS of the gatling guns can rapidly deal large amounts of damage to the exposed flesh of the Hive Lord.
The

can inflict an extreme amount of damage if Helldivers can position it correctly. The best time to use it is typically when the Hive Lord attempts to spew bile, as this attack does not hit at point-blank range and keeps it in place long enough for the Hellbomb's countdown to finish.
Once the armor is broken, high DPS weapons can be used to shred its main health pool by firing into the exposed AV 2 armored flesh. Weapons such as the

When engaging or withdrawing from the Hive Lord, Helldivers should maintain distance from one another. The size of the Hive Lord's attacks makes it dangerous for them to remain close to each other, as one strike could potentially kill all of them.
Most of the damage dealt by the bile of a Hive Lord is explosive, so bringing armor with the Fortified passive can help save Helldivers from these attacks or even make their damage negligible.

Currently, the Hive Lord is the only enemy which always grants Experience when killed. 222 experience is rewarded for its death, and it will show up as a completed Optional Objective when the mission ends.
The Hive Lord has its own section of the Hive World theme that plays when it is engaged in combat, overriding all other sections of the theme until it retreats or dies.
Despite being classified as "massive" in the game's enemy data, the Hive Lord is referred to as a Titan-class Terminid in-universe, which also refers to to other heavy Terminid enemies like the

Although the Hive Lord was a Boss Enemy in Helldivers 1, this was changed in Helldivers 2, where it was changed into a "force of nature" and would roam the map(s) rather than be a required enemy to kill during a mission.
According to the Helldivers 1 Encyclopedia entry for the Hive Lord, they are capable of perforating the entire crust of a planet if left unaccounted for.
While unlikely to happen, the rocks produced when the Hive Lord surfaces can land on and hurt Helldivers.

attacchi.descrizione: The Spore Burst Bile Titan is also capable of crushing whatever is before it with its multi-ton "pikes", impaling and skewering exos, cars and even tanks and outright obliterating anything smaller.

attacchi.effetti: Acid / (1.5x Damage to Exosuits) / (3.0x Damage To Bastion) / 3/s Acid DPS (4.0s) / (Via Blast Damage)

s: Spore Burst Bile Titans can be first found on Difficulty 5 (Hard), replacing Bile Titans on planets invaded by the Spore Burst Strain as the Mission Target of the Eliminate Bile Titans mission.
Starting on Difficulty 6 (Extreme), Spore Burst Bile Titans can spawn from Bug Breaches and can be found patrolling the map on their own.

Starting on Difficulty 7 (Suicide Mission), Spore Burst Bile Titans can be found guarding certain heavy Bug Nests layouts, and Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive)'s Mega Nests; these Nests can also contain a Bug Hole that Spore Burst Bile Titans can spawn from.
Spore Burst Bile Titans behave identically to natural Bile Titans with the exception of its attacking, trading off its corrosive bile spew with a powerful spewing of Spores.
Said Spore Spew will cause Helldivers not wearing armor with the
passive to be ragdolled on hit, as well as leaving a vision-blocking cloud of spores on impact that increase the speed of other nearby Spore Burst Terminids.
Spore Burst Strain Specific
The Spore Burst Bile Titan’s bile-spewing attack leaves spores on the ground that disrupt vision and buff other nearby Spore Burst Terminids.

When entering a cloud of spores (created by another Spore Burst Terminid’s death or through the Spore Burst Bile Titan’s bile spew), Spore Burst Terminids will gain a significant increase in speed, allowing them to close the gap on Helldivers.

The Spore Burst Bile Titan deals far less damage than the regular Bile Titan in its spew attack, posing little direct threat in terms of damage. Although Helldivers ragdolled by it will likely be vulnerable to attacks from other Terminids, the Bastion and other vehicles benefit greatly from this reduced damage.
Additionally, its bile-spewing attack has a much higher stagger force, capable of easily ragdolling Helldivers. This can be prevented by wearing armor with the
passive.

Spore Burst Bile Titans are slightly more durable than their standard counterpart, with 500 more Main health (7,000 vs 6,500), 1,000 more head health (2,500 vs 1,500) and 250 more bile sac health (750 vs 1,000).
This means that the
and
will not kill the Spore Burst Bile Titan in a single shot. The best alternative Anti-Tank weapons to use would be the
. or the
Destroying a Spore Burst Bile Titan's sacs is especially important compared to its standard variant, as this prevents it from buffing other nearby Spore Burst Terminids and ragdolling the Helldiver.
General

With AV 4 armor and massive damage, Spore Burst Bile Titans are one of the most dangerous Terminids that Helldivers will face, requiring teamwork and/or strong Stratagems. Helldivers are advised to maintain a safe distance and engage Spore Burst Bile Titans with offensive stratagems.
Offensive Stratagems such as the
, and
are all capable of killing Spore Burst Bile Titans with one use, but this can vary due to positioning.

If available, a Hellpod can deal significant damage to a Spore Burst Bile Titan. The Power Steering module can greatly increase the chances of landing on the Titan, as it can be difficult to land directly on the body or head.
Destroying a Spore Burst Bile Titan's sacs will prevent it from using spew attacks, instead engaging Helldivers only with its legs.
Spore Burst Bile Titans are IMMUNE to any stun & confusion effects. However, Gas DoT still affects them.

A Spore Burst Bile Titan's death ragdoll can potentially crush Helldivers underneath it, and its legs may swing around widely, killing Helldivers that come into contact with it, as well as other Terminids including
s and
s.
Ironically, Spore Burst Bile Titan bodies have sufficient demolition force to destroy Bile Titan Bug Holes.
Despite being different from the Bile Titan, when pinged, the Spore Burst Bile Titan will still be called "Bile Titan".

The Damage page explains how different Enemies, Weapons, and Stratagems handle damage.

Calculating Damage in Helldivers 2 takes a large number of variables into consideration. All damage calculation information in this section of the document has been confirmed to be accurate as of Game Version 1.001.001
Enemy Parts

An enemy's hitbox is not as simple as a single value of health and universal armor value. An enemy is made up of many different enemy parts, each part with its own armor value, health, durability, and a Main health pool. Parts can also be considered "Durable" parts, which take damage in a completely different way.
Enemy parts can be destroyed, but that does not always mean the enemy dies. An enemy will die if one of the following conditions are satisfied:
Enemy Main health is reduced to 0.
A fatal enemy part is destroyed.
Percent (%) to Main

Enemy parts that take damage generally have a percentage of the damage dealt to them also be applied to their Main Health. Most enemy parts will cap the damage to main at their full HP value, however some parts allow excess damage to overflow into Main.
Regular Example: A
Main Health is 750, with its arms having 260 Health and 50% damage to main. An
deals 90 damage to the arms leaving them at 170 Health. 45 damage is also dealt to the Main Health leaving it at 705.
Uncapped Damage Example: A
Main Health is 125, with its arms having 65 Health and 50% damage to main. A single shot from an
will deal its full 300 damage to the arms, dealing 150 damage to the Trooper's Main Health which will kill it.
Health Constitution (Bleed)

Constitution is a second health pool that begins decaying once the main health is depleted. The enemy is now in the "downed" state and will limp until they bleedout and die. Bleedout is a second health pool for limbs that determines how long they live for once they are destroyed, at which point, its Constitution will begin to decay, or "bleed out," at a set rate. For some limbs, the decay rate may be 0, meaning they will not decay over time and bleedout must be depleted with further damage to fully destroy the limb.
Constitution Example:

have 750 constitution with a decay rate of 100hp/s. Destroying the butt or depleting main health will trigger the "downed" state and the Charger will bleed out until it depletes its constitution and dies. Bleedout is usually fatal.
Bleedout without Decay Example:
have 1,500 leg health and 2,000 constitution but 0 decay therefore the constitution effectively behaves as extra health so the legs have 3,500 effective health.
Explosion Damage
Explosive damage deals 100% durable damage and due to the ability to hit multiple limbs, This allows explosives to deal multiplied damage to Main health.
Explosion damage transferred to Main via explosion vulnerable parts "ignore" Main AV and its ExDR.
For example: An HE shell explosion from the
which is AP 4 armor penetration fired at an
vent will ignore the Main AV when transferring damage to Main which is AV 5 armor.

Explosions damage Main via a mechanic called Affected By Explosion. This allows Explosion damage to damage Main via a 100% ExDR Part because instead of the limb taking the damage, it will be redirected to Main. Note: This can only occur once, regardless of parts hit and explosion armor penetration must match or exceed Main armor to deal damage.
For example: An
exploding underneath a
and dealing damage to all four of its legs, bile sacs, underside, torso armor and head.
Explosive Damage Resistance (ExDR)
Enemy limbs commonly have explosion resistance and/or immunity to protect against explosions dealing multiple instances of damage by hitting multiple parts.
A limb with an ExDR value of 100% means it is Explosion immune and that part itself does not take explosion damage. Main takes the explosion damage instead.
An ExDR value of a percent lower than 100% means that the target can negate a percent of explosion damage done to that part to reduce their effectiveness (e.g. Tank hulls have an ExDR value of 35%).
Explosions have 3 different radii from the center of impact where the following rules apply:
Inner Radius: 100% damage, 100% stagger, Full AP, 100% demolition force.
Outer Radius: 99-0% damage 100% stagger, -1 AP (minimum 2 AP), 99-0% demolition force.
Explosions have linear damage, stagger & demolition force fall-off.
Shockwave (Stagger): 0% damage, 99-0% stagger, Full AP, 0% demolition force.
Helldivers will only experience stagger if they are hit by the inner or outer radius.
Going prone reduces explosion damage by 90% only in the outer radius as well as being in ragdoll state.
Inner radius will bypass obstacles and obstructions, while outer radius will only let shockwave and stagger effects through obstacles.
Explosion Verification Mode (ExVM)

Explosions use raycasts; ExVM dictates whether these raycasts require Line of Sight (LoS) or not. ExVM is part-dependent on enemies. Note: Multiple limbs with ExVM: Outer Radius or None can have explosions "clip" through hitboxes as the raycast can ignore the LoS requirement.
All: Inner & Outer Radius require LoS.
Outer Radius: Inner Radius ignores LoS, Outer Radius requires LoS.
None: Inner & Outer Radius both ignore LoS.
Armor Penetration & Armor Values

Every part of every Enemy has a specific Armor Value, with a range of 0 to 10. This number indicates how armored that part is, and how much armor penetration or AP a Weapon needs to be to deal damage to it.
Armor Penetration is abbreviated as AP0-10.
Armor Values are abbreviated as AV0-10.

s: Similar to enemies, every weapon has a set of Armor Penetration Values that indicate how much armor the weapon can pierce.
If the Armor Penetration Value is greater than the enemy part's Armor Value, the weapon deals 100% damage (Red Hitmarker)
If the Armor Penetration Value is equal to the enemy part's Armor Value, the weapon deals 65% damage (White Hitmarker)
If the Armor Penetration Value is less than the enemy part's Armor Value, the weapon deals NO damage (Ricochet)
Each weapon has a total of four penetration values:
One penetration value for a direct hit, looking straight at the enemy part with (almost) no angle of attack: less than 25°.
One penetration value for hits at a slight angle: 26 to 60°
One penetration value for hits at a large angle: 61 to 80°
One penetration value for hits at an extreme value: 81 to 90°
The first three penetration values are often identical, resulting in a general penetration value and a bouncing angle.
For explosions, only one armor penetration value is used. It decreases by 1 in the outer radius.
Breakable Armor Plating
Some enemies have protective armor plating shielding vulnerable and fatal parts underneath it. The enemies that have this are
and

Breakable armor plating has a separate health pool from the parts underneath it that DOES NOT transfer excess damage to the parts underneath. The armor plating must be destroyed in order to deal damage to the vulnerable and usually fatal part underneath.
For example: Destroying a Charger's Leg Armor with a rocket from the
and finishing off the exposed vulnerable flesh off with a primary weapon such as the
Overpenetration (Cleave)

Overpenetration is when a projectile pierces multiple parts or enemies. Overpenetration occurs when the armor penetration of the projectile exceeds the armor value of the struck part by 2 or more. With each hitbox cleaved, the projectile has its armor penetration reduced by 1.
Some enemies sport breakable armor, overpenetration of which requires a projectile with at least three times the armor penetration as the armor value of the struck part.
Example 1: The
cleaving through a horde of
as it has AP 2 armor penetration vs AV 0 armor.
Example 2: The
can cleave through the butt of a Charger and hit its inner flesh as its armor penetration is three times greater than the butt, but with 1 additional AP as it loses 1 AP after cleaving the butt.
Penetration Slowdown
Penetration slowdown is the percentage of velocity lost when a projectile cleaves through an enemy's damage zone.

Example: A projectile has a velocity of 500m/s with no velocity loss and 25% Penetration Slowdown. That means 25% of velocity is lost, so the projectile will exit the target at a rate of speed of 375m/s.
Weapon Damage
Each weapon, stratagem, etc. has two different damage values assigned to them
Standard damage is the normal damage the weapon does to anything it shoots.
Durable damage, is the damage done to durable enemy parts and large volume bodies, both of which have a durability greater than zero.
Ballistics
Caliber: Drastically increases damage fall-off.
Speed: The bullet's initial magnitude to its velocity, higher speed increases damage fall-off slightly.
Mass: Reduces damage falloff.
Drag: Increases damage falloff.
Gravity Multiplier: How much the bullet drops in travel.
Damage Fall-Off

Many damage sources can suffer from reduction independently of their target. Damage fall-off is affected by Caliber, Speed, Mass, and Drag. There are two types; velocity-based fall-off (ballistics) and range-based fall-off (explosions).
If a projectile is slower than its muzzle velocity, damage is lost.
If a projectile is faster than its muzzle velocity, damage is gained.
This can be achieved via diving, jumping with the
or traveling at high speeds in the M-102 Fast Reconnaissance Vehicle.
Projectiles lose velocity due to drag factor. Damage increase can occur when firing at a target at a lower elevation using, for instance,
which has 0% Drag but is affected by gravity. Reduction in speed and gravity is otherwise typical for most weapons no matter the elevation.

An exception to this rule are weapons with guided projectiles. Guided projectiles lose speed but are programmed to accelerate to match their initial velocity, simultaneously resulting in no damage lost. These weapons are the
, and
Weapons with 0% drag do not suffer damage fall-off.
The explosion from projectiles is not affected by this system, only the projectile.
One important thing to note, these damage values are the damage done at point-blank range. Damage decreases as the distance traveled increases.
Enemy Durability & Durable Damage
Enemy parts may also have Durability. This is a variable between 0 and 100%.
A value of 0% means the enemy part is not durable at all, and will take full standard damage
A value of 100% means the enemy part is 100% durable and will take full durable damage.
The ratio of durability & standard damage always adds up to 100%
For example: An enemy part is 30% durable, therefore 70% standard damage is also taken into account.

Each weapon has a specific value defined for the amount of damage it can do to standard enemy parts, and a separate value defined for the amount of "durable" damage it can do to enemy parts. The part's durability value defines the ratio of standard damage vs. durable damage applied.
Examples of Damage to a Durable Part
Formula to calculate damage vs durable targets:
Standard Damage × (1 - Durable %) + (Durable Damage × Durable %) = Damage Dealt
Note: Round DOWN to the nearest whole number for the damage dealt.
For this example, we'll be using the
which has a standard damage of 95 and durable damage of 23 firing at a 30% durable target with an armor value of AV 2 with no damage fall-off.
Example: 95 × (1-30%) + (23 × 30%) = 73.4 → 73 damage dealt to the target.

For this example, it will be assumed that the weapon used has 1,000 standard damage and 500 durable damage with no damage fall-off. Assume a single shot is being fired at a specific Enemy Part, and that the shot pierces the armor of the enemy completely (AP > AV).
If the enemy part has a durability value of 0 (0% durable), the part will take 1,000 damage.
100% of standard damage = 1000
0% of durable damage = 0
If the enemy part has a durability value of 100 (100% durable), the part will take 500 damage.
0% of standard damage = 0
100% of durable damage = 500
If the enemy part has a durability value of 50 (50% durable), the part will take 750 damage.
50% of standard damage = 500
50% of durable damage = 250
If the enemy part shot by this weapon has a durability value of 75 (75% durable), the part will take 625 damage.
25% of standard damage = 250
75% of durable damage = 375
Squishy Enemy Parts
Squishy parts have an Armor Value of 0 (AV 0) but have extremely high Durability, high health and normally 0% ExDR (e.g.
butts).
Example: Charger butts are AV 0, 950 hp and 80% durable.
This means that all weapons can damage the part, but the damage done is almost entirely related to the guns durable damage, not its standard damage.
Weapons, Stratagems, etc. with explosion damage such as the
are most effective against squishy enemy parts because explosives deal 100% durable damage.
Demolition Force & Structures
See also:

All destructible structures in the game have a Demolition Threshold value between 0 and 60. In order to destroy most structures, the user needs to be using a weapon/stratagem that has enough Demolition Force. Depending on the structure, the weapon/stratagem may need to be explosive as well if it has BaDR (Ballistic demolition resistance) set to Yes. Currently only spawners such as Bug Holes, Automaton Fabricators, and Grounded Warp Ships have BaDR set as Yes. Armor penetration is irrelevant to this check, as is damage. If the threshold is met, the structure is destroyed.
Other Structures
These structures are not exclusively dependent on Demolition force.

Weapons that have status effects are not so simple that a single pellet can hit an enemy and proc the status effect; they have status strength or "buildup" where once the threshold is met the status effect will have a chance to trigger on the enemy, with the effect guaranteed to trigger at the maximum threshold. Status Strength also has decay so ensure to continuously apply the "buildup" to trigger the effect.
For Example: The
has 0.6 status strength per pellet and a

has a minimum trigger threshold of 2.1 & 3.3 maximum for fire DoT. This means that at least 4 pellets need to hit the Warrior to have a chance to trigger the burning DoT, with the chance to trigger guaranteed with 6 pellets (since maximum threshold is reached)
Damage over Time

Damage over time, commonly known as its abbreviation, DoT is a status effect that deals damage ONLY to Main health. The status effect must be able to penetrate the Armor Value or AV of the enemy in order to deal damage. DoT is also subject to the damage reduction from armor penetration being identical to the armor value.
For Example: Fire DoT which is AP 4 armor penetration deals 35% less damage to a Charger's main health which is AV 4 armor.
Fire does 100 dmg/s × 1.5 = 150 dmg/s × 0.65 = 97.5 → 97 dmg/s.
Sources of DoT are Fire, Burning Heavy,
Burn, Thermite, Gas, Acid, Thorn Bushes and Barbed Wire and Bleeding (Helldiver only)
Elemental Multipliers

Elemental damage and Status Effects operate via damage multipliers, the most common being Fire, though there are few enemies with Arc and Gas status effect damage multipliers that are also affected. Such as

s receiving a 1.8x Arc damage multiplier or Helldivers with a 1.3x Gas damage multiplier. These multipliers operate are based on enemy size; the larger the enemy the higher the multiplier and vice versa, with smaller enemies having a smaller multiplier.

There are various status effects that can alter the Helldiver or their Enemies. The following effects exist in Helldivers 2.

Staggering can range from mere flinching to being knocked off your feet entirely. It is caused by dealing or taking damage with sufficient Stagger Force to meet an enemy's stagger thresholds. Higher thresholds impart stronger effects, such as completely interrupting animations. Unlike other status effects, Stagger Force does not build up over multiple attacks.
Enemies
Staggering will cause an enemy to be pushed back and usually interrupts their movement, with the distance pushed scaling with Stagger Force.
Most enemies have abilities that can be interrupted upon being attacked with sufficient Stagger Force.
Some notable interruptable abilities include certain attacks and calling for reinforcements.
Stagger thresholds listed on enemy pages will be the value required to cause interrupting stagger.

Armor can be equipped at the Armory or in a Hellpod on the Bridge before Missions in Helldivers 2.
Most armor sets can be acquired by unlocking them through Warbonds with Medals or buying them from the Superstore using Super Credits.
Armor
Body armors come with designated armor passive abilities and specific stats; they are categorized into light, medium, and heavy types. There are a total of light, medium, and heavy armors.
Helmet

Designated as standard issue, helmets provide no additional bonuses; they have no practical effect despite being rated at 100 for armor, speed, and stamina. However, if the worn body's armor rating exceeds 100, the wearer takes reduced headshot
as well.
Cape
Capes, like helmets, are effectively cosmetic. However, since they display stats in-game, they are categorized as armor.

Armors have three primary stats: • Armor Rating : Represents the armor's ability to absorb damage. • Speed : Determines how quickly the Helldiver can move across the battlefield. • Stamina Regen: Affects the regeneration of stamina, which is used when sprinting and performing other strenuous actions.

Armor rating (AR) increases or reduces damage taken using the following formulas: • If Armor Rating ≤ 150 ◦ Damage taken = Attack Damage × (1.5 - (Armor Rating ÷ 200)) • If Armor Rating > 150 ◦ Damage taken = Attack Damage × (1.05 - (Armor Rating ÷ 500))
Speed is calculated based on the raw Armor Rating stat (before factoring in passives like

) using the following formula: • Speed = 600 − Armor Rating Based on the formula Light armor (50 AR) is 10% faster than Meduim (100 AR) and 22% faster than Heavy (150 AR) and Heavy armor is 10% slower than Medium.
– Calculated after passive perk
is applied.
Stamina Regen (SR) is similarly calculated using these formulas: • If Armor Rating ≥ 100 ◦ Stamina Regen = 200 − Armor Rating • If Armor Rating < 100 ◦ Stamina Regen = 150 − Armor Rating ÷ 2

When selecting a Mission in Helldivers 2 using the Galactic War console, a difficulty can be selected between level 1 Difficulty 1 (Trivial) and level 10 Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive).
Each difficulty level offers a different set of missions. For example, some missions offered to the player on Difficulty 1 (Trivial) are not offered on Difficulty 6 (Extreme).
The number of Medals, Requisition, and Experience you earn from a mission all depends on the difficulty you select.
Higher difficulty missions have increasing percentage multipliers for Requisition Slips and Experience, from +25% on Difficulty 3 (Medium) to +300% on Difficulty 10 (Super Helldive)

The Eradication Main Objective base-reward depends on the selected difficulty. Each difficulty affects the rewards by 20 Experience and 100 Requisition. E.g. Difficulty 6 (Extreme) Eradication-mission rewards 120 Experience and 600 Requisition, and Difficulty 3 (Medium) rewards 60 Experience and 300 Requisition.
Enemy forces are enhanced to increasingly lethal degrees.
The number of enemies and the type of enemy both depend on the difficulty level set.
The frequency of enemy patrol being spawned increases alongside the difficulty.
In relation, the frequency of DSS Eagle Strike and other tactical actions during missions decreases with increased difficulty.
The number of Operation Modifiers present during the mission.
One modifier is added on Difficulty 5 (Hard).
A second modifier is added on Difficulty 8 (Impossible).
The number of Sub-Objectives required to complete a Main Objective increases at higher difficulties.
The number and size of enemy Outposts (Bug Nests/Automaton Outposts/Illuminate Encampments)
Outpost spawning can vary quite drastically depending on a number of other factors as well, including biome, mission type, and faction.
The number of Optional Objectives increases at higher difficulties.
Map size increases to accommodate the increased amount of Mission Objectives on the Expedition-mission. The size increase is lesser on the Metropolis biome maps.
As difficulty increases once maximum map-size has been achieved, the Mission Objectives occupy spaces which otherwise might have had Minor Places of Interest being places upon.
The number and type of Common Rare Super Samples able to be found depends on the set difficulty.
Common Commons appear on all difficulties, while Rare Rares first appear on Difficulty 4 (Challenging), and Super Supers on Difficulty 6 (Extreme) difficulty.
The type of samples available during an operation can be confirmed on the Galactic War console when selecting an operation.

s: Separate from Damage, the Demolition Force of an attack determines if said attack can destroy a structure.
All destructible structures in- game have a Demolition Threshold between 10 and 60.

In order to destroy a structure, the user needs to be using a weapon/stratagem that has enough Demolition Force. Explosions have demolition force fall-off in the outer radius. Armor penetration is irrelevant to this check, as is damage, and whether or not the attack is explosive. When the threshold is met, the structure will be destroyed.

The exceptions to this are enemy spawners; Bug Holes, Automaton Fabricators, Bulk Fabricators and Grounded Warp Ships, which require a minimum demo force of 20 and the explosive property to destroy via their open hole, vent and door; as they have Ballistic Demolition Resistance, or BaDR. Ballistic Demolition Resistance means that the structure(s) resists demo force from non-explosive projectiles such as bullets or electric arcs. For example, an
which has a demo force of 20, but is not explosive. Therefore, it will not destroy the structure.

Note: Certain structures such as Spore Spewers and Shrieker Nests, are not labeled as structures that require demo force to destroy. These entities are considered non-moving enemy units with low Armor Value, high HP, and Durability. The only exceptions to this are Automaton Fabricators, Bulk Fabricators and Grounded Warp Ships, which use both health, armor, and demolition force systems.
Demolition Force Sources

A variety of weapons and other gear used by Helldivers are capable of destroying structures. The following tables list all sources of at least 20 Demolition Force available to players, along with their Demolition Force values and whether they are considered explosive.
Demolition Force vs. Structures
Note: BaDR means Ballistic Demolition Resistance. Projectile weapons that meet demo threshold but are not explosive cannot destroy said structure with BaDR.
For example: LAS-98 Laser Cannon has demo force 20 but cannot destroy bug holes, fabricators or warp ships since it is not explosive.
